 involved and provides clear oversight, ensuring continuous improvement and accountability. Staff
 are confident, well trained and supported by effective policies and safeguarding procedures.

source_index.name: Whitchurch House
source_index.provider: ios recruitment and training services limited

source_index.name: White House Residential Home
source_index.summary:
The White House residential home provides care and support for thirty-seven people. It is located
 close to Wrexham city centre and there is a strong focus on Wrexham running throughout the
 home’s décor and activities.

 People benefit from high-quality, person-centred care and support provided by a dedicated and
 knowledgeable staff team who know them really well. Relative’s comments include “The care home
 truly puts the residents first”. People and relatives told us the White house is friendly, welcoming
 and homely. They said, “It is brilliant”, “Quite content” and “Very happy and would not want to be
 anywhere else”. People are involved in making choices and decisions about their lives with many
 opportunities to participate in creative and meaningful activities and events both at home and in the
 community.

 Staff are dedicated, work well as a team and feel very supported. They receive training and have
opportunities to develop further in their roles. Staff commented on “Excellent staff. Dedicated to
their job” and “Staff are passionate about service users and their welfare”. People also commented
on lovely staff and complimented the manager on how well they had chosen staff members.

Systems and processes in place provide effective oversight of the service. The responsible
individual (RI) visits the home every three months and a six-month quality of care review is also
completed, identifying any areas for further improvement.

source_index.name: White Rose Care Home
source_index.summary:
People are very happy with the care and support they receive from skilled and
compassionate care staff. People rate their experience of living at White Rose as excellent.
Care staff are knowledgeable and caring, and told us how much they enjoy their job. The
provider highly values all the staff working at the service and is committed to supporting
them in their continued development. The opportunities available for people to take part in
meaningful activities, which boosts their health and well-being, are outstanding. People live
in an environment which is maintained to a very high standard and promotes their
independence and wellbeing. The Responsible Individual (RI) and manager are
enthusiastic and committed to providing people with the best quality of life and experience
of living in a care service as possible. There is excellent leadership and management at the
service, and the governance arrangements in place to support the provision of high-quality
care are robust.

source_index.name: Wilbury House Limited
source_index.summary:
Wilbury House is a residential care home which provides personal care and support to people. It is
 homely and welcoming situated in pleasant grounds in a quiet, rural area.

 People living at the service experience excellent well-being outcomes as they consistently have
 control over their lives and are treated with dignity and respect. We saw people relaxing in their
 environment and participating in meaningful activities. Family ties are encouraged and people’s
 well-being is promoted.

 Care and support is good. We saw person-centred care planning and the review of personal plans
 is completed frequently and with involvement of people and/or their representatives. People and
 their families expressed satisfaction with the quality of care provided.

 The environment is good and promotes people’s well-being outcomes by providing safe, clean and
 homely accommodation. The service provider currently has an ongoing programme of
 refurbishment and is continually making improvements to the environment.

 Leadership and management is good. There is a dedicated and knowledgeable management team
 in place who support staff through formal and informal supervision. The Responsible Individual (RI)
 visits the service routinely and ensures effective governance and oversight.

source_index.name: Williamston Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Williamston is a nursing home for adults. It is located in a rural area approximately eight miles from
 Milford Haven town. It is a large, detached manor house and provides residential and nursing care
 to people who are frail or living with dementia.

 People experience good wellbeing outcomes because of the relationships they have with those
 caring for them. More opportunities for people to engage in meaningful activities would enhance
 well-being.

 Care and support is good because a registered nurse is always available for support and advice.
 Improved record keeping would enhance standards of care and support.

 Some improvements have been made to the environment but the length of time the work is taking
 together with the appearance of the service means this remains an area for improvement. This will
be followed up at the next inspection.

Leadership & Management is good because the manager is very visible within the service and is
well regarded by the team. The Responsible Individual (RI) has good oversight of the service and is
responsive and receptive.

source_index.name: Willow Hall Residential Care Home limited
source_index.provider: WILLOW HALL RESIDENTIAL CARE HOME LIMITED
source_index.summary:
Willow Hall is located close to the centre of Caernarfon and is within reach of local amenities.

 People's wellbeing requires improvement. The condition of parts of the environment does not
 consistently provide a safe, comfortable and dignified setting, and this has the potential to impact
 on people's quality of life and overall wellbeing. Despite these concerns, people benefit from
 positive and caring relationships with staff who know them well and understand their individual
 needs and preferences. Staff are committed to supporting people in a respectful and
 compassionate manner, helping to promote their wellbeing and maintain their independence
 wherever possible.

 Care and support is good. People benefit from the input of a committed and dedicated staff team
 who know them well and understand their individual needs, preferences and routines. Medication is
 managed safely and effectively. Staff provide appropriate support that enables people to achieve
 and maintain their personal wellbeing outcomes as far as possible. Personal plans are
comprehensive, person-centred and provide clear guidance for staff on how to meet people's
assessed needs.

The environment requires significant improvement. The premises are not maintained to a suitable
standard and, in their current condition, do not consistently support the delivery of safe, dignified,
person-centred care. We identified concerns relating to repair, maintenance and the overall upkeep
of the home, which present potential risks to people's health, safety and wellbeing.

Leadership and management require significant improvement. The Responsible Individual (RI) has
not established sufficiently robust governance and organisational arrangements to ensure the
service is delivered with appropriate care, competence and skill, in accordance with the Statement
of Purpose. Systems and processes are not effective in providing adequate oversight of the
management, quality, safety and overall effectiveness of the service.

source_index.name: Willowbrook House Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Willowbrook House Nursing Home is in a suburb of Cardiff, with local amenities close by. People
 experience good well-being outcomes because the service provides consistency of care from a
 dedicated care team. People form strong bonds with care staff, who know them well. The residents’
 committee regularly meets with service leaders. People’s voices are informing and shaping service
 development.
 People experience a good standard of care and support and are complimentary of the service they
 receive. Most daily outcomes are met. The service is continuing to strengthen how they deliver care
 in-line with people’s preferences and needs, and ensuring daily records are an accurate account of
 the care delivered. People access healthcare professionals and medications are well managed.
 The environment is good, which supports people’s daily outcomes. It is clean, comfortable and
 decorated to a high standard. Access to well-kempt outdoors spaces, and ample communal areas
 supports well-being.
 Leadership and management is good. Since the last inspection the provider has enhanced the
 governance systems with mostly good effect. Organisational structure, responsibilities and
 accountability is clear. The responsible individual (RI) is accountable for the quality monitoring of
 the service. The RI and governance team are taking prompt and effective steps to strengthen their
 processes to address matters identified at inspection.

source_index.name: Willowdale Care Home
source_index.summary:
Willowdale is a residential care home situated in Buckley, Flintshire. It is registered to provide
 accommodation and personal care for up to twenty-eight people.

 People’s well-being outcomes are good as care staff know the people they support well, they know
 what is important to them and follow detailed personal plans. Care staff support people to
 understand their rights and maximise their independence.

 People live in an environment which is good and suits their needs. The home is clean and
 comfortable. The provider undertakes regular maintenance and repairs, and ensures the
 environment is safe.

 The service is well-led and has a positive culture of promoting the well-being of supported people
 and staff. Improvements have been made since the last inspection and the service is now fully
 compliant with regulations. A new manager has been appointed who has the skills and knowledge
 required to run the service effectively. There are suitable governance and quality assurance
systems in place helping the service operate smoothly. Care staff receive training relevant to the
needs of the people they care for and receive the required level of formal support.

source_index.name: Wimsly Care Home
source_index.summary:
People living in Wimsly Care Home benefit from being cared for by a familiar staff group
who know their needs well. People are treated with dignity and respect. The service actively
supports people of diverse cultures. People can have choice and control over their daily
lives and are encouraged to be a part of the local community.

Care is planned according to the needs of individual residents. Care staff are aware of local
safeguarding procedures to keep people safe. The service is mindful of health and safety
and infection control measures to mitigate risks and keep people as safe as possible.
Medication storage and administration is good. People can access health care
assessments and advice in a timely way.

The environment in the home is clean and homely. People can personalise their rooms to a
high degree. People can access equipment needed for their care, this is serviced and
maintained as required. Fire alarm tests are regularly performed, and utility checks are up
to date for the home.

The Responsible Individual (RI) visits the home and reports on quality standards as
required by legislation. Care staff are given training and supervision to help them in their
role. Recruitment and retention of staff is good. The manager regularly audits the service to
ensure good care standards and is visible and approachable for staff.

source_index.name: Windsor Road
source_index.summary:
Windsor Road provides accommodation for up to six people. It does not provide nursing care.
 People receive an excellent standard of care and support from a consistent care staff team who
 know them well and understand their aspirations and needs. Personal plans are produced with
 people and clearly identify the desired outcomes of each individual and how best to support them to
 achieve these goals.
 People’s wellbeing is excellent because they are consistently supported to achieve positive
 outcomes, whilst any identified risks are managed effectively.
 The property is homely and welcoming and meets the needs of people living there. It is well
 maintained; safety checks are carried out and the level of cleanliness is good. The overall standard
 of the environment is good.
 People benefit from an excellent standard of Leadership and Management. The Responsible
 Individual (RI) visits the home frequently and knows the staff and residents well. The RI works
 closely with the home manager and assistant manager to provide and maintain an open and
positive culture at the service. Care staff enjoy working at the service, they feel extremely well
supported and are motivated by a caring and compassionate management team. Highly effective
governance is clearly documented through robust audit and reporting processes.

source_index.name: Windsor Street
source_index.summary:
Windsor Street is located near the town of Aberdare, offering convenient access to local amenities.
 The service provides accommodation for up to four people, each in their own self-contained flat.

 People experience good well-being outcomes. People can make choices about their day to day
 lives and are supported to engage in activities they enjoy. People are supported with their health
 needs and have good access to relevant health and social care professionals.

 Care and support is good. Care documentation is person-centred, outcome focused and reflective
 of people’s care and support needs. Care documentation is reviewed regularly and updated as
 required to reflect changes in needs. Risks to people’s health and safety are appropriately
 assessed and managed.

 The environment is good. People live in an environment that is suited to their needs and promotes
 their comfort, safety, and well-being. The home is clean, well maintained, and provides a
 welcoming and homely atmosphere.

 Leadership and management require improvement. Care staff report feeling well-supported in their
roles and express satisfaction working at the service. Care staff have access to training to support
them in meeting the needs of people; however, further improvement is required to ensure training
provision is consistently effective and meets all identified needs.

source_index.name: Witla Court
source_index.summary:
Witla Court is a care home located in a residential area of Cardiff. The service supports people
 living with learning disabilities, mental health and associated needs.

 People living at Witla Court experience excellent well-being outcomes. We found care staff promote
 independence, and positive risk-taking. Activities are personalised and encourage people to access
 their local communities. People told us they are actively involved in decisions which affect them.

 The standard of care and support is excellent. The provider conducts detailed assessments, paying
 attention to the compatibility of the individuals at the service. People are supported by staff who
 know them well. Personal plans are detailed, accurate and regularly reviewed with people and with
 their multi-disciplinary team.

 The environment is good, safe and supports people’s well-being. Indoor and outdoor areas are
 attractive, personalised and comfortable to suit people’s preferences. People give their opinion on
 their home and this is listened to.
The leadership and management at Witla Court is excellent. The provider priorities staff well-being
and has several initiatives in place such as access to free counselling. Staff told us they feel
supported and management are approachable. The Responsible Individual (RI) completes regular
visits and gathers feedback from people and staff.

source_index.name: Woburn Hill
source_index.summary:
People are supported to have their own routines and activities, as well as live together,
within a homely setting. They are encouraged and supported to develop independence
skills, to socialise in and away from the home. We saw people are fully involved in planning
their daily routines and care needs, which focus on individual choice and preferences.

People are responsible for their own rooms, and these are personalised to their taste.
Communal areas meet people’s needs and preferences. We found people thrive, feel at
home and are content in their surroundings. They have positive relationships with the
people they live with and care staff who support them.

The provider ensures safe recruitment of staff and provide support through formal
supervision and training. Staff told us they feel valued. There are robust monitoring systems
in place to ensure effective oversight of the service.

source_index.name: Woffington House
source_index.summary:
Woffington Care Home is a service in Tredegar providing care for adults without nursing needs.
 Since our last inspection, the service has appointed a new service provider, responsible individual
 (RI) and manager. Although these changes are recent, we found significant improvements across
 the service. Two areas for improvement (AFI) identified at the previous inspection have been
 addressed and are no longer required. Both related to oversight by the RI, which has strengthened
 considerably. The AFI relating to medication management remains in place. Whilst medication
 systems have improved, further action is required to ensure medicines are managed consistently
 and safely.

 Many people experience positive outcomes because their well-being is promoted and they receive
 good quality care and support. People are encouraged to make choices, maintain relationships and
 take part in meaningful activities. The environment is comfortable, personalised and supports
 people's needs. Leaders have strengthened governance and oversight arrangements, which
 support the continued development of the service. Planned environmental improvements and
 ongoing work to enhance care planning demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement.
 We have rated all four inspection themes as ‘Good’.

source_index.name: Woodcroft
source_index.summary:
Woodcroft Care Home is a large, purpose-built service on the outskirts of Cardiff. The service
 provides accommodation and care for up to 60 people aged 55 and over. It is organised into three
 self-contained communities, offering support for people living with dementia, general residential
 needs and respite care. There is good access to local transport links with local shops within walking
 distance.

 Wellbeing is rated as excellent because people live in a vibrant and inclusive environment where
 they are supported to enjoy life and have positive meaningful experiences. People describe living in
 the service as highly positive, with a strong emphasis placed on activities that bring joy and
 purpose.

 Care and support is rated as good because people receive good quality care from staff who know
 them well and treat them with kindness dignity and respect. Care staff support people to maintain
independence and make choices. People are supported to maintain their identity and interests.

Environment is rated as good because people live in a safe, comfortable, and welcoming
environment which supports their wellbeing.

Leadership and management is rated as excellent because the management team has
successfully created an environment where there are high levels of confidence from residents,
relatives, and care staff, and where continuous improvement is both expected and achieved.

source_index.name: Woodcroft Care Home Ltd
source_index.summary:
Well-being is good. The service demonstrates a strong commitment to supporting people to
 develop their independence, daily living skills, and participation in meaningful activities. People are
 empowered to express their views, share concerns, and feel confident their voices are listened to
 and acted upon.

 Care and support is good. Care documentation is detailed, clear, and person-centred, ensuring
 people remain at the heart of planning and delivery. People are supported to make choices about
 their daily lives and prioritise what matters most to them. Medication management systems are
 robust, and standards of hygiene and infection prevention and control are well maintained.

 The environment is good. It is safe, clean, and comfortably maintained to meet people’s needs.
 There are plans in place to refurbish and redecorate the service, which demonstrates a
 commitment to continuous improvement.
Leadership and management are good. The provider maintains effective oversight and is
committed to delivering a high-quality service. Staff receive appropriate training and reported
feeling well supported and satisfied in their roles. Recruitment processes are robust, and staffing
levels are sufficient to meet people’s needs. There are effective audit systems in place to monitor
performance and drive improvements. The Responsible Individual (RI) values feedback from
people using the service and is committed to implementing changes to enhance their experiences.

source_index.name: Woodfield Care Home (Nursing)
source_index.summary:
Woodfield Care Home is a nursing home set in a countryside location, providing care and support
 to people with nursing needs. We found outcomes for people are Good across all four inspection
 themes: Well‑being, Care and Support, Environment, and Leadership and Management. People
 experience positive well‑being outcomes and are supported by knowledgeable and motivated staff
 who know them well. Care and support is person‑centred and delivered with kindness and respect.
 Families and professionals gave consistently positive feedback about the quality of care. People
 live in a clean, safe, and homely environment that supports comfort, dignity, and well‑being.
 Leaders are visible and approachable and promote an inclusive culture. While some systems
 require strengthening, these have not impacted on people’s outcomes.

source_index.name: Woodland Lodge
source_index.summary:
People receive a good standard of care and are happy living at this service. People are
supported to live meaningful and active lives and receive care in the way that best meets
their needs. People’s individuality is celebrated at this service, and they are supported by a
dedicated and caring team of care workers.

Care workers are happy working at this service. They told us they are supported by the
manager and Responsible Individual (RI) and can raise any matters whenever they need to.
Care workers receive appropriate training for their role and are supported to develop their
skills by further training if they wish. Care workers work flexibly to meet the needs of the
service and to support the people who live there.

The RI has good oversight of the service and is supported by a manager. There are good
governance and oversight arrangements in place within the service to ensure its smooth
operation.

The service has undergone a series of improvements and is clean, clutter free and a
homely warm environment for those who live there.

source_index.name: Woodland Lodge Care Home
source_index.summary:
Woodland Lodge Care Home provides residential care for adults age eighteen and over. It can
 accommodate a maximum of nineteen people, of any gender. The service is located near the
harbour town of Tenby on the picturesque Pembrokeshire coastline.

People experience good well-being outcomes. They told us they feel safe and happy with the
service. Care staff have developed positive relationships with people, relatives and visiting
professionals.

Care and support are good. We saw care staff treat people with dignity and respect and encourage
them to make choices about their care and support. Care staff know people well and understand
what is important to them.

The environment is good. People live in a clean, comfortable and welcoming home. The provider
continues to invest in the environment and people benefit from a range of communal and private
spaces which reflect their individual preferences and interests.

Leadership and management are good. An experienced management team leads the service with
oversight from a visible and accessible Responsible Individual (RI).

source_index.name: Woodlands
source_index.summary:
Woodlands is a homely and welcoming service for adults based in the Swansea area close to
 numerous community facilities and amenities. People and their relatives told us they are happy with
 the care and support provided by the service. There are personal plans in place which reflect the
 person well. The Responsible Individual (RI) demonstrates good governance which in turn drives
 any improvements needed. The management team have a strong presence in the service and are
 experienced and dedicated. The service employs a skilled staff team who are appropriately trained
 to meet people’s needs. Staff feel well supported by the management team and are confident in
 their roles.

 People experience good wellbeing outcomes as the service actively promotes independence and
 support to achieve their goals. People are supported to do the things that matter to them in a
 person-centred way. The care and support people receive is good, and people tell us their
 experience of being supported by the service is positive. The environment is good and enables
 people to achieve their identified outcomes. Leadership and management of the service is good.
 The service is very well led and has a positive culture of promoting the well-being of the people it
 supports along with its staff.

source_index.name: Woodlee - Short-term care
source_index.provider: Flintshire County Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Woodlee is a short-term respite service for people with a learning disability situated in Buckley. It is
 a bungalow adapted for the needs of people with mobility issues in a quiet residential area. It is
 within walking distance of the town centre, in which there are shops, cafes and public houses. The
 service is homely and comfortable throughout, providing a ‘home from home’ feeling for people
 during their stays.

 People are treated with dignity and respect by support staff who know them well. They know
 people’s routines and preferences and people can enjoy good wellbeing outcomes during their
 stay. A good level of care and support is delivered by skilled and qualified support staff. The team
 is supported by a manager and deputy manager, who visit the services regularly and provide good
 oversight.

source_index.name: Woodside & Elms
source_index.summary:
Wellbeing is excellent at Woodshed and Elms. Staff use innovative, person-centred approaches to
 improve independence and well-being. People achieve meaningful outcomes through community
 participation, hobbies, positive risk-taking and technology. They enjoy choice, cultural inclusion and
 social connections, while skilled staff provide safe, compassionate support that promotes dignity
 and safeguards individuals.

 Care and support is good. People receive safe, person-centred care supported by effective multi-
 agency working, positive risk management and robust healthcare arrangements. Staff know people
 well and promote independence, choice and wellbeing. Improving personalised care planning and
 co-produced outcomes will further strengthen responsive support.
The environment is good. Woodside and Elms comprising of two properties supporting eight people
in a safe, accessible, and homely environment. Spacious indoor and outdoor areas promote
independence, social interaction, meaningful activities and well-being. Ongoing maintenance and
improvements ensure peoples safety and quality of life.

Leadership and governance arrangements are good and effective, with robust oversight,
responsive quality assurance processes and a strong commitment to continuous improvement.
Leaders act promptly when concerns arise, support staff development, recognise achievement, and
ensure policies, training and practices promote high-quality, safe and person-centred care.

source_index.name: Woodside Grange Care Home
source_index.summary:
People are happy with with the support they receive at Woodside Grange. People are
supported by responsive and skilled staff who know them well. Care staff provide positive
reassurance and interaction regularly. People are supported to make choices about their
daily lives wherever possible. Personal plans are person-centred, detailed, reflect people’s
needs, reviewed and changed accordingly. Activities are on offer with staff facilitating them
and external entertainers coming to the service periodically.


Staff feel well supported by Management and are provided with training to meet people’s
needs. There are suitable governance arrangements in place with the Responsible
Individual (RI) visiting the home regularly to oversee management of the home and gather
the opinions of people, relatives and staff to help to improve and develop the service.
People’s views are reflected in six monthly quality of care review reports. The environment
is well maintained, and the service is operating in line with the statement of purpose.

source_index.name: Woodside House Residential Home
source_index.summary:
Wellbeing of residents is rated as good. People experience warm and respectful relationships and
 feel safe, supported, and involved in decisions about their care. Activities and family contact are
 encouraged. However, outdoor and communal spaces need improvement, and Welsh language
 provision is still underdeveloped.

 Care and support are rated as requiring improvement because infection prevention and control are
 not strong enough. Despite this, care is person‑centred, well organised, and responsive. Staff
 monitor health, nutrition, hydration and risks effectively. Residents and relatives give highly positive
 feedback. Safeguarding, medication management, and infection control processes are strong,
 though care records could better capture individuals’ personal voices.

 The home is safe and adequately equipped, but several areas need attention. Outdoor areas look
 untidy, some communal spaces feel cramped, and there are internal storage and safety issues that
 require action. Fire safety and maintenance checks are mostly completed but need more consistent
 auditing. Governance is effective, with clear accountability, good communication, and strong audit
 systems. Staff feel supported and well trained. Recruitment documentation needs improvement,
 particularly in ensuring consistent references and digitising staff files.

source_index.name: Wylesfield Residential Care Home
source_index.summary:
Wylesfield Residential Care Home is a homely and welcoming service which provides personal
 care and support to people. It is situated in Llandrindod Wells, within walking distance to local
 amenities such as shops, cafes and restaurants.

 People living at the service experience excellent well-being outcomes as they have control over
 their lives and are treated with dignity and respect. We saw people relaxing in their environment
 and participating in meaningful activities. Friendships are encouraged and people’s well-being is
 promoted. Care and support is good. We saw person-centred care planning and the review of
 personal plans is completed frequently and with involvement of people and/or their representatives.
 People and their families expressed satisfaction with the quality of care provided.

 The environment is good and promotes people’s well-being outcomes by providing safe, clean and
 homely accommodation. The service provider currently has an ongoing programme of
 refurbishment and is continually making improvements to the environment.

 Leadership and management is good. There is a dedicated and knowledgeable management team
 in place who support staff through formal and informal supervision. The Responsible Individual (RI)
 visits the service routinely and ensures effective governance and oversight.

source_index.name: Wynne Crest Care Home
source_index.summary:
Wynne Crest care home is a residential care home for adults over the age of 55. It is situated in a
 quiet residential area of Old Colwyn, and is in walking distance of local shops, a church, park, and
 the beach. There is easy access to local transport links for those who wish to visit the local area.
 People live in a home which is comfortable and homely with access to good facilities and specialist
 aids.

 People experience good wellbeing outcomes because they are treated with dignity and respect by
 care staff who know them well. Care staff support people to maintain their independence as much
 as possible. They deliver person centred care and ensure people receive a good level of care and
 support in line with their wishes.

 The manager and responsible individual (RI) have good oversight of the service. The manager
 completes regular audits to ensure the service is running smoothly. They are approachable and
 take any feedback seriously to ensure it is acted upon. The RI visits every three months, speaking
 to people, for their views and inspecting the premises.

source_index.name: Y Bwthyn
source_index.provider: Carmarthenshire County Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Y Bwthyn is a residential care home located in Llanelli, Carmarthenshire.

 Wellbeing is rated as ‘Good’, as people are involved in a range of meaningful activities, their views
 and opinions are sought and valued, and people tell us they feel safe.

 Care and Support is rated as ‘Good’, as the person and /or their representative are involved in their
 care. Health, medical and other external professionals are involved in people’s care when needed.

 The Environment is rated as ‘Good’, as the service is well maintained, safe and homely.

 Leadership and Management is rated as ‘Good’, as the service is led by a dedicated manager and
 Responsible Individual (RI) who are respected by a well-trained and supported staff team.

source_index.name: Y Frondeg
source_index.provider: Gwynedd Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Y Frondeg provides a home for people living with physical and learning disability. The home is
 situated close to Caernarfon Town.

 Wellbeing at Y Frondeg is excellent. People are supported to be as independent and active as
 possible and achieve their chosen objectives. A person told us their life has improved drastically
 since living in the home. The service offers a strong active offer of the Welsh language and people
 remain a part of the local community.

 Care and support are excellent. People have care planned with them and records are person
 centred and reflect people’s choices and preferences. People receive care from familiar staff who
 provide continuation in care. Medicine processes are well thought out and audited.

 The environment is rated good. People can personalise their bedroom surrounding themselves with
things of importance to them. The home is an older building that requires upgrading, a budget has
been agreed to meet this.

Leadership and management are excellent. Senior staff are supportive of care staff. Care staff
receive training and meaningful supervision. Care staff are supported to advance their careers and
young apprentices receive mentorship. The Responsible Individual (RI) visits the service and
provides quality reports in line with legislation.

source_index.name: Y Garreg Lwyd Care Home
source_index.summary:
An experienced and well-regarded manager effectively leads a team of experienced
workers to make sure people receive person centred care in a relaxed and homely
environment. Care workers know people well, knowing what and who is important to them.

Care workers are safely recruited and suitably trained, supported and supervised. They feel
valued and part of the team and some have had their skills acknowledged and been
promoted during their employment.

Detailed records help inform care, but some improvements are required to make them more
person centred. Care workers know people well, and relationships between people, their
families and the staff team are good. Relatives have high levels of confidence in the
service.

source_index.name: Y Gelli
source_index.summary:
Y Gelli is a residential service for ten adults. Accommodation is provided in either individual or
 shared flats and there is plenty of outside space for people to access and enjoy. It is well located
 close to local amenities with good transport links which support independence.

 People are happy, their voices are heard and they have as much control over their lives as
 possible. They experience high quality care and support from excellent care staff who know them
 well. People are involved in their personal plans, attend reviews and achieve their own life goals.
 Close friendships and strong bonds have formed between people living there, providing emotional
 support and making memories together. There are ample opportunities to make new friends and
 stay in touch with other people who are important in their lives.

 People benefit from a stable and committed staff team, who offer continuity and consistency. Care
 staff are carefully recruited; people have a very strong say in who works there and are actively
involved in the recruitment process. Care staff complete a variety of training with some
opportunities for further promotion. They told us they all feel very well supported and are positive
about the service.

Quality assurance systems and processes ensure good oversight of the service. The RI completes
reports and obtains feedback from everyone, identifying what works well and areas for
improvement.

source_index.name: Y Gilwen
source_index.provider: Prestwood Residential Homes Ltd and CareTech Community Services Limited.
source_index.summary:
Y Gilwen is set within its own grounds on a residential estate in Caernarfon. Y Gilwen comprises of
 a large four-bedroom house with two smaller self-contained flats adjacent to the property.

 People are happy living in Y Gilwen are recognised and respected for who they are. People have
 developed positive relationships with staff, who encourage and support them to live a healthy
 lifestyle. People are encouraged to speak out and influence decisions affecting their everyday lives.
 They are able to follow their interests and spend time outdoors and in the community.

 People are supported in clean, homely accommodation that is well maintained. The home is well
 run and there is a positive culture within the service. Standards of practice within the home are
 closely monitored, and action is taken where improvements can be made. People are supported by
 adequate numbers of staff.
Leadership and management are good as managers lead by example, work in partnership with
people, staff and professionals to provide a safe, reliable service that enhances people’s lives.
There are robust systems of audit to help the Responsible Individual (RI) monitor the quality of the
service and drive improvement.

source_index.name: Y Plas EMI Care Home
source_index.summary:
People are generally treated with kindness, dignity and respect and live in an environment that
 supports their well-being. However, inconsistencies in care documentation and monitoring records
 limit assurance that people’s health, personal care and social needs are always met effectively.

 Care and Support is rated Requires Significant Improvement. There are continued inconsistencies
 regarding personal planning, medication management and record keeping. Personal plans do not
 always provide clear, accurate or person-centred guidance. Medication errors and weaknesses in
 oversight processes were also found. Due to the seriousness of these issues, Priority Action
 Notices were re-issued.

 The service provides a generally safe, clean and homely environment. Living spaces support
 people’s comfort and safety. Communal areas offer opportunities for social interaction and
 relaxation.

 Leadership and Management is rated Requires Improvement. Although some progress has been
 made since previous inspections, quality assurance and governance systems have not been
 effective in identifying and addressing ongoing concerns. Further improvements are required to
strengthen oversight, ensure compliance and secure sustained positive outcomes for people using
the service.

The provider has acknowledged the areas of concern identified in the inspection. They have
assured us actions are underway to make the necessary improvements and provide additional
leadership and management oversight. Further embedding of these actions is required to ensure
the required improvements are made.

source_index.name: Y Plas Residential Care Home
source_index.provider: Carmarthenshire County Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
This is a residential care home located in the centre of Llanelli in Carmarthenshire.
 During this inspection the rating awarded for Wellbeing is ‘Good ’as people are involved a range of
 meaningful and beneficial activities, their views and suggestions are valued and they feel safe. The
 rating awarded for Care and Support is ‘Good’ as the person and /or their representative are
 involved in their care. Health, medical and other external professionals are involved in people’s
 care when needed. The rating awarded for the Environment is ‘Good’ as the service is well
 maintained, safe and homely. The rating awarded for Leadership and Management is ‘Good’ as
 there is strong oversight of the service by the Responsible Individual (RI) and the manager leads a
 motivated, well trained team of staff which value their support and leadership.

source_index.name: Ynysddu Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
People are very happy with the care they receive and speak positively about the home and
care staff. There are dedicated activity staff who ensure that people spend their time doing
things that matter to them. Care staff are experienced, knowledgeable and understand the
needs of the people they care for. Care staff receive training and supervision and are very
happy working at Ynysddu Nursing Home. Care staff feel supported and valued by the
manager. Personal plans of care contain detailed information about people’s needs and
how they should be met and are reviewed regularly. There are policies and procedures in
place for the running of the home and people are given information about the service
including details of how to complain if they are not happy. Quality assurance monitoring
takes place regularly but would be strengthened with clinical auditing. The Responsible
Individual (RI) visits often and has good oversight of the service; the manager feels well
supported by the RI. People live in a suitable environment that is safe and meets their
needs, but some cosmetic redecoration and updating of some areas of the home is
required.

source_index.name: Ynystawe Lodge
source_index.summary:
Ynystawe lodge is a specialised service delivering support and accommodation to individuals with a
 range of complex diagnoses including learning disabilities, mental health conditions, brain injury
 and autism.

 People have excellent well-being in Ynystawe lodge, leading active and busy lives with dedicated
 and driven care staff who know them well. People’s progression in the service with gaining
 confidence and independence is visible and people are happy and enjoy doing things that matter to
 them.

 Care and support is excellent, Personal plans portray the views of people ensuring family members
 are involved in their production and routine reviews. Relatives spoken with during the inspection
 gave exemplary feedback of the care provided to their loved ones and the frequent communication
 they have from the service.

 The environment is good providing people with various, safe, internal and external communal and
 private spaces to spend their time. Whether this is alone, with others or to undertake events and
 activities. There is clear ongoing investment in the service to keep it well maintained and implement
changes that improve people’s outcomes

Leadership and management is good and there is a drive to encourage people to reach their goals
and aspire to new ones. The provider has good oversight and governance arrangements in place to
ensure the continuous smooth running of the service. Care staff are recruited appropriately,
supported and well trained to carry out their roles successfully.

source_index.name: Yr Hafan Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
People living at Yr Hafan Nursing Home experience good outcomes across all four inspection
 areas. The service meets regulatory expectations and delivers consistent, person-centred care.

 People are supported to live safely and healthily, with choice and control over daily life. Care
 promotes dignity, independence and positive risk-taking. People feel happy and secure, and
 families express confidence in how wellbeing and safety are promoted. Safeguarding arrangements
 are effective. Care is compassionate, responsive and tailored to individual needs. Care plans are
 detailed, regularly reviewed and reflect people’s preferences. People are supported to engage in
 meaningful activities and social interaction. Medicines are managed safely, infection prevention
 measures are effective, and families report high satisfaction with care.

 People live in a clean, safe and welcoming environment that supports comfort and wellbeing.
 Bedrooms are personalised and communal areas are well maintained. Health and safety systems
 are effective, with plans in place to improve outdoor space.

 The service is well led, with effective governance and quality assurance. Staff are well supported
 through supervision, appraisal and training, ensuring they have the skills to deliver safe,
 high-quality care.

source_index.name: Yr Hafod Residential Care Home
source_index.provider: Ceredigion County Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Yr Hafod is a residential care home on the outskirts of Cardigan town. Well-being is rated as good
 because people receive a service which is person centred and enables them to achieve their health
 and well-being outcomes. People have developed positive relationships with the familiar and caring
 staff. Care and support is rated as good because people receive care and support from a team of
 professional and friendly care workers. Care workers are guided by accurate and individualised
 personal plans which enable them to meet peoples needs. The environment is rated as good
 because the provider has completed the work required to the environment to close the Priority
 Action Notice (PAN). People are comfortable and relaxed throughout the home and care workers
 are positive about the impact the improvements have made to people’s well-being. Leadership and
 management is rated as good because the provider has good oversight of the service. The
 effective leadership ensures people receive good quality care from a team of motivated and skilled
 care workers who receive good support from their managers.

source_index.name: Yr Hen Rheithordy
source_index.summary:
Yr Hen Rheithordy has a homely atmosphere that puts people at ease.

 People experience good wellbeing as there is a team of motivated, friendly and caring staff who
 support people to enjoy a good quality of life. People are listened to and respected. Care workers
 embrace their individuality and people have as much control over their day-to-day lives as possible.

 Care and support is good as personal plans now provide more insight into who people are and how
 they can be supported to achieve their goals. They are regularly reviewed and updated. They
 actively promote people’s health and independence. People feel content doing things they enjoy in
 the home.

 People live in an environment which is good. The home is clean, well maintained and suitably
 equipped. There is ongoing refurbishment of the home.
Leadership and management is good as managers lead by example, work in partnership with
people, staff and professionals to provide a safe, reliable service that enhances people’s lives.
There are robust systems and audits to help the Responsible Individual (RI) monitor the quality of
the service and drive improvement.

source_index.name: Yr Ysgol Ltd
source_index.summary:
People who have made Yr Ysgol their home receive a good standard of care. Most people are
 happy with the care and support they get and have formed positive relationships with the staff
 team. Relatives have high levels of confidence in the service.

 Wellbeing is rated as good because the motivated staff team strive to give people opportunities to
 do things that matter to them.

 Care and support is rated as good because the team is led by an experienced manager and deputy
 who are well regarded by the rest of the team. Personal plans help inform and direct care and
 support.

 The environment is rated as good because standards of cleanliness are high and the service is well
 maintained with plenty of outside space as well as several small lounges and dining rooms.
Leadership and management is rated as good because the manager is very visible throughout the
service and has support from a wider team of staff including human resources and senior leaders.
Staff feel proud to work for the service.

source_index.name: Ystrad Fechan
source_index.provider: Rhondda Cynon Taff County Borough Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Ystrad Fechan is a Local Authority respite service for adults with a learning disability and
 associated needs, located centrally in Treorchy. It is co-located on a site with another Local
 Authority service, being based in the smaller bungalow building.


 Well-being is good because people are supported to make choices, maintain independence and
 achieve outcomes which are important to them. Strong person-centred planning, meaningful
 activities and positive risk-taking help people enjoy their respite experiences. Care and support is
 good because people receive personalised care from skilled care staff who understand their needs
 and preferences. Good safeguarding, medication management and infection prevention
 arrangements help keep people safe and well. The environment is good because people stay in a
 comfortable, welcoming and well-maintained setting which promotes independence and meets a
 wide range of needs. Leadership and management is good because leaders provide effective
 oversight and continue to drive improvement. Strong governance, quality assurance and learning
 arrangements support positive outcomes for people, while a well-trained staff team delivers
 consistent care.

source_index.name: Zoar Care Home
source_index.summary:
Zoar is a residential home in Tonypandy, providing care and support for up to 30 people.


 People experience good well-being outcomes and are supported by care staff who know them well
 and promote their dignity, choice and independence. Feedback from people and their
 representatives is positive, with many describing the service as caring, welcoming and supportive.

 Care and support is good. People receive personalised care from care staff who understand their
 needs, preferences and routines. The service benefits from detailed care planning systems,
 effective safeguarding arrangements and good systems for managing medication and infection
 prevention and control.

 The environment is good. People live in a clean, comfortable and personalised home with access
to communal areas that support social interaction and well-being. Systems are in place to maintain
equipment and promote safety, and the provider has plans to further enhance parts of the
environment.

Leadership and management are good. Staff speak positively about the support they receive and
governance systems provide effective oversight of the service. Leaders recognise opportunities to
further strengthen practice and demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement.

topics.name: Medicines management
topics.actions: Audit medicine administration records, storage, reconciliation, PRN protocols and staff competency; document exceptions and follow-up.
topics.evidence: MAR audit, competency records, storage checks and documented corrective actions
topics.local_test: Sample administration records against actual staff practice with the medicines lead.
topics.success_outcome: Exceptions are detected, followed up and checked; staff demonstrate the agreed local procedure.

topics.name: Safeguarding & incident learning
topics.actions: Review safeguarding escalation, incident reporting and CIW notifications. Check that staff understand local procedures and that learning reaches the team.
topics.evidence: Escalation log, training records, incident reviews and notifications

negative.name: Llanthewy House
negative.text: We found the relevant agencies have not always been informed of significant incidents and events.

topics.local_test: Walk through a local escalation scenario and trace a recent incident review.
topics.success_outcome: Staff explain escalation confidently and can show how incident learning changed practice.

topics.name: Personal plans & risk assessment
topics.actions: Sample personal plans for individual preferences, changing needs, review dates and usable risk controls. Check that staff can apply the guidance in practice.
topics.evidence: Plan reviews, resident involvement and observed practice
topics.local_test: Compare sampled plans with current preferences, changing needs and observed care.
topics.success_outcome: Plans are usable and consistent with the support people actually receive.

topics.name: Staffing & recruitment
topics.actions: Review staffing against actual dependency and safe recruitment checks. Examine continuity, induction and the impact of vacancies or agency use.
topics.evidence: Dependency reviews, rota analysis and recruitment checks

negative.name: Llanthewy House
negative.text: Recruitment practices were not considered during the visit, there have been no new staff members employed at the service.

topics.local_test: Compare recent rotas and induction checks with actual support needs and continuity.
topics.success_outcome: The agreed staffing arrangements work in observed practice; identified gaps receive follow-up.

topics.name: Training & supervision
topics.actions: Reconcile the training matrix with current roles and residents' needs. Sample supervision records and assess competence, rather than attendance alone.
topics.evidence: Training matrix, competency assessment and supervision records

negative.name: Llanthewy House
negative.text: Staff must receive core training appropriate to the work they Regulation 36(2)(d) perform The RI must provide a six monthly quality of care and support Regulation 66 report The area(s) identified above require improvement but we have not issued a priority action notice on this occasion.

topics.local_test: Ask staff to demonstrate a role-relevant skill and compare supervision evidence.
topics.success_outcome: Competence is demonstrated in practice rather than inferred from attendance records alone.

topics.name: Leadership & quality assurance
topics.actions: Review responsible-individual oversight and quality reviews. Track audit actions to closure and show how resident and relative feedback changes the service.
topics.evidence: RI visit records, quality reports, feedback and closed action log

negative.name: Llanthewy House
negative.text: Staff must receive core training appropriate to the work they Regulation 36(2)(d) perform The RI must provide a six monthly quality of care and support Regulation 66 report The area(s) identified above require improvement but we have not issued a priority action notice on this occasion.

topics.local_test: Trace an audit exception and resident feedback through ownership, action and recheck.
topics.success_outcome: Oversight detects gaps and verifies improvements with records, observation and resident feedback.

topics.name: Rights, choice & independence
topics.actions: Check consent and decision-making records, legal authorisations where applicable, and how daily practice supports choice, dignity and independence.
topics.evidence: Decision records, authorisations and resident-led goals
topics.local_test: Observe daily choices and compare decision records with what people describe.
topics.success_outcome: People's choices are respected in practice and applicable decision records remain coherent.

topics.name: Nutrition & hydration
topics.actions: Review nutritional and hydration risks, weight trends, meal preferences and escalation when needs change; assess the dining experience with residents.
topics.evidence: Risk screening, monitoring, referrals and resident feedback
topics.local_test: Observe a meal and compare preferences, monitoring records and escalation arrangements.
topics.success_outcome: People describe a suitable dining experience and changing needs receive documented follow-up.

topics.name: Infection prevention
topics.actions: Check infection-control practice, cleaning assurance and staff competence. Follow up audit exceptions and verify that practical supplies and routines are effective.
topics.evidence: IPC audit, cleaning checks and competency records
topics.local_test: Observe agreed cleaning and hygiene routines alongside the local audit evidence.
topics.success_outcome: Routines work in practice and audit exceptions are corrected and rechecked.

topics.name: Environment & fire safety
topics.actions: Review fire and premises safety, servicing, accessibility and environmental risks; verify outstanding maintenance actions and person-specific evacuation arrangements.
topics.evidence: Safety checks, servicing, maintenance log and evacuation plans
topics.local_test: Walk the premises and trace sampled safety or maintenance exceptions to verification.
topics.success_outcome: Identified hazards receive appropriate follow-up and checks reflect actual conditions.

topics.name: Welsh language & culture
topics.actions: Assess the Welsh language active offer and cultural needs proactively, including how preferences are identified and acted upon; do not equate no requests with adequate provision.
topics.evidence: Language preferences, active-offer arrangements and accessible information
topics.local_test: Ask how language preferences are identified and observe the active offer in practice.
topics.success_outcome: People can access the agreed language and cultural support, not merely a recorded preference.

topics.name: Meaningful activity & community
topics.actions: Review opportunities for personally meaningful activity, relationships and community participation, using resident outcomes rather than activity counts alone.
topics.evidence: Resident goals, participation records and feedback
topics.local_test: Discuss meaningful goals with residents and compare participation records with experience.
topics.success_outcome: People describe opportunities that matter to them and feedback shapes future support.

source_index.name: Llanthewy House
source_index.summary:
The individual outcomes of people living at the service are generally met. The ethos of the
service promotes a person centred approach to their care and support. We were told
individuals daily lives have been adversely affected by the pandemic. The staff team is
small and stable which provides consistency and familiarity to residents. We found systems
to support the smooth running of the service are ineffective. Arrangements to protect
individuals from abuse and harm need strengthening. Staff have not received the necessary
core training to update their skills and knowledge. The responsible individual ( RI), is not
carrying out their regulatory duties in regards to overseeing the management of the service
and providing assurance it is safe, well run and complies with regulations. The RI has failed
to conduct any formal visits to the service since its registration in January 2019. Quality of
care reviews have not taken place as required by the regulations. Due to the significance of
our findings, we identified a number of areas of improvements linked to the leadership and
management of the service.

narrative: The fixed cohort contains 2 homes across 2 authorities; 2 latest archived reports provide 20 source PDF pages.

topics.name: Medicines management
topics.actions: Audit medicine administration records, storage, reconciliation, PRN protocols and staff competency; document exceptions and follow-up.
topics.evidence: MAR audit, competency records, storage checks and documented corrective actions
topics.local_test: Sample administration records against actual staff practice with the medicines lead.
topics.success_outcome: Exceptions are detected, followed up and checked; staff demonstrate the agreed local procedure.

topics.name: Safeguarding & incident learning
topics.actions: Review safeguarding escalation, incident reporting and CIW notifications. Check that staff understand local procedures and that learning reaches the team.
topics.evidence: Escalation log, training records, incident reviews and notifications

negative.name: Ty Canol
negative.text: After serious incidents, young people are offered a debrief, however records show young people do not always engage.

actions.name: Ty Canol
actions.text: Young people's files are difficult to follow and incidents are recorded in different places.

topics.local_test: Walk through a local escalation scenario and trace a recent incident review.
topics.success_outcome: Staff explain escalation confidently and can show how incident learning changed practice.

topics.name: Personal plans & risk assessment
topics.actions: Sample personal plans for individual preferences, changing needs, review dates and usable risk controls. Check that staff can apply the guidance in practice.
topics.evidence: Plan reviews, resident involvement and observed practice

negative.name: The Byre
negative.text: Where needed there are Positive Behavioural Support plans in place, as well as care plans and risk assessments, however these are not always cross referenced in the personal plans.

actions.name: The Byre
actions.text: The service provider has failed to provide a personal plan which sets out how a person’s needs will be met and their outcomes achieved.

actions.name: Ty Canol
actions.text: Young people do not have a current personal plan which provides a detailed record of how their needs are to be met.

topics.local_test: Compare sampled plans with current preferences, changing needs and observed care.
topics.success_outcome: Plans are usable and consistent with the support people actually receive.

topics.name: Staffing & recruitment
topics.actions: Review staffing against actual dependency and safe recruitment checks. Examine continuity, induction and the impact of vacancies or agency use.
topics.evidence: Dependency reviews, rota analysis and recruitment checks
topics.local_test: Compare recent rotas and induction checks with actual support needs and continuity.

source_index.name: The Byre
source_index.summary:
The Byre is a respite facility which provides support for up to three people at any one time.
The service has implemented significant improvements since our last inspection in relation
to health and safety of the environment and record keeping. People are happy with the
service provided and family members are very complimentary about the quality of care and
support.

The accommodation is spacious, clean and presented in a manner which reduces risks
while also considering the aesthetics and comfort within the home. The service benefits
from the adjoining community farm which we were told people enjoy carrying out tasks to
help look after the animals.
There are leadership arrangements in place and the responsible individual (RI) is now well
informed of the service quality and effectiveness. The RI has overseen the improvements in
the service since the last inspection and a new Manager has been appointed who, on the
day of inspection, was present and in the process of completing their induction, overseen
by the RI.

source_index.name: Ty Canol
source_index.summary:
Ty Canol is a children’s home providing care and support for young people.

At the previous inspection, significant shortfalls were identified, and we issued seven
Priority Action Notices and two Areas for Improvement in relation to the care and support of
young people, the environment and Leadership and Management of the service. At this
inspection, we found the service provider has taken action to address the regulatory
breaches to ensure good quality care and support for young people is being provided.

The service closed for a period of review and now provides young people with a full
complement of permanent care staff who have received adequate training. Care staff told
us there has been significant change within the leadership and management and it is a
positive place to work.

Young people are beginning to form positive relationships with care staff and although they
do not always actively engage, care staff encourage young people to reach their potential
and demonstrate a desire to improve the well-being of young people

source_index.name: Forestry House
source_index.summary:
Forestry House provides care and support for six young people between the age of five and
nineteen. Young people are supported to achieve positive well-being outcomes and care
staff are motivated and inclusive in developing strategies to increase young people’s
engagement.

Since the last inspection the service provider has focused on the suitability of their service
for young people and sustaining and improving the areas of development identified in 2021.
The overall governance and management of the service is a good standard and provides
assurances it is committed to continuous improvement and development.

Work is required to continue improving the environment, with particular attention to
bedrooms and bathroom facilities and the manager advised there is a development plan in
place.

topics.name: Medicines management
topics.actions: Audit medicine administration records, storage, reconciliation, PRN protocols and staff competency; document exceptions and follow-up.
topics.evidence: MAR audit, competency records, storage checks and documented corrective actions
topics.local_test: Sample administration records against actual staff practice with the medicines lead.
topics.success_outcome: Exceptions are detected, followed up and checked; staff demonstrate the agreed local procedure.

topics.name: Safeguarding & incident learning
topics.actions: Review safeguarding escalation, incident reporting and CIW notifications. Check that staff understand local procedures and that learning reaches the team.
topics.evidence: Escalation log, training records, incident reviews and notifications
topics.local_test: Walk through a local escalation scenario and trace a recent incident review.
topics.success_outcome: Staff explain escalation confidently and can show how incident learning changed practice.

topics.name: Personal plans & risk assessment
topics.actions: Sample personal plans for individual preferences, changing needs, review dates and usable risk controls. Check that staff can apply the guidance in practice.
topics.evidence: Plan reviews, resident involvement and observed practice
topics.local_test: Compare sampled plans with current preferences, changing needs and observed care.
topics.success_outcome: Plans are usable and consistent with the support people actually receive.

topics.name: Staffing & recruitment
topics.actions: Review staffing against actual dependency and safe recruitment checks. Examine continuity, induction and the impact of vacancies or agency use.
topics.evidence: Dependency reviews, rota analysis and recruitment checks
topics.local_test: Compare recent rotas and induction checks with actual support needs and continuity.
topics.success_outcome: The agreed staffing arrangements work in observed practice; identified gaps receive follow-up.

topics.name: Training & supervision
topics.actions: Reconcile the training matrix with current roles and residents' needs. Sample supervision records and assess competence, rather than attendance alone.
topics.evidence: Training matrix, competency assessment and supervision records
topics.local_test: Ask staff to demonstrate a role-relevant skill and compare supervision evidence.
topics.success_outcome: Competence is demonstrated in practice rather than inferred from attendance records alone.

topics.name: Leadership & quality assurance
topics.actions: Review responsible-individual oversight and quality reviews. Track audit actions to closure and show how resident and relative feedback changes the service.
topics.evidence: RI visit records, quality reports, feedback and closed action log

positive.name: Five Oaks
positive.text: The service provider ensures the leadership and management arrangements in place, supports the smooth and effective operation of the service.The manager is experienced and has worked at the service for some years.

topics.local_test: Trace an audit exception and resident feedback through ownership, action and recheck.
topics.success_outcome: Oversight detects gaps and verifies improvements with records, observation and resident feedback.

topics.name: Rights, choice & independence
topics.actions: Check consent and decision-making records, legal authorisations where applicable, and how daily practice supports choice, dignity and independence.
topics.evidence: Decision records, authorisations and resident-led goals

positive.name: Five Oaks
positive.text: Well- established protocols protect people from having their freedom restricted unnecessarily, and detailed risk management plans help to keep people safe and as independent as possible.

topics.local_test: Observe daily choices and compare decision records with what people describe.
topics.success_outcome: People's choices are respected in practice and applicable decision records remain coherent.

topics.name: Nutrition & hydration
topics.actions: Review nutritional and hydration risks, weight trends, meal preferences and escalation when needs change; assess the dining experience with residents.
topics.evidence: Risk screening, monitoring, referrals and resident feedback
topics.local_test: Observe a meal and compare preferences, monitoring records and escalation arrangements.
topics.success_outcome: People describe a suitable dining experience and changing needs receive documented follow-up.

topics.name: Infection prevention
topics.actions: Check infection-control practice, cleaning assurance and staff competence. Follow up audit exceptions and verify that practical supplies and routines are effective.
topics.evidence: IPC audit, cleaning checks and competency records
topics.local_test: Observe agreed cleaning and hygiene routines alongside the local audit evidence.
topics.success_outcome: Routines work in practice and audit exceptions are corrected and rechecked.

topics.name: Environment & fire safety
topics.actions: Review fire and premises safety, servicing, accessibility and environmental risks; verify outstanding maintenance actions and person-specific evacuation arrangements.
topics.evidence: Safety checks, servicing, maintenance log and evacuation plans
topics.local_test: Walk the premises and trace sampled safety or maintenance exceptions to verification.
topics.success_outcome: Identified hazards receive appropriate follow-up and checks reflect actual conditions.

topics.name: Welsh language & culture
topics.actions: Assess the Welsh language active offer and cultural needs proactively, including how preferences are identified and acted upon; do not equate no requests with adequate provision.
topics.evidence: Language preferences, active-offer arrangements and accessible information
topics.local_test: Ask how language preferences are identified and observe the active offer in practice.
topics.success_outcome: People can access the agreed language and cultural support, not merely a recorded preference.

topics.name: Meaningful activity & community
topics.actions: Review opportunities for personally meaningful activity, relationships and community participation, using resident outcomes rather than activity counts alone.
topics.evidence: Resident goals, participation records and feedback

positive.name: Five Oaks
positive.text: Stimulating activities and good relationships with care staff help to support people’s emotional health.

topics.local_test: Discuss meaningful goals with residents and compare participation records with experience.
topics.success_outcome: People describe opportunities that matter to them and feedback shapes future support.

source_index.name: Five Oaks
source_index.summary_kind: Theme-based extracts - official summary blank or absent
source_index.summary:
Well-being: People can do things that matter to them and that they enjoy. Care workers build relationships with people by spending time with them, seeking their views and preferences on an ongoing basis.

Care and Support: People appear content. Staff are kind and caring and provide individual support detailed in personal plans.

Environment: The environment helps to support people to achieve their personal outcomes. The service is located over two sites close to one another.

Leadership and Management: People are provided with accurate information about the service. There is a statement of purpose (SOP) which describes how the service is provided.

topics.success_outcome: Plans are usable and consistent with the support people actually receive.

topics.name: Staffing & recruitment

positive.name: Walker Road
positive.text: Care staff are recruited safely with pre- employment checks completed correctly.

topics.local_test: Compare recent rotas and induction checks with actual support needs and continuity.
topics.success_outcome: The agreed staffing arrangements work in observed practice; identified gaps receive follow-up.

positive.name: Walker Road
positive.text: Care staff receive appropriate training to undertake their roles and feel well supported working at the service.

actions.name: Walker Road
actions.text: The provider does not record or document dates of when staff supervisions takes place.

topics.local_test: Ask staff to demonstrate a role-relevant skill and compare supervision evidence.

topics.name: Leadership & quality assurance

positive.text: There are good cleaning processes in place and the home smells fresh and clean.

source_index.name: Walker Road
source_index.summary:
People are happy living at Walker Road and have good relationships with the care staff who
support them. People are supported to live their lives in their preferred way and do the
things that matter to them. Care staff encourage people to be as independent as they can
be and to make their own choices where possible. Care staff understand the needs of the
people they care for and do so with kindness and compassion. Care documentation is
thorough, robust and clearly outlines how people should be supported. Personal plans of
care are reviewed regularly to ensure they remain accurate. Medication administration
processes are safe and people have access to health professionals when required.
People live in a suitable environment that is safe and meets their needs. People have their
own bedrooms which offer personal space and privacy.
The Responsible individual (RI) is also the manager of the service and has excellent
oversight of the service. Quality assurance monitoring takes place regularly. Care staff
personnel files contain all required information and care staff receive a formal supervision
regularly. Care staff receive appropriate training and feel well supported working at Walker
Road.
