 and works alongside the manager, who is suitably registered with Social Care Wales (SCW).
 People’s wellbeing outcomes are good. Individuals feel listened to and involved in decisions
 relating to their care and support. There are sufficient care staff to provide assistance with suitable
 arrangements in place to cover any staffing shortfalls. People receive good care and support from a
 friendly staff team. Care staff receive training to ensure they can meet people’s needs effectively.
 Care documentation needs improvement to more accurately reflect the care and health needs of
 the people living in the home. People benefit from living in a pleasant, good environment that is
 clean, safe, and well maintained. Infection prevention and control measures are in place and
 implemented appropriately, reducing the risk of cross-infection within the home. People are happy
 with the care they receive and speak positively about the service and the kindness of the care staff.

source_index.name: Ty Nant Care Home
source_index.summary:
People have excellent well-being in Ty Nant. They have a voice, are listened too and influence
 decisions within the service. There is a wide range of activities available for people to engage in.
 People have built positive and valued friendships with others and staff in the service. Feedback
 from people and relatives is overwhelmingly positive.

 People receive good care and support in the service. Personal plans reflect the needs of people
 well and are up to date with their current needs. People and relatives told us they are aware of the
 content of personal plans and feel they reflect their needs well. Relatives told us communication in
 the service is very good and reliable and the care provided is ‘top notch’

 The environment is well thought out. Bedrooms are personalised and homely. There is ongoing
 investment in the service with refurbishment works carried out as needed. Furniture and all areas of
 the service are in good state of repair. There are several communal areas for people to choose
 where to spend their time.

 Leadership and management is good. Care staff are happy in their roles, supported and trained
 well. Many staff have been employed in the service for years. There is a dedicated manager in the
 service who is visible and approachable. Oversight tools are in place to support the smooth running
 of the service. The RI is accessible with scheduled visits due to take place imminently.

source_index.name: Walshaw House
source_index.summary:
People experience good well-being outcomes; they are treated with dignity and respect and have
 activities available to them. People are supported to stay as healthy as possible, with systems in
 place to protect people in an environment that meets their needs. People are treated as individuals
 and can live their lives how they wish.

 Care and support are good. Detailed care documentation is in place to support people’s needs. The
 service has good systems to safeguard people, and good systems to reduce the risk of the spread
 of infection. Care staff treat people with kindness and compassion. Personal plans are an accurate
 reflection of the individual and people receive appropriate care and support.

 The environment is good and meets people’s needs and outcomes, enhances their well-being, and
 is safe. Walshaw House is well decorated throughout and has enough communal space. People’s
 rooms, as well as communal areas, are kept clean and free from hazards. People can personalise
their rooms if they wish. Significant investment in the environment is evident.

The leadership and management of Walshaw House is good. There is a management team in
place who have good oversight of the service. They ensure the required staff recruitment, training,
and support is undertaken and enable good-quality support and facilities to be provided. Care staff
told us they are happy working at the service.

source_index.name: WAM Care Homes Ltd.
source_index.summary:
Ty Mair is a nursing home on the outskirts of Llanelli.

 Well-being is rated as good because people receive a service that is person centred and enables
 them to live as well as possible. People have developed positive relationships with staff at the
 service.

 Care and support is rated as good because people receive care and support from a team of friendly
 care workers. Care workers are guided by individualised personal plans that enable them to meet
 people’s needs.

 The environment is rated as good because people are safe and comfortable throughout the home.
 The provider is working on actions to improve the building to positively impact people’s well-being.

 Leadership and management is rated as good because the provider has good oversight of the
 service. The service has been working closely with associated health and social care professionals
 to ensure people receive good quality.

reports.title: April 2026 publication-month manager learning report
narrative: The fixed cohort contains 56 homes across 16 authorities; 56 latest archived reports provide 497 source PDF pages.
56 reports have official CIW summaries and 0 have explicitly labelled theme extracts. 0 cohort homes have no archived report.
56 homes have at least one published theme rating and 0 have none. The four theme distributions retain missing values and use the full cohort denominator.
Published tables contain 11 specific rows: 0 Priority action and 11 Area for improvement. 0 rows are Achieved; 11 have unknown status.
1 specific action rows have no topic assignment and remain included in the whole-cohort row totals; topic charts must not be treated as a complete action inventory.
All 3,135 extracted finding rows and 336 sections inform the evidence map. Positive and Improvement wording counts are separate overlapping search-label cohorts.

topics.name: Medicines management
topics.actions: Audit medicine administration records, storage, reconciliation, PRN protocols and staff competency; document exceptions and follow-up.
topics.evidence: MAR audit, competency records, storage checks and documented corrective actions

positive.name: Brynawel House Alcohol and Drug Rehabilitation Centre Ltd
positive.text: The service has a robust risk assessment process and medication management policy in place, with the nursing team providing appropriate oversight to ensure medicines are managed safely and in line with individual risk assessments.

positive.name: Pool Cottage
positive.text: We rated Care & Support as Good, because staff are kind and responsive, support is based on people’s plans, and people are helped to access health services and manage medicines safely.

positive.name: Arrow House
positive.text: Overall, effective care staffing arrangements, training, medication management and environmental systems support people to receive safe, consistent and person-centred care.

negative.name: Neyland House Care Home
negative.text: When observing one person’s medication being given to them, we saw the tablets had been prepared earlier but we were told this was because the person was not ready for the tablets at that time.

negative.name: Glamorgan Care Ltd, Danygraig House
negative.text: However, improvements are needed in the recording of the effects of ‘as required’ (PRN) medication, as this was not always completed consistently.

negative.name: Capel Grange Care Home
negative.text: Medication practices were not considered as part of this inspection.

topics.local_test: Sample administration records against actual staff practice with the medicines lead.
topics.success_outcome: Exceptions are detected, followed up and checked; staff demonstrate the agreed local procedure.

topics.name: Safeguarding & incident learning
topics.actions: Review safeguarding escalation, incident reporting and CIW notifications. Check that staff understand local procedures and that learning reaches the team.
topics.evidence: Escalation log, training records, incident reviews and notifications

positive.name: Woodside House Residential Home
positive.text: The inspection findings support this, noting robust safeguarding arrangements, staff awareness of reporting responsibilities, and a secure environment where risks are identified and managed effectively.

positive.name: Martello House
positive.text: Staff feedback indicates a strong understanding of safeguarding, complaints, and whistleblowing processes, and people using the service consistently report feeling safe, respected, and well supported.

positive.name: Arrow House
positive.text: The service works in partnership with professionals, families and others involved, with safeguarding, health and safety, and effective care staff support integral to care delivery.

topics.local_test: Walk through a local escalation scenario and trace a recent incident review.
topics.success_outcome: Staff explain escalation confidently and can show how incident learning changed practice.

topics.name: Personal plans & risk assessment
topics.actions: Sample personal plans for individual preferences, changing needs, review dates and usable risk controls. Check that staff can apply the guidance in practice.
topics.evidence: Plan reviews, resident involvement and observed practice

positive.name: Martello House
positive.text: Personal plans include good quality “about me” information, clear outcomes, and detailed accounts of what matters to each person, demonstrating active involvement in their assessment and care.

positive.name: Brynawel House Alcohol and Drug Rehabilitation Centre Ltd
positive.text: The service has a robust risk assessment process and medication management policy in place, with the nursing team providing appropriate oversight to ensure medicines are managed safely and in line with individual risk assessments.

positive.name: Wepre Villa Homes Ltd
positive.text: The service provider has developed highly personalised care planning documentation and with this they are able to ensure a good level of care and support is consistently delivered.

negative.name: Gibraltar House
negative.text: People’s personal history, cultural identity, protected characteristics, and significant relationships are usually captured within assessments, but this information is not always carried through into care plans.

negative.name: Penrhos Care Home Ltd
negative.text: While personal plans are generally detailed and informative, we found that some require improvement to ensure people’s health needs and associated risks are clearly defined.

negative.name: Glasallt Fawr Care Home
negative.text: Improvements are required in relation to care planning and risk management, as key documents are not always aligned and do not always consider current needs and outcomes.

actions.name: Gibraltar House
actions.text: People cannot be sure that care workers understand the support required to help them achieve their personal outcomes because care plans do not always contain sufficient/consistent information.

actions.name: Glasallt Fawr Care Home
actions.text: People may not consistently receive care and support in line with their assessed needs, personal outcomes and preferences because personal plans and risk assessments lack sufficient detail, are not up to date, clear, or aligned.

actions.name: Moorland Home
actions.text: The service provider must ensure people receive care and support in line with their personal plans and that this is accurately and consistently recorded.

actions.name: Glamorgan Care Ltd, Danygraig House
actions.text: We identified a risk to people's health and safety due to a breach of regulation 21(2). Support plans and risk assessments must contain accurate up to date information so that staff can provide appropriate care and support. In addition systems for monitoring food/fluid intake need to be suitably robust and completed consistently.

topics.local_test: Compare sampled plans with current preferences, changing needs and observed care.
topics.success_outcome: Plans are usable and consistent with the support people actually receive.

topics.name: Staffing & recruitment
topics.actions: Review staffing against actual dependency and safe recruitment checks. Examine continuity, induction and the impact of vacancies or agency use.
topics.evidence: Dependency reviews, rota analysis and recruitment checks

positive.name: Pen Y Fai House
positive.text: Care staff receive thorough and relevant training, recruitment practices are robust, and the service is underpinned by strong governance arrangements that promote effective oversight and smooth day-to-day operation.

positive.name: Cartref Celtaidd
positive.text: Leadership and management at Cartref Celtaidd remain consistently strong, with clear evidence of effective oversight, stable staffing, and a culture that promotes positive outcomes for people.

positive.name: Martello House
positive.text: The environment is secure and there are robust procedures in place to ensure staff are recruited and vetted safely and are suitably trained to carry out their roles effectively.

actions.name: Ty Cila
actions.text: Gaps in supervision, appraisal, and training compliance increase the risk that staff lack the support, oversight, and skills needed to deliver safe and effective care. Ongoing staffing pressures mean staff feel that their ability to deliver care and wellbeing outcomes to a high standard are being impacted, which could increase the risk of unmet needs and poorer outcomes for individuals in the future.

topics.local_test: Compare recent rotas and induction checks with actual support needs and continuity.
topics.success_outcome: The agreed staffing arrangements work in observed practice; identified gaps receive follow-up.

positive.name: Cilymaenllwyd care home
positive.text: Feedback included “Training is good, management is very supportive, it’s a very good place to work”, “Good working atmosphere and motivating management” and “team are friendly and welcoming, and all give 100% in their job roles”.

actions.name: Emral House Nursing Home

positive.name: Rhiwlas Care Home
positive.text: They have warm interactions with care staff who now have a good understanding of the importance of respecting people's privacy and dignity, and it is clear this culture is being embedded across the service.

positive.name: Rhosyn Melyn
positive.text: Staff actively support positive risk taking so individuals can live as independently as possible, and a diverse programme of meaningful, well planned activities helps keep people stimulated and engaged.

topics.success_outcome: People's choices are respected in practice and applicable decision records remain coherent.

actions.title: Test the local medicines management control
actions.why: 51 of 56 archived reports mention this topic; 0 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Audit medicine administration records, storage, reconciliation, PRN protocols and staff competency; document exceptions and follow-up.
actions.assurance_evidence: MAR audit, competency records, storage checks and documented corrective actions
actions.local_test: Sample administration records against actual staff practice with the medicines lead.
actions.success_outcome: Exceptions are detected, followed up and checked; staff demonstrate the agreed local procedure.

actions.title: Test the local safeguarding & incident learning control

limitations: This is a fixed all-data period cohort, not a dashboard-filter cohort. Only each service's latest archived report is included; this is not the complete historical inspection series or a trend in care quality. Early empty periods must not be interpreted as an absence of historical inspections: earlier reports are outside this latest-only archive.

Monthly membership uses reportPublishedActualDate, not the inspection visit or report issue date. Visit start/end, issue and publication are distinct. Empty months mean no latest archived report was published in that month, not that CIW did no inspections.

Ratings are the exact four published directory-snapshot theme values. Their effective dates are not independently auditable and cannot be assumed to match the historical publication month. Missing ratings and missing reports are not evidence of poor care. No overall quality score is calculated.

Positive wording and Improvement wording are automated search labels, not independent CIW findings. Topic counts mean reports mentioning a topic, not failures; topics and evidence sets overlap and must not be added together.

Published action-table rows can be historical or Achieved. New and Reviewed describe status words published in the source, not validation today. Missing status means unknown, not unresolved. Category counts are not counts of current failures or confirmed enforcement notices.

Excerpts and official summaries retain extracted wording and PDF page provenance. Layout changes and damaged characters can occur; the archived PDF is authoritative. Representative examples are not an exhaustive account or a prevalence estimate.
Public latest-report URLs can change after this snapshot. Use the linked local archived PDF to verify the captured evidence; the external source link establishes its CIW origin.

Management controls and the illustrative learning workflow are assistant-suggested local learning prompts, not CIW requirements, legal advice, clinical advice or an accreditation assessment. Validate applicability with appropriate local leads.

CareLens Cymru is independent and not an official CIW product.
