positive.text: People live in an environment with highly effective and well-maintained facilities and equipment to help them achieve their well-being outcomes whilst identifying, mitigating and reducing health and safety risks.

positive.name: Calon Celtaidd
positive.text: Overall, the service provides safe, responsive and person-centred care, supported by a stable and confident staff team, with clear strengths in wellbeing and leadership, and a good environment for people to live in.

positive.name: Aston Hall Care Limited
positive.text: Relatives provided positive feedback about the cleanliness of the home and the overall environment, and inspectors observed that communal areas, bedrooms and bathrooms were tidy and well cared for.

negative.name: The Ivy
negative.text: Health and safety monitoring systems were in place, but these were not sufficiently robust to reliably identify, prioritise and address environmental issues that could affect people’s well-being.

negative.name: Glenmore Residential Home
negative.text: Staff also told us they had requested modern mobility equipment, such as a steady to support safe transfers; however, this request was not supported or approved by management, further limiting people’s safety and independence.

negative.name: The Willows
negative.text: We observed that changes to routine and the environment affected one person’s ability to feel at ease and in control, indicating that individual needs and known triggers were not sufficiently embedded into day-to-day practice.

actions.name: Bellavista Care Cardiff Limited
actions.text: People are living in an environment that is not kept maintained and there are hazards that will pose a significant risk to people.

actions.name: Parade House Residential Home
actions.text: People cannot be assured risks to their health and safety are regularly assessed and reduced as far as reasonable practicable.

actions.name: Castle View
actions.text: Employee fire safety training must be suitable and sufficient to safeguard people living, working and visiting the service.

actions.name: Wentworth Lodge
actions.text: Governance and auditing systems are not sufficiently effective in identifying weaknesses in care planning, risk management and environmental safety. This increases the risk that concerns are not always identified or acted upon promptly and limits opportunities to prevent harm and ensure consistent care.

actions.name: The Ivy
actions.text: The environment requires improvement because it is not currently suitable or fully equipped to meet the needs of the people using the service. The provider must ensure the environment is safe, well‑maintained, and fit for purpose so that people can experience care and support in surroundings that promote their well‑being and independence.

topics.local_test: Walk the premises and trace sampled safety or maintenance exceptions to verification.
topics.success_outcome: Identified hazards receive appropriate follow-up and checks reflect actual conditions.

topics.name: Welsh language & culture
topics.actions: Assess the Welsh language active offer and cultural needs proactively, including how preferences are identified and acted upon; do not equate no requests with adequate provision.
topics.evidence: Language preferences, active-offer arrangements and accessible information

positive.name: Pen Y Bryn Care Home
positive.text: These plans support staff to deliver good quality care that respects people’s wishes, including cultural and language preferences such as Welsh language provision.

positive.name: Llys Herbert
positive.text: The Deputy Manager spoke positively about learning Welsh and integrating Welsh language and culture into everyday life within the service.

topics.local_test: Ask how language preferences are identified and observe the active offer in practice.
topics.success_outcome: People can access the agreed language and cultural support, not merely a recorded preference.

topics.name: Meaningful activity & community
topics.actions: Review opportunities for personally meaningful activity, relationships and community participation, using resident outcomes rather than activity counts alone.
topics.evidence: Resident goals, participation records and feedback

positive.name: Romilly Nursing Home
positive.text: One relative shared, “They decorated the home and we were able to have mum’s 90th birthday party here.” Another person told us, “The carers take me to the park,” highlighting positive access to the community.

positive.name: Wentworth Lodge
positive.text: Students studying health and social care from local colleges spend meaningful time with people, supporting social connection and emotional well-being while contributing positively to practice-based learning.

positive.name: Calon Celtaidd
positive.text: Ratings: Wellbeing is good because people experience positive wellbeing outcomes, with strong evidence of person-centred care, meaningful activity, and support to maintain relationships and community links.

negative.name: Glenmore Residential Home
negative.text: However, people are not always supported to exercise choice, maintain independence or take part in meaningful activities.

actions.name: Parade House Residential Home
actions.text: People cannot be assured there is effective day to day leadership of the service, in the absence of a manager registered with Social Care Wales. People cannot be assured of the arrangements for managing a complaint submitted to the service. People of what processes will be undertaken following the submission of a complaint.

actions.name: The Ivy
actions.text: Outcomes for people require improvement because staffing pressures have reduced people's access to meaningful engagement and activities. People’s choices have been restricted, and care provided has not consistently aligned with their personal outcomes. Care documentation needs be streamlined and updated, to guide staff and fully involve people or their representatives in decisions about their care.

topics.local_test: Discuss meaningful goals with residents and compare participation records with experience.
topics.success_outcome: People describe opportunities that matter to them and feedback shapes future support.

actions.title: Test the local medicines management control
actions.why: 47 of 51 archived reports mention this topic; 0 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Audit medicine administration records, storage, reconciliation, PRN protocols and staff competency; document exceptions and follow-up.
actions.assurance_evidence: MAR audit, competency records, storage checks and documented corrective actions
actions.local_test: Sample administration records against actual staff practice with the medicines lead.
actions.success_outcome: Exceptions are detected, followed up and checked; staff demonstrate the agreed local procedure.

actions.title: Test the local safeguarding & incident learning control
actions.why: 47 of 51 archived reports mention this topic; 2 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review safeguarding escalation, incident reporting and CIW notifications. Check that staff understand local procedures and that learning reaches the team.
actions.assurance_evidence: Escalation log, training records, incident reviews and notifications
actions.local_test: Walk through a local escalation scenario and trace a recent incident review.
actions.success_outcome: Staff explain escalation confidently and can show how incident learning changed practice.

actions.title: Test the local personal plans & risk assessment control
actions.why: 50 of 51 archived reports mention this topic; 7 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Sample personal plans for individual preferences, changing needs, review dates and usable risk controls. Check that staff can apply the guidance in practice.
actions.assurance_evidence: Plan reviews, resident involvement and observed practice
actions.local_test: Compare sampled plans with current preferences, changing needs and observed care.
actions.success_outcome: Plans are usable and consistent with the support people actually receive.

actions.title: Test the local staffing & recruitment control
actions.why: 50 of 51 archived reports mention this topic; 1 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review staffing against actual dependency and safe recruitment checks. Examine continuity, induction and the impact of vacancies or agency use.
actions.assurance_evidence: Dependency reviews, rota analysis and recruitment checks
actions.local_test: Compare recent rotas and induction checks with actual support needs and continuity.
actions.success_outcome: The agreed staffing arrangements work in observed practice; identified gaps receive follow-up.

actions.title: Test the local training & supervision control
actions.why: 51 of 51 archived reports mention this topic; 3 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Reconcile the training matrix with current roles and residents' needs. Sample supervision records and assess competence, rather than attendance alone.
actions.assurance_evidence: Training matrix, competency assessment and supervision records
actions.local_test: Ask staff to demonstrate a role-relevant skill and compare supervision evidence.
actions.success_outcome: Competence is demonstrated in practice rather than inferred from attendance records alone.

actions.title: Test the local leadership & quality assurance control
actions.why: 51 of 51 archived reports mention this topic; 10 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review responsible-individual oversight and quality reviews. Track audit actions to closure and show how resident and relative feedback changes the service.
actions.assurance_evidence: RI visit records, quality reports, feedback and closed action log
actions.local_test: Trace an audit exception and resident feedback through ownership, action and recheck.
actions.success_outcome: Oversight detects gaps and verifies improvements with records, observation and resident feedback.

actions.title: Test the local rights, choice & independence control
actions.why: 50 of 51 archived reports mention this topic; 4 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Check consent and decision-making records, legal authorisations where applicable, and how daily practice supports choice, dignity and independence.
actions.assurance_evidence: Decision records, authorisations and resident-led goals
actions.local_test: Observe daily choices and compare decision records with what people describe.
actions.success_outcome: People's choices are respected in practice and applicable decision records remain coherent.

actions.title: Test the local nutrition & hydration control
actions.why: 45 of 51 archived reports mention this topic; 0 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review nutritional and hydration risks, weight trends, meal preferences and escalation when needs change; assess the dining experience with residents.
actions.assurance_evidence: Risk screening, monitoring, referrals and resident feedback
actions.local_test: Observe a meal and compare preferences, monitoring records and escalation arrangements.
actions.success_outcome: People describe a suitable dining experience and changing needs receive documented follow-up.

actions.title: Test the local infection prevention control
actions.why: 47 of 51 archived reports mention this topic; 0 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Check infection-control practice, cleaning assurance and staff competence. Follow up audit exceptions and verify that practical supplies and routines are effective.
actions.assurance_evidence: IPC audit, cleaning checks and competency records
actions.local_test: Observe agreed cleaning and hygiene routines alongside the local audit evidence.
actions.success_outcome: Routines work in practice and audit exceptions are corrected and rechecked.

limitations: This is a fixed all-data period cohort, not a dashboard-filter cohort. Only each service's latest archived report is included; this is not the complete historical inspection series or a trend in care quality. Early empty periods must not be interpreted as an absence of historical inspections: earlier reports are outside this latest-only archive.

Monthly membership uses reportPublishedActualDate, not the inspection visit or report issue date. Visit start/end, issue and publication are distinct. Empty months mean no latest archived report was published in that month, not that CIW did no inspections.

Ratings are the exact four published directory-snapshot theme values. Their effective dates are not independently auditable and cannot be assumed to match the historical publication month. Missing ratings and missing reports are not evidence of poor care. No overall quality score is calculated.

Positive wording and Improvement wording are automated search labels, not independent CIW findings. Topic counts mean reports mentioning a topic, not failures; topics and evidence sets overlap and must not be added together.

Published action-table rows can be historical or Achieved. New and Reviewed describe status words published in the source, not validation today. Missing status means unknown, not unresolved. Category counts are not counts of current failures or confirmed enforcement notices.

Excerpts and official summaries retain extracted wording and PDF page provenance. Layout changes and damaged characters can occur; the archived PDF is authoritative. Representative examples are not an exhaustive account or a prevalence estimate.
Public latest-report URLs can change after this snapshot. Use the linked local archived PDF to verify the captured evidence; the external source link establishes its CIW origin.

Management controls and the illustrative learning workflow are assistant-suggested local learning prompts, not CIW requirements, legal advice, clinical advice or an accreditation assessment. Validate applicability with appropriate local leads.

CareLens Cymru is independent and not an official CIW product.
