development arrangements can be strengthened further, but these areas do not outweigh the
significant, sustained and measurable positive outcomes we saw for people.

source_index.name: Pant Yr Odyn
source_index.summary:
Pant Y Odyn is a welcoming care home providing accommodation and personal support for adults
 with a range of support needs. It is set in a rural village a short distance from Ammanford. The
 home offers a calm, nurturing environment where people feel valued, supported, and able to live
 meaningful, positive lives. The atmosphere is warm and inclusive, and people are encouraged to
 grow in confidence, develop their independence, and enjoy fulfilling daily experiences.

 The well-being outcomes of people is excellent as they receive highly personalised care and
 support to live fulfilled lives doing things that matter to them.

 The care and support people receive is good delivered by a dedicated and skilled care staff team
 who know people well.

 The environment of which people live is excellent providing safe, comfortable, and homely spaces
that reflect people’s individuality and promote a strong sense of belonging.

The leadership and management of the service is excellent as managers promote a strong positive
culture that is supportive, inclusive and respectful.

source_index.name: Pantanas Care Centre
source_index.summary:
Pantanas Care Centre provides care and support to individuals over the age of 18 with general
 nursing, physical, mental health, and dementia needs. It is spread over 2 floors and set in its own
 private grounds in the small mining town of Treharris. It has good transport links to Cardiff and
 Merthyr and close to local amenities.

 The service provides good care and support in a warm and friendly environment, that promotes
 good wellbeing outcomes for people living at the service. Staff know people well and interact in a
 kind and caring manner. Care files detail how people like their needs met and are reviewed
 regularly. People carry out activities and daily living tasks with the support of staff to ensure their
 physical and emotional well-being. The environment is good. The premises is safe and accessible
 and has suitable indoor and outdoor areas for people to use. Most staff feel well supported, happy,
 and confident in their roles. They receive regular supervision and a variety of training, and policies
 are in place to provide guidance. Quality Assurance systems are in place with regular internal and
external auditing and good oversight by the management team. The Responsible Individual (RI)
visits the service regularly and speaks to people and staff.

source_index.name: Plas Pengwaith
source_index.provider: Gwynedd Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Plas Pengwaith is in the heart of Llanberis, people are close to amenities, local events, and
 enjoyable scenery.

 The well-being rating for the home is good. The service offers people a strong active Welsh offer
 with all staff speaking Welsh. People remain a part of the local community and have support to be
 as independent as they are able. Daily choices are given to people regarding their care and their
 preferences are respected.

 Care and support at Plas Pengwaith is good. People benefit from a stable staff group who know
 their needs well and enable continuity in their care. People are treated with dignity and respect and
 told us they are happy with their care.
The environment in the home is good. The home has a continued maintenance programme to
ensure people have a comfortable home. People are happy with their bedrooms and the facilities.

Leadership and management for the service are good. The manager is visible and approachable
and staff feel well supported. The responsible individual (RI) visits the home and produces quality
reports regarding the service in line with legislation.

source_index.name: Plas y Dderwen Care Home
source_index.summary:
People who have made Plas y Dderwen their home receive an excellent standard of care.
 Everyone we spoke with and had feedback from, have high levels of confidence in the service and
 feel their decision to use it was the best one for the individuals involved.

 Wellbeing is rated as excellent because of the relationships people, and those important to them,
 have with the whole staff team. This, together with the opportunities to do things that are important
 to them and that they enjoy, mean they are treated with dignity and respect and their voices are
 heard.

 Care and support is excellent because the team is led by a highly effective manager who has set
 and embedded the values for the service. The team is well trained and motivated to offer people
 quality care in line with their individualised and person-centred plans.
The environment is excellent because the service is maintained to a very high standard with
options for people to spend time in a range of areas both inside and in the garden areas. Due
regard is shown to make sure the environment is safe and free of any hazards whilst remaining as
homely as possible.

Leadership and management is rated as excellent because people have high levels of confidence
in the service. The culture and values are practiced by a staff team who are committed to quality
and seek ways to enhance people’s lives further.

source_index.name: Priory Mount Eveswell
source_index.summary:
Priory Mount Eveswell is situated on the east side of Newport on an elevated site, providing
 panoramic views of the city and beyond. The service provides specialist nursing and rehabilitation
 support for people with acquired brain injuries, neurological conditions, and complex care needs.


 People’s well-being and the care and support they receive are both rated as good. People are
 treated with dignity, kindness and respect, and are supported to make choices about their care and
 wellbeing. The service has strengthened its focus on personal outcomes. Effective assessment,
 care planning, review processes and strong clinical oversight support positive health and wellbeing
 outcomes.

 The environment people live in, as well as the leadership and management of the service, are also
 both rated as good. People live in a safe and well-looked-after setting that supports their wellbeing
 while helping them feel secure. The service is well managed, with effective systems in place to
 check quality and make improvements. Staff are safely recruited, well supported, receive training,
 and understand the needs of the people they care for.

source_index.name: Queens Care Home
source_index.summary:
Well being is excellent because people are fully involved in decisions and supported to live the lives
 they choose. Positive risk management allows individuals to follow their interests safely.
 Relationships, community involvement and identity are respected, and people feel safe, listened to
 and confident in their home and the support they receive.

 Care and support is excellent because care is carefully planned and consistently delivered to meet
 people’s individual needs. Assessments and transitions are well managed, ensuring continuity.
 Systems for safeguarding, medication and health monitoring are well embedded, enabling a
 coordinated approach that keeps people safe while supporting their day-to-day stability and
 wellbeing.

 The environment is excellent because it is highly personalised and well maintained, supporting
 people to live comfortably and independently. People are actively involved in shaping their
surroundings, with opportunities to share ideas and influence how their home is organised. Spaces
are safe, welcoming and used in ways that encourage engagement, choice and a strong sense of
ownership.

Leadership and management is good because effective governance, strong oversight and regular
audits drive continuous improvement. Clear leadership is supported by a positive culture,
knowledgeable staff and robust training. Feedback is valued and informs development, although
some policies and quality reports require further strengthening to fully align with Welsh legislation.

source_index.name: Rhoslan Care Home
source_index.summary:
Rhoslan is a residential care service providing care and support for people aged 18 and over.
 Based in the seaside town of Rhos-on-Sea, the service is close to local amenities and the beach.

 People experience excellent wellbeing outcomes because the service places people's health,
 wellbeing, and quality of life at the centre of daily practice. Staff know people well and support them
 to maintain their independence, make choices and participate in meaningful activities, which reflect
 their interests and preferences.

 Care and support are excellent because staff provide tailored, person-centred care which responds
 to people's individual needs. Personal plans accurately reflect people's wishes, strengths and
 desired outcomes.

 The environment is excellent because it is welcoming and comfortable. The home is thoughtfully
 designed, accessible and maintained to a very high standard, providing people with a safe,
 pleasant and homely place to live.

 Leadership and management are good because leaders provide strong and effective direction
 which promotes a positive culture throughout the service. Effective governance arrangements help
 maintain consistently high standards of care and drive continuous improvement for people living at
the home.

source_index.name: Rickeston Mill Care Home
source_index.summary:
Overall, people experience positive outcomes for their well-being. Many people are engaged in
 meaningful activities and social interactions that support their emotional health and quality of life. A
 varied activity programme, including group activities and community outings, helps people remain
 active and connected. Staff promote relationships with family and friends, and the environment,
 including improved outdoor spaces, supports comfort, independence and engagement.

 Most people receive good care and support from kind and respectful staff. Feedback from families,
 professionals and staff is largely positive, and there are examples of person-centred care planning
 and safe medication practices. However, improvements are needed to ensure consistency. Care is
 not always delivered in line with personal plans, and care records are not always complete. This
 means the service cannot always demonstrate that care is consistently delivered or that risks are
 fully managed.

 Leadership and management show a clear commitment to improvement. Governance systems,
 including audits and reviews, have strengthened and are identifying areas for development. Staff
report improved culture and better working relationships. However, some aspects, such as
supervision, require further consistency.

source_index.name: Rose Cottage
source_index.summary:
Rose Cottage provides care and support to five individuals. Support is provided to people who may
 have learning disabilities or mental health requirements.

 The management team consist of the Responsible Individual (RI), the manager, and deputy
 manager. The team is very established and some have been providing support to people living at
 Rose Cottage for many years. This means they know people well. The team strive to ensure people
 achieve excellent well-being and experience meaningful and personal achievements. People are
 supported to do what is important to them, be a part of their community and lead a healthy and
 happy life. Good care and support is provided in a person centred, postive risk taking way whilst
 ensuring people are safeguarded and have a voice. Reviews are completed quarterly or sooner if
 any changes occur and families/representatives feel involved and are kept informed.

 The environment in Rose Cottage is person centred, representative of what is important to people
 and very homely. Risk assessments and routine checks take place with planned maintenance work
 where required.

 Staff feel supported by the Responsible Individual (RI), manager and deputy manager. Good
 recruitment processes are in place with subsequent training and individual supervision provided.
 Good oversight ensures a service that strives to go from strength to strength.

source_index.name: Tegfan
source_index.summary:
Tegfan is an adult care home that supports people with complex needs to live as independently
 and meaningfully as possible. Since the previous inspection, we found significant improvements
 across the service. Particularly in relation to people's well-being, opportunities for meaningful
 activities, communication with families and the overall culture of the service.

 Well-being is rated Good. People benefit from positive relationships with care staff who know them
 well and understand their individual needs and preferences. People are supported to access
 meaningful activities, maintain important relationships and participate in their local communities.
 Relatives and professionals consistently described improvements in people's quality of life,
 engagement and overall happiness.

 Care and Support is rated Good. People receive person-centred care from staff who understand
 their needs and work closely with families and external professionals. Personal plans are detailed,
 regularly reviewed and support people to achieve their personal outcomes. Whilst some
 improvements are required to ensure daily recordings consistently evidence care delivered and
outcomes achieved; people continue to receive care that reflects their assessed needs and
preferences.

Leadership and Management is rated Good. Leadership has driven positive change across the
service and created a more person-centred culture. Staff, relatives and professionals spoke
positively about improvements in communication, management visibility and partnership working.
Leaders demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement through effective governance; staff
support and quality assurance processes.

Environment is rated Good. People live in a welcoming, personalised and well-maintained
environment that promotes their independence, well-being and safety. The provider continues to
invest in the environment and has taken action to strengthen safety arrangements while further
developing facilities and outdoor spaces to enhance people's experiences.

source_index.name: The Cedars Care Home
source_index.summary:
People experience positive care and support from effective leadership and management team
 overall, but improvements are needed to evidence people’s voice and well-being outcomes are fully
 promoted.

 Well-being is rated as Requires Improvement. People take part in some meaningful activities.
 However, records do not clearly show people’s goals, choices or experiences. In addition, a
 safeguarding investigation was not thorough or in line with the provider’s policy. Improvements are
 needed to ensure the service follows its policies and fully supports people’s well-being and voice.

 Care and support is good. People receive consistent and person-centred care from staff who know
 them well. Personal plans and risk assessments provide clear guidance, and staff support people
 to maintain their health. Some improvements are needed to strengthen reviews and medication
 recording, but outcomes for people remain positive.
The environment is good. The home is clean, welcoming and accessible, with personalised
bedrooms and suitable communal and outdoor spaces. Health and safety checks take place to
ensure the environment is safe for people.

Leadership and management is good. Leaders promote a positive culture and support staff. Staff
are safely recruited, well trained and receive regular supervision, which helps ensure they provide
safe and consistent care.

source_index.name: The Forge Care Centre
source_index.summary:
The Forge Care Centre provides high standards of care and support, including nursing care.
 People at The Forge receive exceptionally detailed, personalised and effective care and support,
 promoting positive outcomes while responding to complex needs.
 People reported feeling safe, loved and valued. Relatives describe the home as welcoming and
 supportive, and evidence demonstrates people’s physical, emotional and social wellbeing is
 promoted to a very high standard.
 The service shows strength in assessment, care planning, dementia care, clinical oversight and
 multidisciplinary working. Support is tailored around individuals, ensuring care is responsive,
 flexible and driven by each person's needs and preferences.
 The environment is safe, clean and meets the needs of people living at the home.
 The Forge Care Centre is well-led, with a highly supportive culture and an experienced workforce
 committed to achieving positive outcomes for people.

source_index.name: The Grange
source_index.summary:
People living at the service experience good outcomes across all four inspection themes. Well-being is
good; people are supported by a caring and responsive staff team who promote dignity, choice and
meaningful engagement. Individuals take part in personalised activities within the home and
community and appear happy and well presented. Relatives spoke positively about the service,
describing it as open, welcoming and focused on people’s comfort and happiness.

Care and support is good; people receive support that meets their needs and promotes their wellbeing.
Staff demonstrate a good understanding of individuals and use effective, compassionate approaches,
including de-escalation where required. Care is safe, person centred and responsive, although care
planning documentation would benefit from further detail to reflect practice.

The environment is good; it is safe, clean and generally well maintained, with effective systems in
place to manage risk, safety checks and infection control. The Responsible Individual has provided a
clear refurbishment plan, and some improvements have already been completed.

Leadership and management is good; there are effective governance and oversight arrangements in
place. Staffing levels are maintained to meet people’s needs, with ongoing effective recruitment. Staff
benefit from regular training and development opportunities, helping to ensure they have the skills and
knowledge needed to ensure safe, person-centred care.

source_index.name: The Laurels Residential Care Ltd
source_index.summary:
The Laurels is a residential care home located in Aberdare, situated within a residential area close
 to the town centre and local amenities.

 Well-being outcomes for people are good. People are treated with dignity and respect and benefit
 from positive, supportive relationships with care staff. People told us they are happy living at the
 service and have access to a range of activities that promote engagement and social inclusion.

 Care and Support requires improvement. Personal plans are in place and provide care staff with an
 overview of people’s care and support needs, as well as associated risks. These plans are
 reviewed regularly and updated when people’s needs change. Care staff demonstrate a good
 understanding of people’s preferences and support requirements. However, improvements are
 needed in medication management arrangements to ensure medicines are stored, managed, and
 administered safely and in line with best practice.

 The environment is good. The home is welcoming and meets people’s needs. People can
 personalise their bedrooms, and communal areas are clean and conducive to social interaction. A
 planned programme of maintenance and repairs is in place to support the ongoing upkeep of the
premises.

Leadership and Management is good. Staff morale is positive, and staff report feeling supported
and valued in their roles. Appropriate recruitment processes are in place to ensure staff are safely
recruited. Staff receive training to enable them to meet the needs of the people they support.
Governance and quality assurance arrangements provide senior staff with appropriate oversight of
service.

source_index.name: The Oaks Respite Services
source_index.summary:
The Oaks Respite Services is based in the Cwmavon area of Port Talbot and provides respite and
 long-term care for people. People receive a highly person-centred service where their well-being,
 independence and aspirations are consistently promoted. People experience excellent well-being
 outcomes and are supported to live safely, happily and with dignity.

 People receive good care and support from a stable, skilled and committed staff team who know
 them exceptionally well. Personal plans are comprehensive and outcome focused, with clear
 involvement from people and those important to them.

 People live in a welcoming and homely environment where they are encouraged to make choices
 and maintain control over their daily lives. Bedrooms are personalised, communal areas are
 comfortable, and the outdoor spaces are spacious and accessible. Robust risk management
 arrangements help keep people safe whilst supporting their independence.

 Leadership and management arrangements are excellent. The responsible individual (RI) and
 registered manager provide effective oversight through comprehensive quality assurance systems,
continuous monitoring and a clear focus on improvement. Staff consistently told us they feel
supported and valued.

source_index.name: The Rookery
source_index.summary:
People experience good well-being outcomes because they have choice and control over their day.
 They decide how to spend their time and benefit from positive, respectful relationships with care
 staff who know them well. Activities are varied and meaningful, promoting social connection and
 emotional well-being. People enjoy nutritious meals and personalised bedrooms that support
 identity and comfort.

 Care staff provide good, reliable and compassionate care. Assessments ensure people’s needs
 can be met, and care staff understand people’s preferences and routines. Care staff interactions
 are warm and respectful, and people are supported in line with their preferences and needs.

 The environment is good, people live in warm, clean accommodation that supports their well-being.
 Communal areas and bedrooms are homely; however, some areas require maintenance and
 improved oversight to ensure safety and accessibility. Systems for fire safety are in place, although
 further work and training are required to ensure full compliance.
Leadership and management are good and effective, supportive, and improvement-focused. Care
staff feel valued and communication is positive. Quality assurance arrangements provide good
oversight.

source_index.name: Towyn Capel Residential Home
source_index.summary:
Towyn Capel Residential Home is in Trearddur Bay close to local amenities and the seaport of
 Holyhead.

 The well-being at Towyn Capel needs improvement. People have not received an updated
 information guide regarding the service after the new provider has purchased the home. People
 benefit from consistent care from care staff who know their needs well and provide activities and
 daily choices for people.

 The care and support in Towyn Capel are good. People receive sensitive care from care staff who
 can anticipate their needs and help them achieve their objectives. People can access health care
 reviews in a timely way. Personal plans are personalised to people’s individual needs and
 preferences.
The environment needs improvement. The basement needs improved storage to comply with
health and safety and fire legislation. The home presents as clean and tidy and people can
personalise their rooms. The kitchen needs further work to comply to food hygiene legislation.

Leadership and management need improvement. This is because an updated Statement of
Purpose document describing the service offered to people has not been provided to people,
commissioners of care and Care Inspectorate Wales (CIW). There is over-sight of the service to
ensure its smooth running.

source_index.name: Trafalgar Park Care Home
source_index.summary:
Trafalgar Park is a care home in Nelson, Caerphilly, providing residential and nursing care. We
 rated Well-being, Care and Support, Environment, and Leadership and Management as Good.

 People told us they feel safe, respected and comfortable, and we observed positive interactions
 promoting dignity, choice and independence. Staff know people well and provide care that
 responds to individual needs, working effectively with healthcare professionals to support positive
 outcomes.

 People live in a clean, welcoming and homely environment that supports their well-being and
 quality of life.

 Effective leadership, governance and quality assurance arrangements help ensure people receive
 safe, person-centred care from a committed and supportive staff team.

 Overall, people experience good outcomes and receive care and support that promotes their well-
 being, dignity and safety.

source_index.name: Ty Camlas
source_index.summary:
Ty Camlas supports up to eight adults aged 18 and over living with complex mental health needs
 and learning disabilities. The service promotes holistic wellbeing and independence across
 Recovery Star domains, including health, daily living, relationships, identity, and resilience. It is in
 Ystradgynlais in Swansea.

 People experience positive wellbeing outcomes through consistent, person-centred support from a
 skilled staff team, which promotes independence, choice and control while upholding individuals’
 rights.

 Care and support is good, with evidence of a focus upon person centred practice. Personal plans
 reflect individual’s needs, preferences and what matters to them, supported by effective risk
 assessments.

 The home environment is warm, clean and homely and supports people’s comfort and
independence. Safety checks are completed and bedrooms are personalised and meet people’s
needs.

Leadership and management is effective with the Responsible Individual (RI) demonstrating clear
oversight and proactively identifying areas of improvement. Staff tell us they feel supported by the
manager and the RI, are suitably trained to do their job and are supported by effective policies and
safeguarding procedures.

source_index.name: Ty Canol
source_index.summary:
Ty Canol is located in Neath and provides personal care and support to people. It is close to a
 number of community facilities which can be easily accessed from the service. During this
 inspection, we found significant improvements have been made since the previous inspection in
 March 2026. Earlier concerns relating to care planning, leadership, care staff support, training
 compliance, and governance have largely been addressed. The service has been rated good in all
 four themes.

 We saw people’s independence consistently promoted and people benefit from person-centred
 care which enables them to make meaningful choices and achieve personal goals.
 Personal plans have improved considerably and are now detailed, regularly reviewed and
 supported by appropriate risk assessments. Daily records are detailed and informative.

 The environment is well-maintained and we saw improvements are planned to further enhance the
 environment for people. Leadership and management have strengthened since the last inspection.
 Supervisions, team meetings and training compliance have improved, and care staff report higher
 morale, better teamwork and increased management support. Quality assurance processes are
focused on wellbeing and service development.

source_index.name: Ty Gwynno
source_index.summary:
Ty Gwynno is a service providing nursing and residential care to older adults, including those who
 live with dementia. The service is located in a residential area to the north of Pontypridd.


 Well-being is excellent because people have exceptional support to achieve personal goals and
 maintain important relationships. A strong culture of inclusion, advocacy and positive risk-taking
 helps people enjoy meaningful experiences and achieve excellent well-being outcomes. Care and
 support is excellent because people receive highly personalised, outcome-focused care which is
 consistently reviewed and delivered by skilled care staff. Robust safeguarding, medication
 management and infection prevention systems help ensure people achieve positive outcomes
 safely. The environment is excellent because the service is thoughtfully designed to enhance well-
 being, independence and quality of life. Innovative facilities, ongoing investment and involvement
 from people help create a warm and homely environment. Leadership and management is
 excellent because strong and visible leaders promote a culture of continuous improvement,
 learning and innovation. Effective governance arrangements, strong staff support and a highly
 skilled workforce help ensure people consistently receive high-quality care and support.

source_index.name: Ty Iscoed
source_index.provider: Caerphilly County Borough Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Ty Iscoed is a 30-bed care home located in Caerphilly County Borough. The service provides
 residential care, including long-term and short-term stays, for people living with dementia. The
 home offers a comfortable environment with communal living areas, accessible outdoor space and
 opportunities for people to maintain links with family, friends and the wider community.

 We found people are treated with kindness and respect by staff who know them well. People are
 supported to make choices about their daily lives and take part in activities that promote their well-
 being. The service maintains positive links with the local community and provides opportunities for
 people to remain socially engaged. People receive care from staff who are committed to meeting
 their needs. Appropriate arrangements are in place to support safeguarding, medication
 management and infection prevention and control. The environment is clean, welcoming and
 supports people's privacy, dignity and independence. Ongoing improvements to the premises
demonstrate a commitment to enhancing people's experience of living at the home.

The manager and responsible individual provide clear direction for the service and have identified
areas for further development. They demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement and
are responsive to feedback.

We identified areas for improvement relating to staff training and supervision. The manager and
responsible individual acknowledged these areas and have started to implement improvements.
We will consider the progress made during the next inspection. Overall, we found positive
outcomes for people and rated all four themes as good.

source_index.name: Ty Mawr
source_index.summary:
Ty Mawr is located in Neath and provides personal care and support to people. It is close to a
 number of community facilities which can be easily accessed from the service. During this
 inspection, we found significant improvements have been made since the previous inspection in
 March 2026. Earlier concerns relating to care planning, leadership, care staff support, training
 compliance, medication management and governance have largely been addressed. The service
 has been rated good in all four themes.

 People participate in meaningful activities, access the community and appear relaxed within a
 personalised and homely environment. Relatives provided positive feedback, describing care staff
 as caring, communicative and person centred. Menus offered choice and information was
 displayed in accessible formats. Personal plans have improved considerably and are now detailed,
 regularly reviewed and supported by appropriate risk assessments. Daily records are detailed and
 informative.

 Leadership and management have strengthened since the last inspection. Supervisions, team
 meetings and training compliance have improved, and care staff reported higher morale, better
teamwork and increased management support. Quality assurance processes are now more
focused on wellbeing and service development.

source_index.name: Ty Nant Care Home
source_index.summary:
Ty Nant is a care home in Williamstown, providing care and support for up to 33 people, including
 those requiring residential or nursing care, with a focus on supporting people living with dementia.

 People’s well-being outcomes are good. The service promotes a strong, person-centred culture
 where individuals are well known by staff and supported to maintain their identity, relationships and
 independence. People appear relaxed, safe and emotionally secure, benefiting from kind,
 respectful interactions and meaningful engagement. Opportunities for activities and community
 involvement support inclusion and reduce isolation, while people’s views are actively sought and
 used to shape the service.

 Care and support are good, with people receiving responsive and effective care from staff who
 understand their needs well. Care planning is detailed and supports safe, consistent delivery. There
 are robust systems in place for safeguarding, medication management and infection prevention
and control, alongside effective partnership working with external professionals to support people’s
health needs.

The environment is good. It is safe, clean and homely, with well-maintained communal and outdoor
spaces that promote both social interaction and independence.

Leadership and management are good. The service benefits from visible and approachable
leadership, a positive staff culture and effective governance systems that support continuous
improvement and good outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Witla Court
source_index.summary:
Witla Court is a care home located in a residential area of Cardiff. The service supports people
 living with learning disabilities, mental health and associated needs.

 People living at Witla Court experience excellent well-being outcomes. We found care staff promote
 independence, and positive risk-taking. Activities are personalised and encourage people to access
 their local communities. People told us they are actively involved in decisions which affect them.

 The standard of care and support is excellent. The provider conducts detailed assessments, paying
 attention to the compatibility of the individuals at the service. People are supported by staff who
 know them well. Personal plans are detailed, accurate and regularly reviewed with people and with
 their multi-disciplinary team.

 The environment is good, safe and supports people’s well-being. Indoor and outdoor areas are
 attractive, personalised and comfortable to suit people’s preferences. People give their opinion on
 their home and this is listened to.
The leadership and management at Witla Court is excellent. The provider priorities staff well-being
and has several initiatives in place such as access to free counselling. Staff told us they feel
supported and management are approachable. The Responsible Individual (RI) completes regular
visits and gathers feedback from people and staff.

source_index.name: Woodcroft
source_index.summary:
Woodcroft Care Home is a large, purpose-built service on the outskirts of Cardiff. The service
 provides accommodation and care for up to 60 people aged 55 and over. It is organised into three
 self-contained communities, offering support for people living with dementia, general residential
 needs and respite care. There is good access to local transport links with local shops within walking
 distance.

 Wellbeing is rated as excellent because people live in a vibrant and inclusive environment where
 they are supported to enjoy life and have positive meaningful experiences. People describe living in
 the service as highly positive, with a strong emphasis placed on activities that bring joy and
 purpose.

 Care and support is rated as good because people receive good quality care from staff who know
 them well and treat them with kindness dignity and respect. Care staff support people to maintain
independence and make choices. People are supported to maintain their identity and interests.

Environment is rated as good because people live in a safe, comfortable, and welcoming
environment which supports their wellbeing.

Leadership and management is rated as excellent because the management team has
successfully created an environment where there are high levels of confidence from residents,
relatives, and care staff, and where continuous improvement is both expected and achieved.

actions.local_test: Compare sampled plans with current preferences, changing needs and observed care.
actions.success_outcome: Plans are usable and consistent with the support people actually receive.

actions.title: Test the local staffing & recruitment control
actions.why: 44 of 48 archived reports mention this topic; 2 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review staffing against actual dependency and safe recruitment checks. Examine continuity, induction and the impact of vacancies or agency use.
actions.assurance_evidence: Dependency reviews, rota analysis and recruitment checks
actions.local_test: Compare recent rotas and induction checks with actual support needs and continuity.
actions.success_outcome: The agreed staffing arrangements work in observed practice; identified gaps receive follow-up.

actions.title: Test the local training & supervision control
actions.why: 48 of 48 archived reports mention this topic; 2 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Reconcile the training matrix with current roles and residents' needs. Sample supervision records and assess competence, rather than attendance alone.
actions.assurance_evidence: Training matrix, competency assessment and supervision records
actions.local_test: Ask staff to demonstrate a role-relevant skill and compare supervision evidence.
actions.success_outcome: Competence is demonstrated in practice rather than inferred from attendance records alone.

actions.title: Test the local leadership & quality assurance control
actions.why: 48 of 48 archived reports mention this topic; 4 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review responsible-individual oversight and quality reviews. Track audit actions to closure and show how resident and relative feedback changes the service.
actions.assurance_evidence: RI visit records, quality reports, feedback and closed action log
actions.local_test: Trace an audit exception and resident feedback through ownership, action and recheck.
actions.success_outcome: Oversight detects gaps and verifies improvements with records, observation and resident feedback.

actions.title: Test the local rights, choice & independence control
actions.why: 47 of 48 archived reports mention this topic; 0 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Check consent and decision-making records, legal authorisations where applicable, and how daily practice supports choice, dignity and independence.
actions.assurance_evidence: Decision records, authorisations and resident-led goals
actions.local_test: Observe daily choices and compare decision records with what people describe.
actions.success_outcome: People's choices are respected in practice and applicable decision records remain coherent.

actions.title: Test the local nutrition & hydration control
actions.why: 40 of 48 archived reports mention this topic; 0 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review nutritional and hydration risks, weight trends, meal preferences and escalation when needs change; assess the dining experience with residents.
actions.assurance_evidence: Risk screening, monitoring, referrals and resident feedback
actions.local_test: Observe a meal and compare preferences, monitoring records and escalation arrangements.
actions.success_outcome: People describe a suitable dining experience and changing needs receive documented follow-up.

actions.title: Test the local infection prevention control
actions.why: 40 of 48 archived reports mention this topic; 0 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Check infection-control practice, cleaning assurance and staff competence. Follow up audit exceptions and verify that practical supplies and routines are effective.
actions.assurance_evidence: IPC audit, cleaning checks and competency records
actions.local_test: Observe agreed cleaning and hygiene routines alongside the local audit evidence.
actions.success_outcome: Routines work in practice and audit exceptions are corrected and rechecked.

actions.title: Test the local environment & fire safety control
actions.why: 48 of 48 archived reports mention this topic; 4 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review fire and premises safety, servicing, accessibility and environmental risks; verify outstanding maintenance actions and person-specific evacuation arrangements.
actions.assurance_evidence: Safety checks, servicing, maintenance log and evacuation plans
actions.local_test: Walk the premises and trace sampled safety or maintenance exceptions to verification.
actions.success_outcome: Identified hazards receive appropriate follow-up and checks reflect actual conditions.

actions.title: Test the local welsh language & culture control
actions.why: 48 of 48 archived reports mention this topic; 0 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Assess the Welsh language active offer and cultural needs proactively, including how preferences are identified and acted upon; do not equate no requests with adequate provision.
actions.assurance_evidence: Language preferences, active-offer arrangements and accessible information
actions.local_test: Ask how language preferences are identified and observe the active offer in practice.
actions.success_outcome: People can access the agreed language and cultural support, not merely a recorded preference.

actions.title: Test the local meaningful activity & community control
actions.why: 48 of 48 archived reports mention this topic; 3 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review opportunities for personally meaningful activity, relationships and community participation, using resident outcomes rather than activity counts alone.
actions.assurance_evidence: Resident goals, participation records and feedback
actions.local_test: Discuss meaningful goals with residents and compare participation records with experience.
actions.success_outcome: People describe opportunities that matter to them and feedback shapes future support.

limitations: This is a fixed all-data period cohort, not a dashboard-filter cohort. Only each service's latest archived report is included; this is not the complete historical inspection series or a trend in care quality. Early empty periods must not be interpreted as an absence of historical inspections: earlier reports are outside this latest-only archive.

Monthly membership uses reportPublishedActualDate, not the inspection visit or report issue date. Visit start/end, issue and publication are distinct. Empty months mean no latest archived report was published in that month, not that CIW did no inspections.

Ratings are the exact four published directory-snapshot theme values. Their effective dates are not independently auditable and cannot be assumed to match the historical publication month. Missing ratings and missing reports are not evidence of poor care. No overall quality score is calculated.

Positive wording and Improvement wording are automated search labels, not independent CIW findings. Topic counts mean reports mentioning a topic, not failures; topics and evidence sets overlap and must not be added together.

Published action-table rows can be historical or Achieved. New and Reviewed describe status words published in the source, not validation today. Missing status means unknown, not unresolved. Category counts are not counts of current failures or confirmed enforcement notices.

Excerpts and official summaries retain extracted wording and PDF page provenance. Layout changes and damaged characters can occur; the archived PDF is authoritative. Representative examples are not an exhaustive account or a prevalence estimate.
Public latest-report URLs can change after this snapshot. Use the linked local archived PDF to verify the captured evidence; the external source link establishes its CIW origin.

Management controls and the illustrative learning workflow are assistant-suggested local learning prompts, not CIW requirements, legal advice, clinical advice or an accreditation assessment. Validate applicability with appropriate local leads.

CareLens Cymru is independent and not an official CIW product.
