The Haven has no extracted notice; the general CIW copyright page provides Crown-material reuse permission. Source links and attribution are retained.

source_index.name: 20 Francis Avenue
source_index.summary:
20 Frances Avenue is a small home that supports young adults with mental health needs, who
 aspire to live independently.

 Well-being is excellent because everyone is treated with dignity and respect and are actively and
 creatively supported to achieve their wellbeing outcomes. They have as much control over their
 lives as possible and experience a sense of calm, freedom, stability and security.

 Care and support is excellent because people experience very high quality care and support; the
 manager completes in-depth, effective assessments of each person’s needs. People build very
 strong relationships with the manager and staff, and compatibility is carefully considered so they
 get along with each other. People have significant involvement in their assessments, care plans
 and reviews. They achieve their outcomes and some have gone on to live independently.

 The environment is good because it meets people’s needs. Large bedrooms and quality fixtures
 and fittings support people’s wellbeing; they feel they have the space and privacy they need to
experience a level of independence while enjoying the security of staff support.

Leadership is good, and we saw some excellent practice. There are a range of measures in place
to ensure good practice and continued compliance with regulations. The RI (responsible individual
for the home) completes thorough analysis of the service and knows in great depth what is working
well and where improvements could be made.

source_index.name: 3 Cwlach Road
source_index.provider: Prestwood Residential Homes Ltd and CareTech Community Services Limited.
source_index.summary:
3 Cwlach Road provides specialist support to people with a physical disability, challenging
 behaviour, mental health and autism. The service is registered to provide support to up to a
 maximum of five people. It is located in the coastal town of Llandudno, Conwy.

 Well-being is good as people are comfortable, relaxed and settled. Care and support is good
 because people receive person-centred care and support that reflects their individual needs,
 preferences and outcomes. Environment is good because it promotes people’s comfort, security
 and well-being. Leadership and management is good because governance systems and workforce
 support helped promote consistency and oversight within the service.

source_index.name: Abbey Dingle Care Home
source_index.summary:
Abbey Dingle Care Home is a residential service providing accommodation and support to adults.
 The service is in Llangollen, Denbighshire, close to local shops and amenities.

 People experience good wellbeing outcomes living at the service. This is because they are involved
 in day-to-day decisions about their care and have autonomy about how to live their lives. People do
 the things which matter to them and have the opportunity to engage in well led, meaningful
 activities.

 People receive good care and support. All aspects of their health and wellbeing are closely
 monitored and supported, in collaboration with external health and social are professionals. Care
 and support is person centred and meets people’s individual outcomes.

 The environment of the service is good. Improvements to the service remain ongoing and people
 are enjoying renovated communal areas and outdoor spaces.

 The leadership and management of the service is good. An experienced team work together to
 support different aspects of the service and deliver a quality provision. Governance processes are
 effective at identifying areas to develop.

source_index.name: Bodawen Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Bodawen Nursing Home is a residential service with the provision for nursing care. The service is in
 Porthmadog within Snowdonia National Park, close to the local town and amenities.

 People experience good wellbeing outcomes because they are consulted about how they want to
 be supported and are encouraged to make choices about their day to day lives. People’s views are
 sought and listened to, with the provider being proactive in taking action to facilitate people’s wants
 and wishes.

 The care and support people receive at Bodawen is good. A high level of clinical oversight means
 people receive the care and treatment they need to be healthy and live well. Care records require
 some development to ensure they are a well-rounded representation of the whole person and
 records of daily care reflect the information within personal plans.

 People live in accommodation, which is safe, well maintained and meets their needs.

 The leadership and management of the service is good. A strong leadership team are establishing
 processes to develop the quality of the service and support a positive culture within the home.

source_index.name: Breakaway Short Stay Service
source_index.provider: Bridgend County Borough Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Breakaway is a short break service in Kenfig Hill, providing respite care for up to six adults with
 learning disabilities and a range of additional needs, including autism, physical disabilities, mental
 health needs, acquired brain injuries and complex needs.

 People experience good well-being outcomes. They are supported to make choices about their
 daily lives, maintain and develop independence and participate in activities that are meaningful to
 them. Staff know people well, provide effective emotional support and work responsively with
 families and professionals to promote positive outcomes.

 The care and support provided is good. Robust assessment processes ensure staff have a good
 understanding of people's needs, preferences and risks before support is provided. Care staff use
 personalised approaches and specialist guidance to provide consistent care, promote positive
 experiences and support people's health and well-being.
The environment is good. People stay in a safe, accessible and suitable environment that supports
their needs. Communal and outdoor spaces promote social interaction, independence and
community engagement.

Leadership and management are good. Managers have created a positive and supportive culture
where staff feel valued and well supported. Training and development arrangements help staff
meet people's changing needs and governance systems provide effective oversight of the service.
Managers demonstrate a reflective approach and a commitment to continuous improvement whilst
maintaining positive outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Briarswood Residential Home
source_index.summary:
Briarswood is a small, friendly, family run home on the outskirts of Llanelli, providing support to
 people with learning disabilities.

 People have good wellbeing outcomes because they have choice and control over their day to day
 lives and are involved in decisions that affect them. They are treated with dignity, kindness and
 compassion from care staff who know them well. People are supported to do the things that matter
 to them.

 Care and support are good and personal plans are detailed, up to date and inform care staff on
 how best to support people. Care is provided by a small, stable team that provide consistency and
 have a good understanding of people’s needs.

 The environment is comfortable and homely, and people are supported to remain active within their
 community. We identified that some actions are required to optimise fire safety as advised by the
 Fire Service. This is an area for improvement and we expect the provider to address this as a
 priority.
Leadership and management is good and care staff feel supported and valued. Governance
arrangements are generally effective, although further formalisation of auditing and quality
assurance systems would strengthen this area.

source_index.name: Cartref Mynydd
source_index.summary:
Cartref Mynydd is a home providing accommodation and specialist support for up to five adults with
 learning disabilities, autism and associated support needs.

 People experience good well-being outcomes because they are supported to make choices,
 maintain relationships and participate in activities which are important to them. People access a
 wide range of community, educational and recreational opportunities, and care staff support them
 to develop independence, maintain their health and achieve personal goals. We found people are
 treated with dignity and respect and benefit from positive relationships with care staff.

 People receive good care and support from care staff who have a good understanding of their
 needs and preferences. Personal plans, risk assessments and health records provide clear
 guidance to support consistent care. Effective partnership working with health and social care
 professionals, including regular multi-disciplinary reviews, helps ensure support remains responsive
to people's changing needs. Medication systems are organised and support safe practice.

The environment requires significant improvement. Although people benefit from personalised
accommodation which promotes privacy and independence, we identified significant shortfalls
relating to maintenance, repairs and the overall condition of several areas of the service. Some
environmental issues had not been addressed in a timely manner despite being identified through
the provider's own monitoring systems. As a result, a Priority Action Notice has been issued to
ensure prompt action is taken to address these concerns and improve outcomes for people.

People benefit from good leadership and management arrangements. Managers and the
Responsible Individual (RI) maintain oversight of the service through a range of monitoring
activities. Most care staff are registered with Social Care Wales, and many have attained relevant
qualifications. Care staff told us they feel supported by management and receive regular training,
supervision and opportunities for professional development.

source_index.name: Chilton Place
source_index.summary:
The service is located in Brynmawr and provides accommodation and support for people with a
 range of physical and emotional needs. Since the previous inspection, leaders have made
 significant improvements across the service.

 We rated Well-being as Good because people are supported by caring staff who know them well
 and promote dignity, choice and meaningful engagement.

 We rated Care & Support as Good because care planning has improved and people receive care
 that is responsive to their individual needs, with appropriate involvement from health and social
 care professionals.

 We rated Environment as Good because people live in a safe, clean and comfortable home.
 Leaders have addressed many of the environmental concerns found at the previous inspection and
 continue to improve the living environment.

 We rated Leadership & Management as Good because governance, oversight and quality
 assurance arrangements have strengthened significantly. Leaders have demonstrated commitment
 and capacity to drive improvement and sustain positive changes.
Although the service has made notable progress since the previous inspection, an Area for
Improvement remains. Leaders need to continue embedding recent improvements and further
develop outcome-focused quality assurance systems to demonstrate the long-term impact on
people's experiences and well-being.

source_index.name: Cildewi
source_index.summary:
Cildewi is a care home located in Johnstown, a suburb of Carmarthen in Carmarthenshire,
 supporting adults with mental health needs. The home can support up to 7 people with 5 en-suite
 bedrooms and two separate studio flats for people moving towards semi-independent living.

 The wellbeing outcomes for people are excellent. People are empowered to make decisions about
 their daily lives and develop independence. They consistently experience a culture of respect,
 inclusion and choice, and told us they feel safe, valued and supported to achieve what matters to
 them.

 The care and support people receive is good as care staff know people well and provide
 compassionate, person-centred support that promotes health, wellbeing and independence.

 The environment is good, it is safe, comfortable and designed to promote independence. People’s
 bedrooms are personalised, communal areas are welcoming, and the environment supports people
 to develop daily living skills within a homely setting.
The leadership and management of the service is excellent, Effective leaders have established a
positive, values-based culture supported by effective governance and quality assurance systems.
Care staff feel well supported, professionals spoke positively about communication and partnership
working, and there is a clear commitment to continuously improving outcomes for people.

source_index.name: College Fields Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
College Fields Nursing home is based in Barry and can accommodate 68 people with a range of
 nursing and personal care needs. This inspection was unannounced. There is a Responsible
 Individual (RI) for the service and a manager who is registered with Social Care Wales (SCW) the
 workforce regulator.
 People experience excellent care and support from a kind and friendly staff team. Staffing levels
 are sufficient to meet individuals’ needs, with arrangements in place to cover any staffing shortfalls.
 Wellbeing outcomes for people are good, supported by a caring staff team and the provider’s
 ongoing commitment to improving the quality of the service.
 Leadership and management arrangements are good and continue to strengthen and promote a
 culture of openness and transparency within the service. The manager is visible, approachable,
 and actively involved in the day-to-day operation of the home, providing clear leadership and
 demonstrating a commitment to improving outcomes for people.
 People live in a good, clean and well-maintained environment that is well decorated. Some areas of
 the home have been identified as requiring improvement, and improvement works remain ongoing.
 While these works do not impact the people living in the home, their management and associated
 safety considerations continue to be monitored.

source_index.name: Colwyn Bay Old Convent Nursing Home, Ltd
source_index.provider: Colwyn Bay Old Convent Nursing Home Ltd
source_index.summary:
Colwyn Bay Old Convent Nursing home is located in a quiet residential area near to the centre of
 Colwyn Bay.

 People living in the service receive good care and support from care staff who know them well.
 Care staff treat people with dignity and respect. People and their relatives speak positively about
 care staff and we saw warm and respectful interactions during the inspection. Care records reflect
 people’s needs and preferences. Care staff seek advice from health professionals when people’s
 needs change.

 The home is clean, comfortable and pleasantly decorated. There is appropriate equipment,
 communal and private spaces to meet people’s needs. We saw people personalise their rooms
 with photographs, ornaments and items important to them. The responsible individual (RI) and
 manager have effective systems to monitor the quality and safety of the service. They seek
 feedback from people, relatives and care staff and act on this to make improvements.

source_index.name: Crick Care Home
source_index.summary:
Crick Care Home is situated in a rural location on the outskirts of Caldicot in Monmouthshire. The
 service provides accommodation, support and nursing care for up to 49 people.

 At this inspection, we found people's wellbeing is good. People and their relatives spoke positively
 about the service, and our observations confirmed that staff treat people with dignity, respect and
 kindness.

 People receive good care and support, with personal plans and risk management arrangements in
 place to promote their health, safety and wellbeing. The management team recognises
 opportunities to further strengthen care planning to ensure it consistently reflects people's individual
 wishes, aspirations and personal outcomes.

 People live in a good environment that is clean, comfortable and well maintained. They can move
 around safely and have access to the equipment they need to promote their independence, comfort
 and wellbeing. The provider continues to invest in the environment to enhance people's quality of
 life.
Leadership and management is good. Effective governance arrangements and visible leadership
support positive outcomes for people. While improvements have been made since the inspection,
further work is required to ensure all staff receive regular supervision, appraisal and opportunities
for professional development.

source_index.name: Duffryn House
source_index.summary:
Duffryn House is a care home which supports people with a learning disability and other associated
 needs. It is located in a residential area of Aberdare.


 Well-being is excellent because people achieve outstanding outcomes important to them, and are
 supported to live meaningful, independent and fulfilling lives. Strong relationships, positive risk-
 taking and excellent community involvement help people maintain choice and control. Care and
 support is good because people receive personalised, outcome-focused care from skilled care staff
 who understand their needs and preferences. Effective safeguarding, medication management and
 infection prevention arrangements help keep people safe. The environment is good because
 people live in a comfortable, safe and personalised home which meets their needs and promotes
 their well-being. Leadership and management is good because effective governance, oversight and
 quality assurance systems support positive outcomes for people. A stable, well-trained and well-
 supported staff team provide consistent care.

source_index.name: East Park Care Centre Limited
source_index.summary:
East Park Care Centre is a pleasant and spacious 21 bed residential home for adults. It is situated
 in the village of Jeffreyston in Pembrokeshire.

 At this inspection we found peoples well-being is good, because both the care and support people
 receive and the environment they live in support them to achieve good well-being outcomes. There
 is a real sense of community and friendship within the service, with people feeling happy,
 comfortable and at home.

 Care and Support is good. People are supported to maintain and improve their physical, mental
 health, and emotional wellbeing by caring and compassionate care staff. Care staff know people
 well and interactions are respectful and personalised to individual needs.

 The environment is good and people benefit from a warm, welcoming, comfortable, and homely
 environment which promotes their well-being.

 Leadership and management of the service is good because the positive actions of the
 Responsible Individual (RI), manager and care staff team ensure people achieve good outcomes.

source_index.name: Elan Specialist Residential Care Service
source_index.summary:
Elan Specialist Residential Care Service provides care and support for people with learning
 disabilities. The service offers accommodation for up to five people. Located in the village of
 Aberfan, the home benefits from close proximity to local amenities and community facilities, all of
 which are within walking distance.

 People experience good well-being outcomes. Staff have a thorough understanding of the people
 they support, including their preferences, needs, and what is important to them. They are
 knowledgeable about the most effective approaches to delivering personalised care and support.
 People are encouraged and empowered to make daily choices and decisions about their lives.

 Care and support is good. Care documentation is person-centred. Care documentation is reviewed
 regularly and updated as required to reflect changes in needs. Risks to people’s health and safety
 are appropriately assessed and managed. People have timely access to appropriate healthcare
 professionals and services to support their ongoing health and well-being.

 The service is well-led and has a positive culture of promoting the well-being of supported people
 and staff. There are governance and quality assurance systems in place helping the service
operate smoothly. Care staff receive training relevant to the needs of the people they care for and
say they feel supported in their roles.

People live in an environment that is suited to their needs and promotes their comfort, safety, and
well-being. The home is clean, well maintained, and provides a welcoming and homely
atmosphere. The provider has effective arrangements in place to ensure the premises are kept in
good condition.

source_index.name: EMJ & GP Ltd TA Park View Care Home
source_index.summary:
Well-being is rated good because people are supported to maintain choice, independence,
 relationships and meaningful lifestyles. Relatives described people as happy, settled, safe and well
 cared for, with positive opportunities for activities, social engagement and community participation.

 Care and Support is rated as good because people receive personalised care based on
 comprehensive assessments, care plans and regular reviews. Safeguarding, medication
 management, nutrition, hydration and infection control arrangements were effective. Relatives and
 professionals reported high levels of satisfaction with care and communication.

 Environment is rated good because people live in a clean, safe and comfortable home with
 attractive communal areas, personalised bedrooms and a secure garden. Health and safety, fire
 safety and maintenance systems were established and effective. Minor maintenance issues
 identified were being addressed and did not significantly affect people’s well-being.

 Leadership and Management is rated good because the service benefits from visible and
 responsive leadership, effective governance and robust quality assurance arrangements. Feedback
 from relatives, staff and professionals was overwhelmingly positive, highlighting strong
communication, supportive leadership and a positive culture. Minor opportunities for improvement
related to documentation, training reporting and staff development.

source_index.name: Glencourt
source_index.summary:
Glencourt is a small care service without nursing in Caerphilly supporting people with a range of
 needs and abilities. At our previous inspection, we identified significant concerns relating to the
 quality of care and the effectiveness of oversight by the Responsible Individual (RI), resulting in the
 issuance of two Priority Action Notices (PANs). At this inspection, we found significant
 improvements across all areas of the service and acknowledge the considerable commitment,
 dedication and hard work demonstrated by the provider, leaders and staff in achieving these
 changes.

 Of particular note has been the comprehensive redevelopment of people's personal plans, which
 are now more person-centred and outcome focused. The provider has also strengthened quality
 assurance arrangements, resulting in improved monitoring, oversight and accountability. A newly
 appointed RI has introduced more meaningful systems for regulatory visits and reporting, providing
 greater scrutiny and improved alignment with regulatory expectations.

 As a result of the progress made, we are satisfied that the concerns which led to the PANs have
 been addressed and both have been removed. The service has achieved ratings of ‘Good’ across
 all four inspection themes.

source_index.name: Heddfan residential Home
source_index.summary:
Heddfan provides care and support for people with learning disabilities. The service offers
 accommodation for up to five people and is located in the town of Merthyr Tydfil. The home is
 within walking distance of a range of local amenities, services, and community facilities, enabling
 people to access and participate in community life.

 People’s well-being outcomes are excellent. Staff provide person-centred care and support that
 promotes people’s rights, choice, and independence. They have a thorough understanding of the
 people they support, including what is important to them and the most effective approaches to
 meeting their needs. Staff have developed positive and trusting relationships with people, enabling
 them to deliver care that is responsive and tailored to personal preferences. Care documentation is
 outcome-focused, clearly identifying people’s goals, aspirations, and the support required to help
 them achieve the best possible outcomes.

 Leadership and management is good. The service is well led and promotes a positive, person-
 centred culture that places the well-being of both people receiving support and staff at its core.
 Effective leadership and management arrangements ensure the service operates smoothly, with
 governance and quality assurance systems in place to monitor performance, drive continuous
improvement, and maintain high standards of care and support.

The environment is good. It is safe, comfortable, and suited to people’s needs. The home is clean,
well maintained, and provides a welcoming atmosphere for those living there. The provider has
established effective systems for the ongoing maintenance of the premises, ensuring repairs are
completed promptly and that the environment remains safe, secure, and fit for purpose.

source_index.name: Kington House
source_index.summary:
Kington House provides a high standard of care and support for adults, specialising in supporting
 those on a journey of recovery following brain injury, or history of substance misuse.

 ‘Wellbeing’ is rated as ‘excellent,’ as people receive highly personalised care and support which
 promotes independence, recovery, health and positive outcomes. People feel safe, valued,
 respected and listened to. People are actively involved in decisions about their lives and are
 supported to pursue meaningful goals and maintain important relationships.

 ‘Care and support’ are rated ‘excellent,’ because people are involved in planning and reviewing
 their care. Documentation around this is strong, relevant and informative, ensuring support workers
 can deliver care and support to meet people’s needs.

 ‘Environment’ is rated ‘good,’ as there are systems in place to monitor and improve the building.
 The environment meets people’s needs, providing them with their own secure and safe space,
 while offering opportunities to engage with others in communal areas.

 ‘Leadership and management’’ are rated ‘excellent,’ because there is effective oversight by
leaders. The recruitment and training of support workers is robust, and the culture fostered within
the service is highly supportive.

source_index.name: Lakeside House Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Since the last inspection, the service has appointed a new Responsible Individual (RI) and
 undergone a change in directorship. The new leadership brings experience, investment, and a
 strong commitment to improving outcomes, while the registered manager has remained in post,
 providing continuity and stability for people, relatives, and the staff team at Lakeside.
 People experience positive well-being outcomes because they are supported to make choices,
 maintain relationships, stay safe and take part in meaningful activities. People feel valued, listened
 to and supported by kind staff and approachable leaders.
 Care and Support is good because people receive personalised support from familiar staff who
 know their needs, preferences and routines well. Effective healthcare involvement, safe medicines
 management and positive mealtime experiences support people’s health and well-being. Stronger
 oversight of personal care planning is needed to ensure all aspects of care are consistently
 delivered, recorded and reviewed.
 The environment is good because people live in a comfortable, clean and well-maintained home
 which promotes dignity, independence and quality of life. Ongoing investment and planned
 improvements will further enhance people’s experiences.
 Leadership and Management is effective because people benefit from visible, responsive
 leadership and a stable, well-supported workforce. Governance arrangements support consistent,
 person-centred care, and leaders continue to strengthen quality assurance and service
 development to improve outcomes.

source_index.name: Llwyn Teg Residential Care Home
source_index.summary:
People who have made Llwyn Teg their home receive a good standard of care.
 Everyone we spoke with has high levels of confidence in the service describing it as
 “marvellous” and “great”. One person told us “I love it here”. People can
 communicate in both English and Welsh.

 Wellbeing is rated as good because of the relationships people and those important
 to them have with the staff team. This, together with the opportunities to do things
 that they enjoy mean they are treated with dignity and their days are meaningful.

 Care and support is good because the team is led by an experienced and well-
 regarded manager who has a lot of confidence in her team. The planned
 improvements to the care records will benefit people and the staff team.
The environment is good because standards of cleanliness are high and although
some parts would benefit from some updating, it is as homely and comfortable as it
can be.

Leadership and management is good because the values set by the organisation are
embedded into practice. The manager leads a team of motivated, kind and
appropriately trained staff.

source_index.name: Llys Gwyn House Limited
source_index.summary:
Llys Gwyn House is a residential care home located in Pontarddulais, Swansea, providing
 residential care and support for older adults, including people living with dementia and age-related
 conditions, in a comfortable environment that promotes wellbeing and independence.

 Well-being is good because people are supported to make choices, maintain important
 relationships and take part in meaningful activities that matter to them. People told us they feel
 safe, respected and well cared for, while relatives and professionals described the service as,
 responsive and welcoming. The appointment of a well-being co-ordinator has increased
 opportunities for engagement and community involvement, helping people to enjoy positive
 experiences and achieve outcomes that are important to them.

 Care and support is good because people receive person-centred care from staff who understand
 their needs and preferences. Care plans are regularly reviewed, concerns are escalated promptly
and people have access to the healthcare support they need. Positive feedback from relatives and
professionals demonstrates people receive good quality care and support.

The environment is good because people live in a safe, comfortable and homely setting that meets
their needs and preferences. People have access to a range of indoor and outdoor spaces,
bedrooms are personalised, and the home is well maintained. There is also evidence of continued
investment to improve the environment and enhance people's experience of living there.

Leadership and management is good because effective governance and oversight systems help
ensure people receive safe, consistent care. Leaders monitor the quality of the service through
regular reviews, audits and feedback, and use this information to drive improvement. Staff describe
managers as approachable and supportive, and benefit from regular supervision, training and
development opportunities that help them meet people's needs.

source_index.name: Llys Hafren Care Home
source_index.summary:
Llys Hafren Care Home is located within walking distance of Welshpool town centre. The service
 provides respite, residential and personal care for adults aged 65 and over of all genders, including
 frail elderly people and those living with a diagnosis of dementia.

 People experience positive well-being outcomes. They are treated with dignity and respect, have
 good relationships with staff and are supported to make choices about their daily lives.

 Care and support is person-centred and of good quality. People’s care and support plans are made
 and reviewed with them, or a representative, on a regular basis. Staff understand people well and
 respond to changes in their health and well-being. Committed care staff are safely recruited, well
 trained and caring.
The home environment is warm, clean and homely and supports people’s comfort and
independence. Safety checks are completed and bedrooms are personalised and meet people’s
needs.

Leadership and oversight arrangements are effective. The Responsible Individual (RI) visits
regularly and seeks feedback from people using the service to support ongoing improvement.
Leadership and governance promote a positive culture through audits, feedback and regular
review. Staff feel supported in their role through appropriate training, supervision and guidance,
enabling them to provide safe, consistent and responsive care.

source_index.name: Llys Meddyg
source_index.summary:
Llys Meddyg is a care home with nursing for 18 older people, most of whom have dementia. The
 service provides accommodation for females only and the provider is focussed on meeting the
 needs of the local community.

 People experience good well-being because their physical and mental health and emotional needs
 are closely monitored and well-being needs are met. Some excellent practice was seen such as
 tailored, person-centred activities and a high level of supervision to prevent falls. People and their
 relatives praise the level of dignity and respect afforded. People have as much control over their
 day as they can with daily routines and choices of food and activities respected and catered for.

 Care and support is good; people are well cared for and are happy in their home. They are treated
 with kindness and genuine compassion. People feel they are listened to and are happy they can
 communicate in Welsh if they prefer as there are Welsh speaking staff.
The environment is good because the layout suits the people who live here. A maintenance person
is employed to keep the home in a good state of repair and a safe, homely, comfortable and clean
environment is provided.

Leadership and management is good because there are systems in place to ensure continued
quality of care and compliance. The provider knows what the service does well and where
improvements could be made.

source_index.name: Luk-ros Bungalow
source_index.summary:
Luk-ros bungalow is situated in a quiet area with access to local amenities. There are 4 registered
 places at Luk-ros bungalow.

 Well-being is excellent. People receive support that promotes dignity, respect and positive
 outcomes. Care staff work proactively with people, relatives and professionals to help individuals
 achieve their personal goals, including accessing holidays, increasing community involvement and
 developing confidence. Care staff provide meaningful opportunities that enhance well-being,
 promote independence and enable people to remain active participants within their communities.

 Care and Support is good. People receive person-centred care from care staff who know them well
 and understand their individual needs. Care staff promote independence while protecting people
 from harm through effective safeguarding arrangements, positive risk management and regular
 monitoring. People receive support from trained and knowledgeable staff who manage medicines
safely and help them achieve meaningful and fulfilling lives.

Environment is good. People live in a welcoming, well-maintained environment that supports their
safety, comfort and well-being. The service provides accessible indoor and outdoor spaces,
including sensory environments that reflect people's interests and preferences. Ongoing
improvements to the property demonstrate a commitment to enhancing people's experiences,
independence and opportunities for engagement in meaningful activities.

Leadership and Management is excellent. The registered manager provides effective leadership
and has identified opportunities to improve outcomes for people. The responsible individual (RI)
Managers maintain strong oversight of the service through quality assurance, staff supervision and
regular review processes. Staff described leaders as approachable and supportive, and the service
promotes a positive culture of continuous improvement, person-centred practice and open
communication.

source_index.name: Pentre House
source_index.provider: Rhondda Cynon Taff County Borough Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Pentre House is a Local Authority residential home providing care and support to older adults with
 residential care needs. It is located centrally within Pentre.


 Well-being is excellent because people are supported to live meaningful, independent and fulfilling
 lives. People are at the centre of decisions about their care and support. They benefit from strong
 relationships with care staff who know them well and promote their rights, strengths and
 aspirations. Care and support is good because people receive personalised, outcome-focused care
 which reflects their needs, preferences and wishes. Detailed care planning, effective
 multidisciplinary working and strong safeguarding arrangements support people to remain safe and
 healthy. The environment is excellent because people live in an exceptionally welcoming,
 comfortable and homely setting which enhances their quality of life. Leadership and management is
 good because strong, values-led leadership, and good governance and quality assurance systems
 support positive outcomes for people. Managers demonstrate a strong commitment to continuous
 improvement and actively involve people and care staff in the development of the service. A stable,
 skilled and well-supported staff team provides consistent care and contributes to a positive culture
 throughout the home.

source_index.name: Plas Bryn Rhosyn
source_index.summary:
Plas Bryn Rhosyn is a residential care home subdivided into five suites. Four, long term residential
 care, and one which supports people on respite/short term basis.
 People experience excellent well-being. They are actively involved in decisions about their care
 and support wherever possible and benefit from highly personalised care delivered by
 compassionate staff. There is an exceptional range of meaningful activities in the service which
 promote choice, independence and dignity.

 People receive good, person-centred care from skilled staff who know them well and work
 effectively with healthcare professionals to meet changing needs. Strong safeguarding practices,
 safe medication management and effective infection control arrangements help protect people from
 harm.

 The environment is excellent. Plas Bryn Rhosyn is a purpose-built, dementia-friendly home,
 promoting independence, confidence and good quality of life through personalised living spaces,
 welcoming communal areas and accessible outdoor environments. High standards of cleanliness,
 maintenance and safety, combined with ongoing investment, ensure people live in a comfortable,
 attractive and well-managed setting.

 Leadership and management are excellent. Strong and visible management, robust governance
 arrangements and a highly skilled workforce create a culture of continuous improvement. Effective
quality assurance, reflective practice and meaningful engagement with people, relatives and
professionals ensure the service consistently delivers positive outcomes and inspires confidence in
people.

source_index.name: Plas Cwm Carw Care Home
source_index.summary:
Plas Cwm Carw Care Home is in the centre of Port Talbot, close to shops and other amenities. The
 provider has taken action to improve standards of care and support, as well as the overall
 management of the service. As a result, people experience good well-being as they receive safe
 care and have consistently positive experiences. They benefit from a varied programme of activities
 and regular opportunities to connect meaningfully with others.

 Although progress has been made, standards of care and support require improvement. Medication
 and infection control procedures have improved, and people receive timely input from medical and
 specialist services. This helps them to stay healthy. However, the care planning and review
 process requires improvement. This is to ensure people’s needs and goals are accurately reflected
 in personal plans and care staff have access to clear and consistent guidance.
The home and grounds are secure and appropriately maintained. The accommodation has a
homely, welcoming feel and a good range of facilities to support activities of daily living. Many
environmental improvements have been made, including the redecoration and development of
communal areas and the renewal of some furniture and furnishings.

Leadership and management arrangements have improved significantly, although some areas
continue to require improvement. New managers have built trust by listening to feedback and
making positive changes. They promote an open and supportive culture, which has resulted in
more effective teamwork and improved staff practice and morale. Staff receive appropriate
induction, training and informal support, although managers require more time to improve
supervision and appraisal processes. Administrative systems also require improvement to ensure
managers have timely access to all the records they need to manage the service effectively.

source_index.name: Pride in Care ltd Glandovery house
source_index.summary:
Glandovery House is a small service which provides personal care and support for up to five adults,
 located in the Blaenau Gwent area. We rated well-being as excellent. People receive exceptional
 support from skilled and committed care staff who know them very well. People are supported to
 make choices, maintain important relationships, take part in meaningful activities and achieve
 outcomes that matter to them.

 We rated care and support as excellent because care is highly personalised, responsive and
 outcome focused. Care staff anticipate and meet people’s needs without delay and support people
 to maintain their health, independence and well-being.

 We rated the environment as excellent. The home is welcoming, clean, homely and highly
 personalised. The provider monitors the environment and makes changes as people’s needs
 change, supporting people to continue living fulfilled lives.

 We rated leadership and management as excellent. Leaders promote an exceptionally strong
 person-centred culture, use effective governance systems to improve the service, and involve
 people creatively in decisions, including recruitment. People, relatives and professionals have high
 levels of confidence in the service.

source_index.name: Rotherslade House
source_index.summary:
People experience good well-being at Rotherslade House. Staff know people very well and treat
 them with dignity and respect. A good atmosphere was apparent with people welcoming visitors to
 their home and extending a family feel.

 Care and support provided to people considers individual outcomes and goals. Referrals to
 specialists are completed ensuring people receive required assessments and support in a timely
 way. Good medication practice was observed on the whole and consideration is being given to how
 this process can be more person-centred considering privacy and dignity. Overall, this theme has a
 good rating.

 The environment at Rotherslade House requires improvement to ensure people’s optimum health
 and well-being is achieved. Certain aspects of the environment are well-maintained with the
 necessary checks and certificates in place. However; there are other aspects such as the former
 laundry/storage area that are in poor condition and have not been improved since the last
 inspection. The Responsible Individual (RI) and manager have given assurances improvements will
 be made.

 Overall, leadership and management at the service is good. A recent new team including the RI,
 manager and deputy manager have settled into their roles. There is good oversight and as a result
 of this an awareness of goals with planned timescales to work towards. Staffing has been identified
 as an area to improve considering staff skill mix and competency levels. This is being worked
 towards with staff going through recruitment and training.

source_index.name: Sandford
source_index.summary:
People experience good well-being outcomes; they are treated with dignity and respect and have
 activities available to them. People are supported to stay as healthy as possible, with systems in
 place to protect people in an environment that meets their needs. People are treated as individuals
 and can live their lives how they wish.

 Care and support are good. Detailed care documentation is in place to support people’s needs. The
 service has good systems to safeguard people, and good systems to reduce the risk of the spread
 of infection. Care staff treat people with kindness and compassion. Personal plans are an accurate
 reflection of the individual and people receive appropriate care and support.

 The environment is good and meets people’s needs and outcomes, enhances their well-being, and
 is safe. Sandford is well decorated throughout and has enough communal space. People’s rooms,
 as well as communal areas, are kept clean and free from hazards. People can personalise their
rooms if they wish. Significant investment in the environment is evident.

The leadership and management of Sandford is good. There is a management team in place who
have good oversight of the service. They ensure the required staff recruitment, training, and
support is undertaken and enable good-quality support and facilities to be provided. Care staff told
us they are happy working at the service.

source_index.name: Springholme Care Anglesey Ltd
source_index.summary:
Springholme provides accommodation, personal care and support for older people, including
 people living with dementia.

 People experience positive well-being outcomes and are supported by staff who know them well,
 treat them with kindness and respect, and promote dignity, independence, choice and meaningful
 relationships.

 Care and support is good because it is planned around people’s individual needs, preferences and
 risks. Care staff provide calm, patient and person-centred support with personal care, mobility,
 meals, medication and healthcare needs. The service works effectively with external health
 professionals and has systems in place to protect people from harm.

 The environment is safe, comfortable, clean and homely. People benefit from personalised
 bedrooms, communal spaces, secure outdoor areas and effective maintenance systems.
 Environmental risks are monitored and addressed through audits, servicing, repairs and
 improvement trackers.

 Leadership and management arrangements are effective. The manager, who is also the
 Responsible Individual (RI), has established strong governance, quality assurance and
improvement systems. Feedback from people, relatives and staff informs service development.
Some practice approaches excellent, particularly in person-centred culture, Welsh language
support, governance and continuous improvement.

source_index.name: Stanley Villa
source_index.summary:
People living at Stanley Villa experience positive outcomes and benefit from a recovery-focused
 service where they are treated with dignity, respect, and compassion. People spoke positively
 about the support they receive and the impact the service has had on their wellbeing,
 independence, and recovery. We observed staff and managers to have warm and professional
 relationships with people, and there were opportunities for individuals to contribute to decisions
 about the service. The environment is clean, comfortable, and generally supports people's recovery
 needs.

 However, outcomes for people require significant improvement in several areas. We identified
 significant concerns regarding medication management, care planning, and workforce
 management. Personal plans were not always complete or sufficiently detailed to guide staff in
 meeting people's assessed needs and managing identified risks. Medication management systems
 were ineffective, with concerns relating to administration, stock control, staff competence, and
auditing arrangements. In addition, there were deficits in recruitment processes, staff registration,
and mandatory training, reducing assurance that staff have the necessary skills and competence to
provide safe care and support. As a result, we have issued Priority Action Notices.

While management and oversight arrangements are in place, they are not effective in identifying
and addressing these shortfalls. The provider must also strengthen governance systems, quality
assurance processes, and aspects of environmental risk management to ensure people
consistently receive safe, high-quality care and support.

source_index.name: Stow Park Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Stow Park Nursing Home provides 24-hour Nursing care and support to people living with dementia
 and mental health related conditions. It is located within walking distance of Newport’s city centre.

 People’s wellbeing is good. They experience positive wellbeing outcomes and benefit from kind,
 compassionate care delivered by a stable and committed staff team. People feel safe, maintain
 meaningful relationships with family and friends and engage in activities that matter to them.
 Relatives, visitors and professionals consistently describe the service as welcoming, homely and
 responsive, demonstrating people are valued, respected and supported to live as well as possible.

 Care and support is good. People receive care and support that promotes their dignity, safety and
 wellbeing. Staff know people well and work alongside healthcare professionals to respond to their
 changing needs. The provider can further improve outcomes for people by ensuring personal plans
 and reviews consistently reflect individuals’ strengths, preferences and progress towards achieving
what matters to them.

We rate the environment as good. People live in a welcoming, clean and well-maintained
environment that supports their comfort, safety and wellbeing.

People benefit from a well-led service. Effective governance systems, quality assurance processes
and oversight arrangements support the safe delivery of care and help drive service development.
Leaders promote a positive culture and are committed to achieving good outcomes.

source_index.name: Sycamore House
source_index.summary:
We rated well-being as requires improvement because people do not always have meaningful
 opportunities to influence reviews, decisions and care planning. Records do not consistently
 demonstrate how people’s views, or those of their representatives, inform decisions. In addition,
 people have not always accessed the range of community and sensory activities described in the
 provider’s Statement of Purpose and assessed as important to them in their personal plans.

 People experience positive care and support from a staff team which knows them well and
 promotes their dignity, respect and individual choices. We observed warm, person-centred
 interactions and found detailed care planning, risk assessments and medication management
 arrangements which support people’s safety and well-being.

 We found the environment to be of good standard. People live in a comfortable, homely and well-
 maintained environment that supports their needs and independence. The home provides a range
of communal and private spaces, accessible outdoor areas and appropriate environmental
adaptations to meet people’s individual needs. Arrangements to promote people’s safety are
effective.

Leadership and management are good because leaders understand the service, identify areas for
improvement and are open and transparent about challenges. However, some improvements
identified through quality assurance processes have not been resolved quickly enough, which has
delayed improvements to outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Sycamore Lodge Residential Care Home
source_index.summary:
People experience good well-being outcomes at Sycamore Lodge. There are regular activities
 which people can be involved in, and staff treat people with dignity and respect. People are
 supported to stay as healthy as possible, with systems in place to protect people in an environment
 that meets their needs.

 People receive good care and support from a care staff team who understand their needs and treat
 them with dignity and respect. Care plans need improvement as they do not always contain
 detailed, personalised information appropriate to the person. Medication processes within the
 service are undertaken well and people attend appointments with health professionals or health
 care professionals are contacted as required.

 People live in an environment that is good. Sycamore Lodge is decorated throughout and has
 ample communal space. The outside areas offer well laid out, safe and appropriate space which
 people use. People have their own bedrooms which they have furnished to their personal
preference, offering privacy and people are free to use them whenever they wish.

Leadership and management of the service is good. The Responsible Individual (RI) and manager
have good oversight of the service and quality assurance monitoring takes place regularly. Care
staff are recruited safely, well supported and receive appropriate training to meet the needs of the
people they support. Care staff are happy working at the service. Safeguarding referrals are made
to the local authority when required and monitored closely.

source_index.name: Talbot Court Care Home
source_index.summary:
Talbot Court Care Home is in the centre of Port Talbot with easy access to amenities, although
 roadside parking is limited. People enjoy a good quality of life at the home, where they have
 developed meaningful relationships with others. Care staff respect people’s wishes and routines,
 helping them to maintain control over their daily lives. People take part in a range of in-house
 activities that promote their well-being.

 People receive a good standard of care and support to help them stay healthy. Care staff know
 people well and support them safely, in line with individual risk assessments and personal plans.
 People have timely access to medical and specialist services.

 The accommodation is secure, presented to a good overall standard and includes some colourful,
 homely features. It has the required equipment and facilities to promote people’s health and safety.
The home has very good leadership and management, so people consistently experience a safe,
reliable service. Staff are appropriately recruited and receive the training and support they need to
carry out their roles effectively. Organised administration and auditing systems help to ensure good
standards of practice are maintained. The Responsible Individual (RI) monitors the quality of the
service closely and works with the manager to make continuous improvements.

source_index.name: The Glynne Home
source_index.summary:
The Glynne achieved a good rating in each of the four themes: well-being, care and support,
 environment, and leadership and management. People living at the home are supported, where
 possible, to lead lives that reflect their preferences and aspirations. They receive person-centred
 care from staff who know them well, promote dignity, choice and independence, and respond
 proactively to changing needs. People and their relatives speak positively about the quality of care,
 and the care staff demonstrate a strong commitment to person-centred practice.

 The environment is comfortable and welcoming, with ongoing investment in refurbishment and
 improvements to ensure it remains suitable for people's needs. Leadership and management are
 effective, with visible and supportive leaders providing oversight through governance and quality
 assurance systems. Staff receive regular training, supervision and support, promoting a positive
 culture focused on continuous improvement and positive outcomes for people living at the service.

source_index.name: The Hollies
source_index.summary:
People achieve excellent well-being outcomes because care staff provide highly personalised
 support that promotes independence, choice, relationships and community inclusion. People live
 fulfilling lives, maintain important relationships and take part in activities that matter to them.
 People, relatives and professionals consistently described positive and excellent outcomes in well-
 being.

 People receive excellent care and support. Care staff know people exceptionally well and provide
 highly personalised support based on individual wishes, strengths and goals. Staff use positive risk
 management to maximise independence whilst keeping people safe. Strong partnerships with
 health, mental health and social care professionals help people access the right support at the right
 time. We found evidence of significant progress in people’s independence, communication,
 confidence and quality of life.
People benefit from a good environment that supports their comfort, independence and well-being.
The home is warm, welcoming and highly personalised. Accessible indoor and outdoor spaces
promote independence and social interaction. Ongoing investment and improvements help ensure
the environment remains safe, comfortable and homely.

People benefit from good leadership and management. Leaders promote a positive, inclusive and
person-centred culture. The manager provides visible leadership and actively involves people in
shaping the service. We found several examples of excellent practice, particularly in promoting
participation, staff support and continuity of care. However, leadership systems require further
strengthening to improve oversight, recording and information sharing of allegations of staff
misconduct.

source_index.name: The Old Manse
source_index.summary:
The Old Manse is a care home service providing accommodation and support for up to four adults
 with learning disabilities, autism and associated needs.

 People experience good well-being outcomes because they are supported to make choices,
 develop independence, participate in meaningful activities and maintain relationships important to
 them. People are treated with dignity and respect and are supported to achieve personal goals
 which enhance their quality of life.

 People receive good care and support personalised to their individual needs, preferences and
 aspirations. Personal plans are detailed and person-centred, helping care staff provide consistent
 support which promotes independence, health and well-being. People are supported to access
 healthcare services, participate in community activities and achieve positive personal outcomes.
People benefit from a good environment which is comfortable, safe and personalised. The home
provides welcoming communal areas, well-maintained bedrooms and outdoor spaces which
support relaxation, recreation and social interaction. Facilities within the home, including sensory
resources, enhance people’s well-being and help meet individual needs.

People benefit from good leadership and management. Effective governance systems, quality
assurance processes and strong management oversight help ensure the service is well organised
and focused on continuous improvement. Care staff feel supported by managers and receive
training and development opportunities which help them meet people’s needs effectively. Feedback
from people, relatives and care staff is sought and used to support the continued development of
the service.

source_index.name: Torestin Care Home
source_index.summary:
People living at Torestin have good well-being outcomes because they are treated with dignity and
 respect from care staff who know them well. They are supported to make choices over their day to
 day lives and how they spend their time.

 Care and support are good, detailed person-centred plans inform care staff on the care required
 and people’s preferences on how they would like to be supported. People’s physical and mental
 health is promoted and referrals to health and social care professionals are made in a timely
 manner when needs change.

 Overall, people live in an environment that is safe, comfortable and homely, with ongoing
 investment helping to enhance the quality of the environment and support positive outcomes.

 Leadership and management are good, care staff report feeling supported and confident in their
role. Governance and oversight arrangements are generally effective and demonstrate the
provider's commitment to continuous improvement. Strengthening and more effective oversight in
some areas would further enhance monitoring quality and drive improvements.

source_index.name: Ty Arfryn
source_index.summary:
Ty Arfryn is situated in the outskirts of Carmarthen town providing care and support to adults with
 functional mental health needs and/ or learning disabilities.

 The well-being outcomes of people is “Excellent” as care staff empower people to thrive by
 providing many opportunities to maintain, develop and explore their interests, strengths and skills.

 The care and support people receive is “Good,” as care workers provide care and support in a way
 that considers people’s wishes, aspirations, risks and specialist needs.

 The environment in which people live is “Good,” as people benefit greatly from living in a home
 which is suitable to their individual needs.

 The leadership and management of the service is “Excellent” as leaders promote an exceptionally
 strong, positive culture in the service where people, relatives, care staff and professionals feel
 listened to and valued.

source_index.name: Ty Mynydd
source_index.summary:
Ty Mynydd is located in Neath and provides personal care and support to people. It is close to a
 number of community facilities which can be easily accessed from the service. The service has
 made significant progress since the previous inspection and people are now benefiting from
 improved outcomes across the service. There are notable improvements in care planning, staffing
 and staff support, governance systems and environmental safety.

 Well-being at the service is good and people receive personalised care and support that reflects
 their individual needs, preferences and aspirations. People have access to a wider range of
 meaningful opportunities and are supported by care staff who understand their communication and
 support needs.

 Improvements have been made to care and support and personal plans are detailed, regularly
 reviewed and provide staff with clear guidance to support people safely and effectively. Further
 improvements are required to ensure all records are completed consistently.

 The environment is good. Improvements identified at the previous inspection relating to health and
 safety monitoring and environmental checks have been addressed. People live in accommodation
 that supports their comfort, safety and well-being.
Leadership and management is good and governance systems have been strengthened. Staff
supervision and support arrangements have improved, and reliance on agency staff has reduced
significantly. Care staff spoke positively about the culture within the service and described
management as supportive and approachable.

source_index.name: Ty Newydd
source_index.summary:
Ty Newydd is a small residential service in Newport. Peoples Wellbeing is good. People are
 supported to maintain their health, independence and quality of life through access to healthcare,
 meaningful activities and community involvement. Staff promote choice, communication and
 positive risk-taking, enabling people to develop skills and maintain relationships. People
 experienced positive outcomes and appeared relaxed, engaged and valued.

 Care and support is good. People receive well-planned, person-centred care supported by effective
 assessment, care planning and multidisciplinary working. Robust pre-admission processes ensure
 needs can be met safely. Medication management is organised and monitored, healthcare needs
 are addressed promptly.

 The environment is good. People live in a clean, comfortable and personalised home that promotes
 independence, participation and well-being. The environment reflects individuals' interests and
achievements, with access to meaningful activities, communal spaces and outdoor areas. Effective
maintenance and security arrangements ensure the home remains safe, welcoming, well-
maintained and supportive of people's rights.

Leadership and management at Ty Newydd demonstrate strong oversight, a positive culture and a
commitment to continuous improvement. Robust governance systems, effective staff support,
multidisciplinary working and responsive safeguarding practices promote safe, person-centred
care. Managers act promptly on concerns and have identified and begun addressing areas for
further development.

source_index.name: Victoria House
source_index.summary:
Victoria house is situated within a quiet area with access to local amenities. There are 3 registered
 places within Victoria House.

 Wellbeing is good. People’s personal plans reflect individual preferences, needs and well-being
 outcomes, providing staff with clear guidance. Well-being documentaiton celebrate achievements
 and experiences through photographs and records of meaningful activities. People participate in
 community groups, develop friendships and maintain independence. Care staff support
 communication, choice, decision-making and the promotion of Welsh language.

 Care and support is good. People receive safe, person-centred care from staff who know them well
 and promote independence while protecting their rights and safety. Staff have appropriate training
 enabling them to provide effective support. Robust risk assessments, medicines management and
 monitoring systems help maintain positive outcomes for people.

 The environment is good as people live in a safe, comfortable and well-maintained environment
that supports independence and social engagement. The sensory room, communal areas and
enhanced garden provide meaningful opportunities for relaxation, activities and interaction.
Bedrooms reflect personal preferences. Planned improvement which includes accessibility and fire
safety works will further improve outcomes.

Leadership and management are excellent. The registered manager has strengthened oversight,
quality assurance and service development. Staff described management as approachable,
supportive and responsive. Effective supervision, appraisal and team meetings promote
accountability and learning. Feedback informs improvements, while recognition schemes support
morale. Key-worker reviews ensure care remains personalised and responsive to changing needs.

source_index.name: Willowbrook House Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Willowbrook House Nursing Home is in a suburb of Cardiff, with local amenities close by. People
 experience good well-being outcomes because the service provides consistency of care from a
 dedicated care team. People form strong bonds with care staff, who know them well. The residents’
 committee regularly meets with service leaders. People’s voices are informing and shaping service
 development.
 People experience a good standard of care and support and are complimentary of the service they
 receive. Most daily outcomes are met. The service is continuing to strengthen how they deliver care
 in-line with people’s preferences and needs, and ensuring daily records are an accurate account of
 the care delivered. People access healthcare professionals and medications are well managed.
 The environment is good, which supports people’s daily outcomes. It is clean, comfortable and
 decorated to a high standard. Access to well-kempt outdoors spaces, and ample communal areas
 supports well-being.
 Leadership and management is good. Since the last inspection the provider has enhanced the
 governance systems with mostly good effect. Organisational structure, responsibilities and
 accountability is clear. The responsible individual (RI) is accountable for the quality monitoring of
 the service. The RI and governance team are taking prompt and effective steps to strengthen their
 processes to address matters identified at inspection.

source_index.name: Ystrad Fechan
source_index.provider: Rhondda Cynon Taff County Borough Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Ystrad Fechan is a Local Authority respite service for adults with a learning disability and
 associated needs, located centrally in Treorchy. It is co-located on a site with another Local
 Authority service, being based in the smaller bungalow building.


 Well-being is good because people are supported to make choices, maintain independence and
 achieve outcomes which are important to them. Strong person-centred planning, meaningful
 activities and positive risk-taking help people enjoy their respite experiences. Care and support is
 good because people receive personalised care from skilled care staff who understand their needs
 and preferences. Good safeguarding, medication management and infection prevention
 arrangements help keep people safe and well. The environment is good because people stay in a
 comfortable, welcoming and well-maintained setting which promotes independence and meets a
 wide range of needs. Leadership and management is good because leaders provide effective
 oversight and continue to drive improvement. Strong governance, quality assurance and learning
 arrangements support positive outcomes for people, while a well-trained staff team delivers
 consistent care.

source_index.name: Zoar Care Home
source_index.summary:
Zoar is a residential home in Tonypandy, providing care and support for up to 30 people.


 People experience good well-being outcomes and are supported by care staff who know them well
 and promote their dignity, choice and independence. Feedback from people and their
 representatives is positive, with many describing the service as caring, welcoming and supportive.

 Care and support is good. People receive personalised care from care staff who understand their
 needs, preferences and routines. The service benefits from detailed care planning systems,
 effective safeguarding arrangements and good systems for managing medication and infection
 prevention and control.

 The environment is good. People live in a clean, comfortable and personalised home with access
to communal areas that support social interaction and well-being. Systems are in place to maintain
equipment and promote safety, and the provider has plans to further enhance parts of the
environment.

Leadership and management are good. Staff speak positively about the support they receive and
governance systems provide effective oversight of the service. Leaders recognise opportunities to
further strengthen practice and demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement.

actions.success_outcome: People's choices are respected in practice and applicable decision records remain coherent.

actions.title: Test the local nutrition & hydration control
actions.why: 59 of 71 archived reports mention this topic; 1 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review nutritional and hydration risks, weight trends, meal preferences and escalation when needs change; assess the dining experience with residents.
actions.assurance_evidence: Risk screening, monitoring, referrals and resident feedback
actions.local_test: Observe a meal and compare preferences, monitoring records and escalation arrangements.
actions.success_outcome: People describe a suitable dining experience and changing needs receive documented follow-up.

actions.title: Test the local infection prevention control
actions.why: 60 of 71 archived reports mention this topic; 0 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Check infection-control practice, cleaning assurance and staff competence. Follow up audit exceptions and verify that practical supplies and routines are effective.
actions.assurance_evidence: IPC audit, cleaning checks and competency records
actions.local_test: Observe agreed cleaning and hygiene routines alongside the local audit evidence.
actions.success_outcome: Routines work in practice and audit exceptions are corrected and rechecked.

actions.title: Test the local environment & fire safety control
actions.why: 71 of 71 archived reports mention this topic; 7 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review fire and premises safety, servicing, accessibility and environmental risks; verify outstanding maintenance actions and person-specific evacuation arrangements.
actions.assurance_evidence: Safety checks, servicing, maintenance log and evacuation plans
actions.local_test: Walk the premises and trace sampled safety or maintenance exceptions to verification.
actions.success_outcome: Identified hazards receive appropriate follow-up and checks reflect actual conditions.

actions.title: Test the local welsh language & culture control
actions.why: 71 of 71 archived reports mention this topic; 0 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Assess the Welsh language active offer and cultural needs proactively, including how preferences are identified and acted upon; do not equate no requests with adequate provision.
actions.assurance_evidence: Language preferences, active-offer arrangements and accessible information
actions.local_test: Ask how language preferences are identified and observe the active offer in practice.
actions.success_outcome: People can access the agreed language and cultural support, not merely a recorded preference.

actions.title: Test the local meaningful activity & community control
actions.why: 71 of 71 archived reports mention this topic; 1 include matching published action rows (possibly historical). Use both positive practice and weaknesses as learning material, not a prediction about your home.
actions.suggested_action: Review opportunities for personally meaningful activity, relationships and community participation, using resident outcomes rather than activity counts alone.
actions.assurance_evidence: Resident goals, participation records and feedback
actions.local_test: Discuss meaningful goals with residents and compare participation records with experience.
actions.success_outcome: People describe opportunities that matter to them and feedback shapes future support.

limitations: This is a fixed all-data period cohort, not a dashboard-filter cohort. Only each service's latest archived report is included; this is not the complete historical inspection series or a trend in care quality. Early empty periods must not be interpreted as an absence of historical inspections: earlier reports are outside this latest-only archive.

Monthly membership uses reportPublishedActualDate, not the inspection visit or report issue date. Visit start/end, issue and publication are distinct. Empty months mean no latest archived report was published in that month, not that CIW did no inspections.

Ratings are the exact four published directory-snapshot theme values. Their effective dates are not independently auditable and cannot be assumed to match the historical publication month. Missing ratings and missing reports are not evidence of poor care. No overall quality score is calculated.

Positive wording and Improvement wording are automated search labels, not independent CIW findings. Topic counts mean reports mentioning a topic, not failures; topics and evidence sets overlap and must not be added together.

Published action-table rows can be historical or Achieved. New and Reviewed describe status words published in the source, not validation today. Missing status means unknown, not unresolved. Category counts are not counts of current failures or confirmed enforcement notices.

Excerpts and official summaries retain extracted wording and PDF page provenance. Layout changes and damaged characters can occur; the archived PDF is authoritative. Representative examples are not an exhaustive account or a prevalence estimate.
Public latest-report URLs can change after this snapshot. Use the linked local archived PDF to verify the captured evidence; the external source link establishes its CIW origin.

Management controls and the illustrative learning workflow are assistant-suggested local learning prompts, not CIW requirements, legal advice, clinical advice or an accreditation assessment. Validate applicability with appropriate local leads.

CareLens Cymru is independent and not an official CIW product. The Haven has no extracted notice; the general CIW copyright page provides Crown-material reuse permission. Source links and attribution are retained.

source_index.name: 59 Beechley Road
source_index.summary:
59 Beechley Road is a residential home with individual apartments for up to seven people with
 complex needs. It is located close to the town of Wrexham with transport links to access the local
 and wider community.

 Wellbeing is excellent because people are empowered to have control over their lives. They are
 supported extensively to understand, communicate and make choices. People have made
 significant improvements in their physical, mental and emotional wellbeing. They achieve their
 outcomes which are celebrated. People benefit from positive and trusting relationships with others
 and are proactively protected from harm.

 Care and support is excellent because people experience high-quality care and support from staff.
 Comprehensive person-centred plans are tailored to their individual needs. People, relatives,
 independent advocates, staff and relevant professionals are involved in plans, reviews and their
contributions are valued.

People live in a good, low stimulus environment which adapts to suit their complex, sensory and
changing needs. Arrangements are made for people to access outdoor spaces within the local and
wider community.

Leadership and management of the service is excellent. A highly skilled, motivated and committed
staff team are very well supported and have opportunities for learning, development and promotion.
They feel valued, included and find their work both rewarding and enjoyable. The responsible
individual (RI) and manager have robust oversight ensuring a high-quality service for all.
Opportunities are actively sought to share best practice, lessons are learnt and a strong positive
and compassionate culture is promoted.

source_index.name: Ael-y-Bryn
source_index.summary:
People living at Ael-y-Bryn experience positive outcomes and benefit from warm, caring
