 relationships with staff who know them well. Staff promote people's wellbeing, independence and
 quality of life, and people told us they feel safe and supported. Relatives spoke positively about the
 care provided and described improvements in people's confidence, mobility, social engagement
 and overall wellbeing since moving into the service. People are supported to maintain relationships
 that are important to them and to make choices about their daily lives.

 A particular strength of the service is its commitment to meaningful occupation and social
 engagement. People benefit from a varied programme of activities and opportunities to participate
 in community life, helping them remain active and connected to others. The service also provides a
 comfortable and homely environment. Ongoing investment and planned improvements to further
 enhance dementia-friendly features demonstrate a commitment to supporting people's
 independence and helping them navigate their surroundings with confidence.

 Staff work collaboratively to meet people's needs and promote positive outcomes. Effective
 leadership supports a positive culture within the service and a commitment to continuous
 improvement. Quality assurance systems are in place to monitor the quality of care and support
 provided. These could be strengthened further to ensure matters affecting people's day-to-day
 experiences, such as meal choices, are identified and acted upon as early as possible.

source_index.name: Alexandra House
source_index.summary:
People experience good well-being outcomes; they are treated with dignity and respect and have
 activities available to them. People are supported to stay as healthy as possible, with systems in
 place to protect people in an environment that meets their needs. People are treated as individuals
 and can live their lives how they wish.

 Care and support are good. Detailed care documentation is in place to support people’s needs. The
 service has good systems to safeguard people, and good systems to reduce the risk of the spread
 of infection. Care staff treat people with kindness and compassion. Personal plans are an accurate
 reflection of the individual and people receive appropriate care and support.

 The environment is good and meets people’s needs and outcomes, enhances their well-being, and
 is safe. Alexandra House is decorated throughout and has enough communal space. People’s
 rooms, as well as communal areas, are kept clean and free from hazards. People can personalise
 their rooms if they wish. The provider attempts to ensure the same people use the same rooms
when they come for respite care. Investment in the environment is evident.

The leadership and management of Alexandra House is good. The managers and Responsible
Individual (RI) have good oversight of the service. They ensure the required staff recruitment,
training, and support is undertaken and enable good-quality support and facilities are provided.

source_index.name: Ashdale Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Ashdale Nursing Home provides residential, respite and nursing care for adults. It is situated near
 the harbour town of Pembroke on the picturesque Pembrokeshire coastline.

 People experience good well-being. We found people to be safe and happy. Care staff have good
 relationships with people, relatives and professionals visiting the service. People experience good
 well-being outcomes and maintain control over many aspects of their daily lives. Care staff treat
 people with dignity and respect, encouraging them to make choices about their care and support.

 People receive good care are support. People are protected from harm and abuse. Personal plans
 are good. They provide clear guidance for staff on the care and support needs of people. People’s
 medication is safely managed.

 The environment is good. People have access to quality indoor and outdoor space which impacts
 positively on their health and wellbeing. There is clear ongoing investment into the service.

 The leadership and management are excellent. People are placed at the heart of the service by
 leaders who are visible role models. The service provider’s oversight and governance
 arrangements foster a strong positive culture which is supportive, inclusive and respectful.

source_index.name: Ashton Park Care Home
source_index.summary:
Ashton Park Care Home is situated in a residential area of Newport overlooking Belle Vue Park and
 provides accommodation and care for older adults, including people living with dementia.

 The Well-being of people living at Ashton Park Requires Improvement. People told us they felt
 safe, valued and well supported by staff, and we observed positive and respectful interactions
 throughout the inspection. However, opportunities for meaningful occupation and engagement were
 not consistently available for all residents.

 The Care and Support received is good. People received personalised care from staff who knew
 them well and understood their needs. Care plans were person-centred, risks were appropriately
assessed and managed.

The environment at the service requires improvement. Although people appeared comfortable in
their home, we identified a number of maintenance concerns, including damaged flooring and
areas requiring repair and refurbishment. Several of these issues had previously been identified by
the provider but remained unresolved. As a result, a Priority Action Notice has been issued.

Leadership and Management at Ashton Park also Requires Improvement. The service benefited
from a committed manager and staff team. However, whilst governance systems were in place,
issues identified through audits, Responsible Individual visits and improvement plans had not
always been addressed within reasonable timescales. An Area for Improvement has been identified
in relation to governance and oversight arrangements.

source_index.name: Beach Court Care Home
source_index.summary:
Beach Court is located in a quiet location of Prestatyn opposite the beach and within easy access
 of local shops and amenities. It is a homely, family-run service which provides a calm and
 welcoming environment where people can enjoy their daily lives.

 People's wellbeing is promoted effectively, as the service is committed to supporting individuals to
 maximise their independence, develop daily living skills, and participate in meaningful activities.
 Staff encourage people to remain as independent as possible and provide opportunities for them to
 engage in activities and experiences which reflect their interests, preferences, and goals.

 Care and support arrangements are of a good standard. Care documentation is detailed, regularly
 reviewed, and person-centred, providing staff with clear guidance on how to meet people's
 individual needs and preferences. People have choice and control over their daily lives and are
 supported to make decisions about what they want to do, enabling them to prioritise the things that
 matter most to them and achieve positive outcomes.

 The home is well maintained, providing a comfortable and welcoming environment. People benefit
from ongoing investment in the premises, including regular environmental improvements and
upgrades enhancing quality of life and supporting individual needs. The provider and manager
demonstrate a clear commitment to creating and maintaining a dementia-friendly environment.

The service benefits from trusted leaders and managers who promote and maintain good
standards of practice. There is a strong, shared culture within the home, with staff demonstrating
common values and a commitment to providing high-quality, person-centred care. The Responsible
Individual (RI) provides effective oversight of the home and actively monitors the quality of care and
support delivered.

source_index.name: Beatrice Webb
source_index.provider: Caerphilly County Borough Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
People at Beatrice Webb experience good wellbeing through positive, respectful relationships with
 caring staff, meaningful activities, and strong community connections. People value the garden and
 social opportunities that reduce isolation. However, care planning needs improvement to better
 identify, monitor, and review individual wellbeing outcomes, aspirations, and personal goals.

 Care and support at the service requires improvement. Although staff work effectively with health
 and social care professionals, personal plans are outdated, inconsistent risk assessment reviews,
 training compliance, record quality, consultation processes, and medication management. These
 issues reduce assurance that care remains person-centred, safe, responsive, and consistently
 monitored.
The environment is good, whereby people enjoy a clean, welcoming, and accessible environment
that supports people’s wellbeing. People enjoy personalised living spaces, comfortable communal
areas, and a valued garden that promotes social engagement. While environmental improvements
are evident, stronger governance is needed to ensure consistent health and safety monitoring, fire
safety oversight, and completion of maintenance actions.

Leadership and management at the service requires significant improvement. Inspection findings
identified widespread governance and oversight failures affecting care planning, staff supervision,
training, health and safety, recruitment, and quality assurance. Although the interim manager has
begun addressing concerns, ineffective monitoring systems have not ensured sustained
improvements, regulatory compliance, accountability, or safe, high-quality care.

source_index.name: Bethany Residential Home LTD
source_index.summary:
Bethany is a care home located in the town of Chepstow, providing personal care and support for
 older people.

 People experience good wellbeing outcomes because they are well known, understood and
 provided with care and support by a long standing and dedicated staff team. The valuable support
 people receive helps them to live well and maintain and improve upon their physical and mental
 health.

 The care and support people receive is good. Co-produced plans for people’s care and support
 detail the support required to help them achieve their outcomes and the information care workers
 require to understand what is important to them. Care workers know people well and
 have positive relationships with them. People receive support to maintain and improve their
 wellbeing with involvement from professionals.

 The environment is rated as good because people live in a warm, comfortable and welcoming
home which meets their needs. There is a feeling of homeliness and there is space for people to
spend time together or enjoy some quiet time. Regular monitoring and maintenance of the
environment ensures people are kept safe.

Leadership and management is rated as good. Audits of quality of care contain detailed analysis
and action planning to improve service quality. People and staff provide feedback which contributes
to assessing care quality and improving the service. Care workers receive effective induction,
ongoing training and development to support them to perform their roles.

source_index.name: Bevan College
source_index.summary:
Bevan College is a care home service for up to 32 people with additional learning needs, providing
 accommodation, care, education and developmental opportunities. The service supports people to
 develop independence, pursue personal goals and prepare for adulthood within a person-centred
 environment.

 People are supported to experience good well-being outcomes through positive relationships with
 care staff and access to meaningful educational, social and recreational opportunities. People are
 encouraged to share their views, participate in decision-making and develop confidence,
 independence and skills that support their personal aspirations.

 People receive good care and support informed by assessment and care planning arrangements
 which consider their individual needs, preferences and goals. Care staff have access to information
 and guidance to support consistent care delivery, whilst risk management and incident
arrangements help promote people's safety and well-being.

People benefit from a good environment that is welcoming, accessible and designed to meet their
needs. Personalised living spaces, specialist facilities, outdoor areas and opportunities for learning
and recreation support independence, participation and well-being. Maintenance and health and
safety arrangements help ensure the environment remains safe and suitable.

People are supported by good leadership and management arrangements that provide oversight of
service delivery and support continuous improvement. Quality assurance processes, workforce
development opportunities and recruitment practices contribute to a positive culture focused on
delivering safe, consistent care and positive outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Blaen y Pant
source_index.provider: Newport City Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Blaen-Y-Pant House is situated in a residential area of Newport, close to the community of Bettws.
The home is easily accessible for relatives, friends and professionals and provides accommodation
and care for older people.

Well-being is good. People told us they feel safe, valued and well supported by staff who know
them well. We observed warm and respectful interactions, opportunities for social engagement and
support that promotes people's independence, dignity and personal preferences.

Care and Support is good. People receive personalised care from staff who understand their needs
and preferences. Personal plans are detailed and reviewed regularly, helping staff provide
consistent support. People and relatives spoke positively about the care provided, and we saw
evidence of effective partnership working with healthcare professionals to promote people's health
and well-being.

The Environment is good. People live in surroundings that are safe, comfortable and well
maintained. Bedrooms are personalised and communal areas provide welcoming spaces for
relaxation and social interaction.

Leadership and Management is good. Leaders have effective systems in place to monitor the
quality of the service and drive improvement. Staff described managers as approachable,
supportive and visible. We found a positive culture within the home, with managers and staff
committed to achieving good outcomes for people and responding appropriately when
improvements are identified.

source_index.name: Blaenos House Care Home
source_index.summary:
Blaenos House is a care home in Llandovery, Carmarthenshire that provides accommodation,
 personal care and nursing care for older people, including those living with dementia.

 People experience good well-being because they are supported by kind and attentive care staff
 who know them well. People maintain important relationships and are encouraged to have choice
 and control over their daily lives.

 The care and support provided is good because people receive responsive and person-centred
 care from care staff who understand their needs and preferences. Positive partnership working with
 relatives and healthcare professionals helps support people's health, safety and wellbeing.

 People benefit from a good environment that is comfortable, welcoming and supports
 independence. The facilities available provide opportunities for social interaction, family
 involvement and meaningful engagement.

 The service benefits from good leadership and management. Managers are approachable and
 supportive and demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement.

source_index.name: Brigadoon Care Home
source_index.summary:
Brigadoon Care Home is a small, family-run service that provides a friendly and homely
 environment for people living here. The home is conveniently located close to local amenities in
 Llandudno.

 People’s wellbeing is good as they have many opportunities to socialise with others and do things
 they enjoy. People’s care and support needs are accurately reflected in risk assessments and
 personal plans, which are kept under review. Medication systems and standards of hygiene and
 infection control are mainly good.

 Care and support require improvement as the correct equipment is not in place and there is not
 enough staff to care for immobile people at night. People receive dignified and respectful care, with
 meaningful interactions with staff and their care is individually tailored to each person’s own
 individual needs.
Environment requires significant improvement as the provider has failed to act on external
professional advice and sustain compliance with the external condition of the grounds. The
environment is homely, clean and well-maintained. People are also benefitting from an ongoing
refurbishment and safety checks of the home.

Leadership and management require significant improvement. The Responsible Individual (RI) has
not ensured that effective organisational arrangements, governance systems and oversight
mechanisms are in place to support the safe and effective operation of the service. As a result,
there are shortcomings in the provider’s ability to monitor the quality of care, identify areas of
concern and drive continuous improvement.

source_index.name: Brompton Lodge limited
source_index.summary:
Brompton Lodge is an established family run residential home and provides personal care for up to
 34 people. The home is in a residential area of Rhos on Sea within easy access of the beach and
 local facilities.

 People experience good wellbeing and feel happy and safe in their home. Their rights are upheld
 and they receive timely care and support which promotes good health and well-being.

 People experience positive outcomes because care and support are delivered in accordance with
 personalised care plans that reflect their assessed needs, preferences, strengths, and aspirations.
 The provider ensures that daily routines, activities, and support arrangements are tailored to each
 person's individual circumstances, promoting choice, independence, dignity, and wellbeing.

 People live in a good environment which is nicely presented and has good facilities that meet
people’s needs. Regular upgrades ensure the accommodation and facilities are constantly
improving.

The service is managed well. People experience good continuity of care from a stable team of staff.
Staff receive a high level of support to enable them to fulfil their roles effectively. The Responsible
Individual (RI) has good oversight of the service and continuously drives up standards.

source_index.name: Brookside Care Home
source_index.summary:
Brookside Care Home is a care home based in Powys, providing care and nursing support to
 people with a range of needs.

 We identified improvement in most areas since the previous inspection. At the last inspection, we
 issued two Priority Action Notices (PANs) and five Areas for Improvement (AFIs) relating to health
 and safety, personal planning, dignity and respect, Responsible Individual (RI) oversight, and
 staffing arrangements. During this inspection, we found sufficient progress had been made to
 remove one PAN and three AFIs. The remaining PAN relating to health and safety has been
 downgraded to an AFI because improvements have reduced the level of risk to people. Whilst
 some residual health and safety concerns remain, we no longer consider people to be at significant
 or imminent risk.

 We found continued improvement in staff training arrangements. However, whilst training
 compliance has improved it remains below the standard expected. Further work is required to
 ensure personal plans are consistently person-centred, outcome focused and accurately reflect
people's needs. Therefore, these two AFIs remain open.

Overall, leaders have demonstrated commitment to improvement and the changes made since the
previous inspection are having a positive impact on people’s well-being. Ratings have improved
since the last inspection. We rate Well-being and Leadership and Management as Good. This
reflects improved wellbeing for people and strengthened governance arrangements. We rate Care
and Support and Environment as Requires Improvement because further work is needed to ensure
people’s personal plans reflect their needs and they live in an environment that fully promotes their
safety and well-being.

source_index.name: Bryn y Wawr
source_index.summary:
Bryn y Wawr is a residential Care Home providing care for 10 adults with Learning Disabilities,
 Mental Health needs and Autism. It is a charming older property set in large grounds in the centre
 of Llandeilo, a picturesque market town in the Towy Valley, Carmarthenshire.

 The well-being outcomes for people are “Excellent” as people maintain and improve upon their
 physical, mental, and emotional health because of the exemplary support they receive from staff.

 The care and support people receive is “Good” as people receive high-quality care and support
 from staff who know them well and place them at the heart of the service.

 The environment in which people live is “Good” as people benefit greatly from a well maintained
 and safe home which is suitable to their individual needs.

 The leadership and management of the service is “Excellent” as people have very high levels of
 confidence in the provider because leaders promote an exemplary positive culture that is
 supportive, inclusive and respectful.

source_index.name: Cae Glas
source_index.summary:
Cae Glas provides nursing care and support to adults with mental health needs. The three-story
 home is on the main street of Denbigh town, so people have easy access to shops, cafes and
 pubs.
 Wellbeing is good because people live a safe and healthy life, doing things they choose to do. They
 are supported to be independent and achieve their wellbeing outcomes.
 Care and support require improvement. People praise the quality of care and level of freedom they
 have living in the home; they are particularly impressed with the support staff who they describe as
 genuinely caring and kind. However, medication administration practices do not comply with
 regulatory guidance; a qualified witness is required to evidence the administration of certain drugs,
 and this does not happen. This is an area for improvement.
 The environment is good. The provider has invested in the building, making bedrooms larger and
 including en-suite shower rooms in all of them. The dining room has been redecorated and there
 are plans to improve other areas.
Leadership is good. The RI (responsible individual for the service) has a range of systems in place
to ensure continued monitoring of the service. They know what is working well and where
improvements need to be made.

source_index.name: Cartref Care Home Ltd
source_index.summary:
Cartref Care Home is a service located in the village of Henllan, near Newcastle Emlyn, providing
 care for up to 36 adults. The service supports older people, including people living with dementia,
 and promotes Welsh language and culture.

 Well-being requires improvement. People are generally positive about the care and support they
 receive and staff know people well. However, there is limited evidence people and their
 representatives are consistently involved in planning and reviewing of their care and support. Care
 records do not always reflect people's preferences, wishes and personal outcomes.

 Care and Support requires significant improvement. Concerns exist regarding care planning, risk
 assessment and the oversight of care delivery. Care records do not consistently provide assurance
 people's needs are accurately assessed, planned for and reviewed. Concerns relating to
 medication management further reduce assurance that people consistently receive safe and
 effective care.

 The Environment requires significant improvement. People do not consistently benefit from an
 environment where risks are identified and reduced. There is insufficient assurance that health and
safety arrangements, maintenance processes and environmental oversight are effective in
identifying concerns and ensuring timely action is taken to mitigate risk.

Leadership and Management requires significant improvement. Governance and oversight
arrangements have not been sufficiently effective in identifying and addressing concerns, managing
risk and driving sustained improvement across the service.

As a result of these concerns Priority Action Notices have been issued.

There has been a change in the management of the service since our last inspection. The new
manager is addressing where improvements can be made. New management arrangements are
having a positive impact.

source_index.name: Ceiriosen Bren
source_index.summary:
Ceiriosen Bren offers residential care in the Llandysul area of Ceredigion. It is in a rural setting with
 pleasant views of the surrounding countryside. It offers residential care to adults with mental health
 needs.

 Wellbeing is good. People speak positively about the service and the care they receive as they
 have highly effective working relationships with care staff.

 Care and support are excellent. People are treated with dignity and respect. They experience high-
quality care and support. Personal plans provide care staff with guidance on how to support people
safely whilst promoting choice, independence and dignity.

The environment is good. People live in an environment which is comfortable, safe and suitable for
their needs. We found communal areas were clean, tidy and well maintained.

Leadership and management are excellent. The provider seeks and values the views of people,
their relatives and care staff. People have high levels of confidence in the service because leaders
ensure there is a very strong positive culture that is supportive, inclusive and respectful.

source_index.name: Celynbrook Care Home
source_index.summary:
Celynbrook Care Home is a small service situated in the Vale of Glamorgan, with local amenities
 and attractions within easy reach. People are content, settled and receive a high standard of care
 and support from dedicated and compassionate care staff. Well-being is excellent because care
 staff know them extremely well, the provider prioritises well-being, affording people to live
 meaningful and valued lives. Care and support is excellent. People access medical professionals
 and receive effective support to maintain their physical and mental health. The service is highly
 responsive when there are changes in people’s health with admirable outcomes for people with
 complex support needs. The environment is good. People live in a nurturing atmosphere where all
 care staff and management present a united approach to delivering the best outcomes for people.

 Leadership and management is excellent because the organisational structure is stable, reliable
 and highly effective in delivering a high-quality service. Robust governance procedures provide
 highly effective oversight of the service which supports continuous improvement, staff development
 and excellent outcomes for people. Service leaders are held in high regard by stakeholders, and
 they work well with visiting professionals and people’s representatives to support the very best
 outcomes for people using the service.

source_index.name: Clayford
source_index.summary:
Clayford Farm Care Home provides residential care for up to five younger adults with learning
 disabilities. It is a trust, managed on a not-for-profit basis. It is situated in a rural setting near Wiston
 in the picturesque county of Pembrokeshire.

 People experience good well-being. People speak positively about the service and the care they
 receive. They have highly effective working relationships with care staff. People are supported to
 remain as healthy as possible. The service links closely with health and medical professionals.

 People receive good care and support. Care staff involve people and where appropriate, their
 relatives or representatives in care planning and reviews. People are supported by highly skilled
 care staff with an excellent understanding of their individual needs and preferences.

 The environment is good. People told us they were happy with their surroundings and feel
 comfortable living at the service. The atmosphere within the home is calm, relaxed and welcoming.
The leadership and management are excellent. The service benefits from outstanding leadership
and management arrangements which support positive outcomes for people. Leaders have an
excellent understanding of the service and have established high-quality systems to review quality,
monitor performance and identify areas for improvement.

source_index.name: Cysgod Y Coed Ltd
source_index.summary:
People living at Cysgod Y Coed receive good-quality, person-centred care in a warm, homely, and
 supportive environment. Well-being is rated Good, reflecting the positive experiences of people
 who told us they feel safe, valued, and well supported by caring staff who knew them well and
 respect their choices, preferences, and independence. People are supported to exercise choice
 and control in their daily lives, maintain important relationships, and communicate in Welsh, helping
 to promote their cultural identity and sense of belonging.

 Care and Support is rated Good. Care arrangements are tailored to people's assessed needs and
 regularly reviewed to ensure support remains responsive to changing circumstances. A stable and
 experienced staff team promote continuity of care and demonstrate a good understanding of the
 people they support.

 Environment is rated Good. The home is clean, comfortable, and well maintained, providing a
 range of communal and private spaces that enables people to socialise, relax, and maintain their
independence. Leadership and Management is rated Good. Strong leadership, effective
governance, and visible management oversight contributes to a positive culture within the home.

source_index.name: Dan-y-Bryn Care Home
source_index.summary:
Dan-y-Bryn House is a residential care home that provides care for adults who need support for
 their rehabilitation and/or behavioural problems within a community setting. Individuals can be
 supported for a range of care needs including learning disability and mental health needs.

 Well-being is good because people are supported to live fulfilling lives, pursue their interests and
 achieve goals that are important to them. Care staff take time to understand what matters to people
 and support them to access opportunities that promote happiness, confidence and inclusion.

 Care and support is good because people experience care and support that is responsive to their
 individual needs, promotes their wellbeing and helps them remain safe while participating in
 activities and relationships that are important to them

 The environment is good because people live in a home that is safe, welcoming and suited to their
 needs. Effective health and safety arrangements are in place; environmental risks are appropriately
 managed and there is clear evidence of ongoing investment and improvement.
Leadership and management is good because people benefit from a service with a positive,
person-centred culture. Leaders demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement. While
some records require further development, people receive good care and support, and
improvements are underway to strengthen oversight and governance.

source_index.name: Daniel House
source_index.summary:
Daniel House provides an exceptionally caring and person-centred service where individuals
 receive high-quality support from a dedicated care staff team. Care staff know individuals well and
 promote dignity, respect, independence and choice. Families spoke highly of the service and were
 very positive about the care and support provided. Individuals appeared happy, settled and
 comfortable in their individual flats and enjoyed warm, positive interactions with care staff. Care
 and support provision is excellent.

 Well-being outcomes are excellent. Individuals are supported to make choices, pursue their
 interests and participate in meaningful activities tailored to their preferences and abilities. Care staff
 demonstrate a detailed understanding of individual needs and support people to achieve positive
 outcomes and maintain fulfilling lives.

 The environment is good. The home and individual flats are clean, comfortable and homely,
 providing a settled and welcoming atmosphere. While some areas would benefit from
 modernisation and freshening up, maintenance records and plans evidenced ongoing and
 proposed improvement work, demonstrating ongoing investment within the service.

 Leadership and management is good. Managers are visible within the service and demonstrate
 commitment to supporting individuals and care staff. Governance arrangements are effective. Care
 staff spoke positively about the support they receive and described feeling valued by the
 management team.

source_index.name: Dol Y Felin
source_index.provider: Carmarthenshire County Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
People who have made Dol y Felin their home receive a good standard of care. Everyone we
 spoke with has high levels of confidence in the service.

 People experience good wellbeing because of the relationships they have with the people
 important to them and the staff team. This, together with the range of opportunities to do things that
 matter to them mean their days are generally meaningful and they are treated with dignity and
 respect.

 Care and support is rated as good because the team is led by an experienced and dedicated
 manager who is supported by a deputy and team of staff who share the values of the service and
 strive to provide individualised and person-centred care and support. Detailed personal plans help
 to inform and direct care and the planned improvements will enhance this further.
The environment is rated as good because standards of cleanliness are high and whilst some
areas would benefit from updating it is mostly as homely and comfortable as possible.

Leadership and management is rated as good because the values set by the manager are
embedded into practice. The manager is very visible throughout the service and has a good
knowledge of the people cared for, their families and the staff team. Some improvements to the
internal auditing processes would enhance this further.

source_index.name: Dolywern
source_index.summary:
Dolywern Care Home provides accommodation and care for people with physical disabilities,
 learning disabilities, autism and nursing care needs. People experience positive outcomes and the
 service has made significant progress since previous inspections, with improvements evident
 across all inspection themes.

 People have good well-being outcomes because they are treated with dignity and respect and have
 opportunities to influence decisions about their lives and the running of the service. They benefit
 from a calm, welcoming atmosphere, meaningful activities and improved access to outdoor spaces.

 People receive good care and support from enough staff who know them well. Care planning,
 record keeping, safeguarding and medication arrangements have improved. Some records still
 need strengthening, but the manager is monitoring these areas and taking action to sustain
 progress.

 The home provides a pleasant environment. People are involved in decoration plans and enjoy
 gardening, social events and community activities. Some environmental work remains outstanding,
 but this does not currently impact people’s outcomes.

 Governance and quality assurance systems are stronger. The registered manager, who is also the
newly proposed Responsible Individual (RI), is visible and staff feel supported. Thorough audits,
practice observations and feedback systems help identify issues and drive improvement, although
these arrangements need further embedding to demonstrate long term positive impact and
sustained improvements across the service.

source_index.name: Elliots Hill Care Ltd - Elliots Hill RCH
source_index.summary:
Elliots Hill is a care home for up to 23 adults in Pembrokeshire. The service supports people with a
 range of needs, including older people, people with learning disabilities and mental health needs.
 People live in a homely rural environment and are supported by a staff team who know them well
 and provide person-centred care.

 People experience good well-being because people maintain important relationships and make
 choices about their daily lives. Staff understand people's individual preferences and routines, and
 people appear comfortable and relaxed.

 The care and support provided is good because people receive personalised care from staff who
 understand their needs, preferences and goals. Care planning is outcome focused, healthcare
 needs are supported and effective systems help ensure medication management and infection
 prevention arrangements remain safe.

 The environment is good because people live in a comfortable, personalised setting that supports
 their needs and well-being. The service provides suitable facilities, equipment and outdoor spaces.
 The provider continues to invest in environmental improvements which benefit people living at the
 service.
The leadership and management of the service is good because managers have developed
effective governance arrangements, use digital systems to support care planning and quality
assurance, and demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement. Regular audits and quality
reviews provide assurance that the service is monitored effectively.

source_index.name: Erwhir Care Home
source_index.summary:
Erwhir is a care home located in a quiet residential area of Carmarthen that provides good quality
 care. People experience positive well-being outcomes because they are supported by a caring and
 dedicated staff team who know them well. Staff develop warm and meaningful relationships with
 people and promote choice, dignity and independence. The atmosphere throughout the service is
 welcoming, relaxed and homely, helping people feel comfortable, valued and secure.

 People benefit from good quality care and support which reflects their individual needs and
 preferences. Staff work well with health and social care professionals to support people's health,
 well-being and independence. People enjoy meaningful activities, social opportunities and time
 spent with others, which contributes positively to their well-being.

 People live in a good environment that offers a choice of spaces in which to spend their time. Well-
 furnished communal areas provide opportunities for both social engagement and quiet relaxation,
 and bedrooms are personalised to reflect people's interests and preferences.

 Leadership and management are good. Leaders demonstrate a reflective, open and transparent
 approach and continue to strengthen governance, auditing and oversight arrangements. Overall,
 people benefit from a service that promotes their well-being, safety and quality of life.

source_index.name: Fairfield House
source_index.summary:
Fairfield House is located in Llandaff, Cardiff, and provides residential care and support for adults
 with a learning disability and/or autistic people who may present with behaviours that challenge
 services, as well as those with complex needs.

 Well-being is excellent because people experience exceptional, life-enhancing outcomes. They are
 empowered to make meaningful choices, achieve ambitious goals and maximise their
 independence. As a result, they enjoy improved well-being, strong relationships, greater community
 inclusion and enriched, self-directed lives.

 Care and support is good because people receive safe, personalised support which helps them
 stay healthy, maintain their independence and achieve what matters to them. Care is regularly
 reviewed and adapted to meet changing needs, and effective health, safeguarding, medication and
safety arrangements help people to live well and achieve positive outcomes

The environment is good because people benefit from an environment which supports their safety,
comfort and well-being. The home offers a variety of facilities enabling people to spend their time in
ways which are meaningful to them, while robust health and safety systems and an established
improvement plan provide confidence the environment will continue to be maintained and
enhanced.

Leadership and management is good because the service is well run, staff are appropriately trained
and supported, and robust quality assurance arrangements drive continuous improvement.

source_index.name: Gardens Care Home
source_index.summary:
Gardens Care Home is situated in Neath within walking distance of community facilities such as
 cafes, restaurants and parks. The service provides person-centred care and support to people.

 Well-being is good and people are actively involved in decisions about their lives. They are
 supported to maintain their health and well-being and participate in activities that are important to
 them.

 Care and support is good. There are thorough personal plans in place which are reviewed regularly
 with people and reflect their individual needs, preferences and aspirations.

 The environment is good as it is welcoming and homely and supports people's wellbeing.
 Bedrooms are personalised and communal areas are well maintained and inviting. Environmental
 improvements had been completed since the previous inspection, including redecoration, new
 flooring and replacement furnishings.

 Leadership and management of the service is good. The manager and responsible individual (RI)
 provide effective oversight and have implemented robust governance systems that drive
 continuous improvement. Care staff consistently described the management team as approachable
and supportive.

source_index.name: Hallmark Greenhill Manor Luxury Care Home
source_index.summary:
Greenhill Manor is a purpose-built care home on the outskirts of Merthyr Tydfil. The service
 supports people with nursing needs, those living with dementia, younger people living with a
 physical disability and people who require support to manage their social care needs.


 People experience excellent outcomes across all areas of the service. Staff place a strong
 emphasis on promoting meaningful lives, maintaining important relationships and supporting
 people to exercise choice and control over their daily lives. People and relatives consistently
 describe the service positively and told us they feel safe, respected and valued.


 Care and support are excellent. Staff know people exceptionally well and provide highly
 personalised care that promotes positive outcomes. People benefit from strong partnership working
 with healthcare professionals, innovative approaches to care planning and responsive support
 which enhances their health, wellbeing and quality of life.


 The environment is excellent. People benefit from high quality facilities that actively enhance their
 wellbeing, independence and opportunities for meaningful engagement. Extensive indoor and
 outdoor spaces offer opportunities for recreation, socialisation and meaningful occupation.


 Leadership and management are excellent. Strong governance systems, visible leadership and a
 culture of continuous improvement ensure people consistently experience positive outcomes and
 high-quality care. Leaders promote learning, development and innovation while maintaining a clear
 focus on delivering person-centred care.

source_index.name: Hengoed Court Care Home
source_index.summary:
Hengoed Court Care Home is a large nursing care home situated in Winch Wen, Swansea. The
 home benefits from extensive grounds, scenic views over Swansea Bay and access to its own
 eight-acre nature park. The service provides nursing, complex nursing, palliative, end-of-life and
 respite care for up to 114 adults aged 55 years and over.

 Well-being is excellent because people are supported to live the lives they want to live. We saw
 clear evidence of improved outcomes, meaningful experiences and strong relationships. People
 told us they feel safe and listened to, while professionals recognised the service's innovative and
 person-centred approach.

 Care and support is good because people receive care that is responsive to their individual needs.
 Staff know people well, monitor their health closely and work effectively with families and
 professionals when concerns arise. Robust systems help ensure people are safe and receive the
support they need at the right time.

The environment is excellent because people benefit from a home that enhances their wellbeing
and quality of life. A wide range of personalised living spaces, exceptional outdoor facilities and
ongoing investment in the environment provide people with choice, comfort and opportunities to do
what matters to them. Strong safety arrangements help ensure people can enjoy their surroundings
with confidence.

Leadership and management is excellent because there is a clear commitment to providing high-
quality care. Effective oversight, investment in new ideas and a strong staff culture ensure people
benefit from a service that is responsive, ambitious and focused on achieving positive outcomes.

source_index.name: Heol Don Care Home
source_index.summary:
Heol Don Care home is based in Cardiff and can accommodate 78 people with a range of nursing
 and personal care needs. At this time of inspection, the service did not have a Responsible
 Individual (RI) or general manager in post. An application for a new RI has recently been submitted.
 Recruitment arrangements were also underway to appoint a new General Manager registered with
 Social Care Wales (SCW).

 People receive good quality care and strong support from a friendly, stable, and experienced staff
 team. There are sufficient staff available to meet people's needs, with agency workers used to
 cover any staffing shortages when required. However, we identified some occasions where people
 experienced delays in receiving assistance. Overall, wellbeing outcomes for people are good, as
 the staffing arrangements enable individuals to benefit from compassionate, dedicated, and
 person-centred care delivered by a committed staff team.

 Leadership and management are strong, with the Clinical Manager maintaining a visible presence
 and providing effective day-to-day leadership and support. Robust governance and quality
assurance systems help ensure care reflects people's wishes, preferences and outcomes. Staff are
well supported through training, development opportunities and clear guidance, and told us they
feel valued by the management team. Feedback from relatives, representatives and staff is
consistently positive, with the service described as “excellent” and “staff are so very good, we
occasionally have to wait but lately that has improved a lot”.
People live in excellent, well-maintained and welcoming accommodation. The environment is
attractively decorated and features pleasant outdoor spaces that provide opportunities for
relaxation and enjoyment.

source_index.name: Llanrhaeadr Hall
source_index.summary:
Llanrhaeadr Hall is a care home for older people, some of whom have dementia care needs. The
 service is provided in a beautiful, characterful listed building with spacious grounds.
 People’s wellbeing is excellent because they are treated with dignity and respect, supported to
 make choices, and enjoy a wide range of tailored, meaningful activities.
 Care and support is good as people are consistently treated with kindness, empathy and
 compassion. Comprehensive assessments and care planning ensure people receive support in
 their preferred way. We saw examples of excellent care, including respect for people’s differences
 and language, and support to do what matters to them. Staff regularly go above and beyond. The
 manager is reviewing care planning and reviews to strengthen outcome-focused practice.
 The environment is good. The home and grounds provide ample space, giving people choice about
 how and where they spend their time. The environment is safe, well maintained, and continually
 reviewed for improvement.
 Leadership and management is good because the RI (responsible individual for the service) has
 established systems in place that provide good oversight of the whole operation. Effective oversight
 identifies strengths and areas for development. Recruitment includes robust vetting, and staff
 retention is excellent because employees feel supported and valued. We also saw strong examples
 of reflective learning and the sharing of good practice with other providers.

source_index.name: Llys Newydd Care Home
source_index.summary:
Llys Newydd is a residential home on the outskirts of Ammanford. Well-being is rated as good
 because people receive a person-centred service, that enables them to achieve their health and
 well-being outcomes. People have developed positive relationships with the caring staff team.

 Care and support is rated as good because people receive an effective service from a team of
 consistent and familiar staff. Care workers are guided by accurate and individualised personal
 plans that enable them to meet people’s needs.

 The environment is rated as good because people are relaxed and comfortable throughout the
 home. Improvements have been made to the building and the provider has a clear plan to continue
 these to enhance people’s well-being.

 Leadership and management is rated as good because the provider has effective oversight of the
 service. The onsite leadership team ensure people receive reliable and highly valued care from a
 team of dedicated care workers who are well supported by their managers.

source_index.name: Maes Y Bryn
source_index.summary:
Maes Y Bryn is a small residential care home that provides accommodation and support for people
 with a range of needs such as learning disabilities and autism.

 We rated well-being as excellent because people are supported to develop skills, maintain
 important relationships and participate in activities that are meaningful to them. We saw strong
 examples of people achieving personal goals and experiencing positive outcomes.

 We rated care and support as excellent because people receive highly personalised care and
 support from a knowledgeable and committed team of care staff. Care staff understand people
 exceptionally well and promote choice, independence and well-being.

 We rated the environment as excellent. People live in an environment that reflects their individual
 needs and preferences. Care staff adapt the environment thoughtfully to promote emotional well-
 being, safety and independence. The service is welcoming, well maintained and designed around
 the needs of the people living there.
Leadership and management is rated as excellent and arrangements are highly effective. Care
staff receive good support and supervision and leaders promote a positive culture focused on
achieving the best outcomes for people. Governance systems are robust and support ongoing
improvement.

source_index.name: Maes Y Vaynor
source_index.summary:
Maes Y Vaynor is a small residential home for four adults. The service focuses on supporting
 people to become as independent as possible by building on their strengths and developing new
 skills.
 Wellbeing is good because people live their lives how they wish with choice and control. People
 achieve their outcomes becoming more confident and independent.
 Care and support is excellent because people are extensively supported to live well and achieve
 self-directed outcomes. People are proud of their achievements and praise staff highly for their
 excellent support.
 The environment is good as it is spacious and provides people with the room to live how they wish
 and the privacy they need. Communal areas need decorating and carpets need replacing, but this
 is something the service has already taken steps to address.
 Leadership and management is good. The manager and RI (responsible individual for the service)
 know the service well because they work closely with staff and residents, routinely carry out audits
 of records and procedures, and check the quality of care. They know what is working well and
 where improvements need to be made.

source_index.name: Maes-y-felin Care Home Ltd
source_index.summary:
Maesyfelin is a homely care service in a rural location on the outskirts of Llanybydder. It is a close
 knit community and most people living at the service are from the local area. Welsh language
 provision is embedded within the service with many of the staff and people preferring to converse in
 Welsh.

 People benefit from positive wellbeing outcomes as they are treated with respect and dignity from
 staff that know them well. They have choice and control over their day to day lives and are
 supported to spend their day as they wish.

 Care and support is good, care staff are guided by person centred plans which are accessible to
 staff and kept up to date. People’s health is promoted and the staff work closely with external
 health and social care professionals to ensure people have the right support when they need it.
 The environment supports people living at Maesyfelin by providing a safe, comfortable and
attractive place for people to live which supports the achievement of positive well-being outcomes.
Improvements to the environment are ongoing and the building and contents are well maintained.

Leadership and management is good and the Responsible Individual (RI) has good oversight of
the service. There is a positive management culture, staff feel supported and people and their
families feel listened to. The service is well led and demonstrates a commitment to continuous
improvement.

source_index.name: Magnolia House Residential Home LTD
source_index.summary:
Magnolia House provides residential care to older people. It is based close to local amenities such
 as a local supermarket and public houses. There is a leisure centre and country park nearby.

 People are supported by care staff who know them well. Many people are supported to achieve
 good wellbeing outcomes, with access to choices about their meals, activities and where they
 spend their time. Whilst we found personal plans lacked clear detail for care staff to follow, they
 know people well and overall, a good standard of care and support is provided. Required
 improvements to personal plans will help strengthen and maintain this standard and ensure people
 receive the right care at the right time.

 The home is clean, homely and welcoming, with access to facilities and specialist equipment to
 support people. People have comfortable bedrooms which they can personalise to suit their
individual tastes. They live in a good environment to meet their needs.

The oversight of the service is inconsistent, and we found several areas which require improvement
to ensure any risks are identified and promptly managed. The responsible individual (RI) needs to
ensure systems and policies are in place to strengthen oversight of the service.

source_index.name: Milford House
source_index.provider: Pembrokeshire County Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Milford House is a residential care home in Milford Haven. Well-being is rated as excellent because
 people receive a highly person-centred service, that enables them to achieve their health and well-
 being outcomes. People have developed extremely positive relationships with the skilled and
 passionate staff.

 Care and support is rated as excellent because people receive care and support from a team of
 well-informed and friendly care workers. Care workers are guided by accurate and outcome
 focused personal plans that enable them to successfully meet people’s needs.

 The environment needs improvement. The provider has resolved the health and safety issues
 identified previously; upgrades have been made to the home and the provider intends to continue
 these to further enhance people’s well-being.

 Leadership and management is rated as good because the provider has good oversight of the
 service. The leadership ensure people receive high quality care from a team of dedicated and
 motivated care workers who receive effective support from their managers.

source_index.name: Morgannwg House
source_index.summary:
Morgannwg House Nursing Home provides care and support for up to 20 adults aged 18 and over,
 including older people and those living with a diagnosis of dementia. The home is conveniently
 located near Brecon town centre, enabling people to access local amenities and participate in
 community activities.

 People experience positive well-being outcomes. They are treated with dignity and respect and are
 supported to make informed choices about their daily lives.

 Care and Support is person-centred and of good quality. Staff understand people’s needs well and
 respond to changes in their health and wellbeing promptly.

 People’s care and support plans are made with them, or a representative and or professionals
 involved. However, we found these are not regularly reviewed as they should quarterly to meet
 regulations. We found this does not have a detrimental impact on people. The manager
 acknowledges the need to improve the timely review of this area and has plans in place to address
 it. We will monitor progress at the next inspection.
The home environment is safe, warm, clean and homely and supports people’s comfort and
independence. Safety checks are completed and bedrooms are personalised and meet people’s
needs.

Leadership and oversight arrangements are effective. The Responsible Individual (RI) visits
regularly and seeks feedback from people using the service to support ongoing improvement.
Leadership and governance promote a positive culture through audits, feedback and regular
review. Staff feel supported and valued in their roles through training, supervision and guidance,
enabling them to provide safe, consistent and responsive care.

source_index.name: Mumbles Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Well-being is rated good because people reported feeling safe, happy and well supported.
 Relatives consistently described people as settled, respected and treated with dignity. Meaningful
 activities, family involvement and person-centred support promoted positive wellbeing outcomes.
 Welsh language provision was developing but not consistently evidenced through an active offer
 approach.

 Care and Support is rated good as people received personalised care that generally met their
 assessed needs. Care planning, safeguarding and medication management arrangements were
 effective, supported by positive feedback from relatives and professionals. Minor opportunities were
 identified to strengthen person-centred information and some care records.

 Environment is also rated good because people lived in a generally clean, welcoming and well-
 maintained home with appropriate facilities, equipment and safety systems. Relatives and
 professionals spoke positively about the environment. However, the prolonged lift outage created
 risks relating to mobility, dignity and emergency evacuation, and Long Term Care Team (LTCT)
 findings highlighted environmental and equipment concerns requiring ongoing monitoring.
Finally, Leadership and Management is rated good because leadership was stable and well
regarded by staff, relatives and professionals. Governance arrangements included audits, quality
reviews, RI oversight and staff supervision. Improvement plans had been implemented in response
to LTCT findings. However, quality assurance systems had not consistently identified some
environmental and safety concerns, indicating a need to strengthen audit effectiveness, training
oversight and governance assurance.

source_index.name: Options Pen-Y-Bryn
source_index.summary:
Pen Y Bryn is an adult care home that delivers excellent outcomes for people with learning
 disabilities and complex communication needs. People enjoy an excellent quality of life because
 care staff know them exceptionally well and provide highly personalised support that promotes
 choice, independence and well-being. People are treated with dignity and respect, supported to
 express their views, and encouraged to participate in meaningful activities and community
 opportunities that reflect their interests and aspirations.

 People receive excellent care and support tailored to their individual needs and personal outcomes.
 Robust assessment, admission and care planning processes ensure support is responsive, person-
 centred, and promotes safety, health and quality of life. Effective safeguarding arrangements help
 people feel safe and secure, while care staff support them to maximise independence and achieve
 positive outcomes.
The environment is excellent, safe, comfortable and maintained to a high standard.
Accommodation is personalised and adapted to meet individual needs, promoting a sense of
belonging. Communal and outdoor spaces encourage relaxation, social interaction and meaningful
engagement, while ongoing investment demonstrates a commitment to continuous improvement.

Leadership and management are excellent. Robust governance, quality assurance and oversight
arrangements drive continuous improvement and ensure consistently outstanding care. Managers
promote a positive culture centred on people, and care staff receive excellent support, supervision
and development to achieve the best possible outcomes.

source_index.name: Options Phoenix House
source_index.summary:
People living at Phoenix House benefit from an excellent quality service where they feel safe,
 respected, and valued. People are encouraged to share their feelings and wishes, make choices
 and take an active role in decisions about their lives. Positive relationships with care staff help
 people feel secure and supported, and they have access to healthcare, community activities and
 opportunities that reflect their interests and personal goals. This helps people develop confidence,
 maintain their independence, and achieve positive outcomes.

 People receive excellent care and support from a skilled care staff team who know them well and
 understand their individual needs. Assessment and admission processes help ensure the service
 can meet people's needs, and care staff provide consistent support that promotes their safety,
 health, and well-being. Safeguarding arrangements are robust, and care planning focuses on
 supporting people to achieve their goals and live meaningful lives.
People live in a good quality environment that is clean, safe, and well maintained. Individual flats
are personalised to reflect people's individual needs and support their independence, helping them
feel comfortable in their home. The service provides suitable communal and private spaces where
people can relax, socialise and take part in activities they enjoy. Regular maintenance and health
and safety checks help ensure the environment remains welcoming, safe, and appropriate to
people's needs.

The service benefits from excellent leadership and management. Extremely effective governance,
monitoring, and quality assurance arrangements provide robust oversight of the service and
support continuous improvement. Managers are committed to achieving the best possible
outcomes for people and promote a positive, person-centred culture throughout the service. Robust
recruitment processes, alongside regular training, supervision and support, ensure care staff have
the skills, knowledge, and confidence to meet people’s needs effectively. The Responsible
Individual (RI)and management team maintain comprehensive oversight of the service, helping to
ensure people consistently receive an extremely high standard of care and support.

source_index.name: Pen Bryn
source_index.summary:
Pen Bryn is a care home which supports people with a learning disability and mental health needs.
 It is in the Porth area of Rhondda Cynon Taf close to the town centre and local amenities and
 consists of a main house with an adjoining flat.

 The service provides good care and support in a warm and friendly environment, that achieves
 excellent well-being outcomes for people. People are encouraged and supported to participate in
 activities that interest them and of their choosing ensuring their physical and emotional well-being.
 Care workers know people well and interact in a kind and caring manner. Care files detail how
 people like their needs met and are reviewed regularly. The environment is good. It is safe and
 accessible and has suitable indoor and outdoor areas for people to use. Leadership and
 management are good. Care workers feel well supported, happy, and confident in their roles. They
 receive regular supervision and a variety of training, and policies are in place to provide guidance.
 Audits and oversight are carried out by a committed and passionate management team. Robust
quality assurance systems are in place, and the Responsible Individual (RI) visits the service
regularly, as required.

source_index.name: Peniel Green Care Home
source_index.summary:
Peniel Green Care Home is a care home providing accommodation, personal care and nursing
 care for up to 34 people. The home is situated in Peniel Green, Swansea, with access to local
 amenities, community resources and opportunities for people to maintain connections with the local
 area. People also benefit from access to secure outdoor spaces and a range of activities and
 community engagement opportunities. Based on our findings, we have rated Well-being as Good,
 Care and Support as Good, Environment as Good, and Leadership and Management as Requires
 Improvement.

 During our inspection, we found people were supported by a caring and committed staff team who
 knew them well and promote their well-being and independence. People and relatives spoke
 positively about the home, describing it as welcoming and homely. Feedback demonstrates people
 are listened to and are able to influence aspects of daily life, including activities and food provision.
 We saw positive interactions between staff and people throughout the inspection and found people
 are supported to access healthcare services when required.

 The home is generally clean, comfortable and well maintained. However, our review of care
 records identified that care plans, risk assessments and daily recordings do not always fully reflect
 people's current needs or consistently evidence the care and support provided. Whilst we did not
 find evidence that people are receiving unsafe care, improvements are needed to strengthen care
 planning and recording systems. An Area for Improvement (AFI) was identified within Care and
Support.

Leadership arrangements have supported improvements in several areas, including staff training
and development. However, governance and quality assurance systems do not always effectively
identify or address issues relating to care records, recruitment documentation and oversight of
quality assurance processes. An AFI was identified within Leadership and Management, and this
theme is rated as Requires Improvement.

source_index.name: Perrots Lodge
source_index.summary:
Perrots Lodge is a care home service for up to eight adults in Haverfordwest, Pembrokeshire. The
 service supports people with a range of needs, including learning disabilities, physical disabilities
 and complex health needs. People live in a homely environment and are supported by a dedicated
 staff team who know them well and promote person-centred care.

 People experience good wellbeing because many people experience positive outcomes, maintain
 important relationships and access meaningful activities in their home and local community. Staff
 support people to make choices, maintain independence and take positive risks safely

 The care and support provided is good because people receive personalised care from staff who
 understand their needs, preferences and goals. Care planning is outcome focused, health needs
 are supported well, and effective systems help ensure medication and infection prevention
 arrangements remain safe.

 The environment is good because people live in a comfortable, personalised environment which
 supports their needs and well-being. The service is clean, well maintained and provides suitable
 facilities, equipment and sensory resources.
The leadership and management of the service is excellent because leaders have developed highly
effective governance arrangements, introduced innovative digital systems and created a strong
culture of continuous improvement. They invest significantly in staff development and maintain
excellent oversight of the quality of care and support people receive.

source_index.name: Plas Gwyn Care Home
source_index.summary:
Plas Gwyn Residential Home is a Georgian mansion set within its own grounds overlooking
 Cardigan Bay. The home provides residential care for up to 16 adults in a warm, welcoming and
 homely environment where dignity, independence and well-being are at the centre of everyday
 life. People’s well-being is excellent because they are supported by an exceptionally skilled and
 compassionate staff team who consistently adapt care to help people achieve meaningful
 outcomes that significantly improve their quality of life. Care and support is exemplary, staff know
 people exceptionally well and deliver highly personalised care that promotes
 independence, confidence and wellbeing. The environment has been thoughtfully designed and
 continually adapted to meet people’s changing needs whilst maintaining a warm, homely
 atmosphere where people clearly feel a strong sense of belonging. Leadership and management
 have embedded a positive culture of continuous improvement, ensuring people consistently receive
 high-quality care from a confident, well-supported workforce.

source_index.name: Plas Lorna
source_index.summary:
Plas Lorna is a home that provides a warm and nurturing environment for the adults living there.
 People receive support from a care staff team who know them well and understand their needs.
 Personalised support helps people to remain as independent as possible and achieve positive
 outcomes in a safe and supportive home.

 Well-being is good. The home offers high level of care, supported by a team who know each
 person well and treat them with dignity. Care staff work in a way that encourages independence,
 choice and respect.

 Care and support provided is good. Care staff provide person-centred care that is tailored to
 people's individual needs and preferences. People are supported to access healthcare services,
 maintain relationships with family and friends, and participate in a range of meaningful activities
 that reflect their interests. Care plans provide clear guidance to ensure care is delivered
consistently and in line with people's assessed needs.

The environment is good. People live in a clean and comfortable environment that meets their
individual needs. Bedrooms are personalised and reflect people's preferences, helping them feel
comfortable in their surroundings.

Leadership and management oversight is good. The manager and care staff team have a good
understanding of people's needs and work effectively to ensure they receive appropriate care and
support. The Responsible Individual (RI) maintains active oversight, gathering feedback from
residents, care staff, and professionals to guide ongoing improvements.

source_index.name: Plas Y Don
source_index.provider: Gwynedd Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
People experience good well-being at Plas Y Don. Care staff create a warm, welcoming
 atmosphere and develop positive, respectful relationships with people. Individuals feel listened to
 and valued, and they contribute to decisions through meetings and everyday choices. People take
 part in meaningful activities and maintain connections with family, friends and the wider community.


 People receive good care and support that is person centred and responsive. Care staff use clear,
 detailed care plans and review them regularly. They involve health professionals to support
 physical and mental health. Care staff assess and manage risks effectively and follow safeguarding
 and medication procedures that promote safe, consistent practice.


 People live in an environment that is clean, comfortable and homely. Communal areas are
 welcoming, well maintained and support social interaction. Facilities meet people’s needs and
 enable independence in daily routines. Indoor and outdoor spaces provide pleasant surroundings
 where people can relax, spend time with others and enjoy a sense of familiarity and security.
Leadership and management are good, with proactive managers providing clear direction.
Managers are visible and support care staff to deliver quality care. Governance systems and
oversight arrangements monitor performance and drive improvement. Training and supervision
support staff development and maintain consistent, effective practice across services.

source_index.name: Priory House Care Home
source_index.summary:
Priory House Care Home provides care and support for up to 29 people. The home is situated
 within Prestatyn town and close the local shops and amenities.

 People’s well-being requires improvement as they are not consistently living in accommodation that
 promotes or supports the achievement of their personal well-being outcomes. Shortcomings in the
 quality and maintenance of the living environment, are having a negative impact on people’s
 comfort, dignity and overall quality of life. People do always have a choice.

 Care and support require improvement due to inadequate arrangements for the safe storage of
 medication and oversight of weight loss and falls management. However, people benefit from a
 committed and dedicated staff team who know them well and provide appropriate support, helping
 individuals to maintain their well-being outcomes as far as possible.
The environment requires significant improvement. The premises are not being maintained to a
suitable standard and do not currently support the delivery of safe, dignified care. Poor upkeep,
outstanding repairs and maintenance issues present risks to people’s health, safety and well-being
and require urgent attention and investment from the provider.

Leadership and management also require significant improvement. The Responsible Individual has
not ensured effective governance, oversight or organisational arrangements to support the safe
and effective operation of the service or the delivery of consistently high-quality care

source_index.name: Rhyd Hir
source_index.summary:
Rhyd Hir is a small care home located in a residential area on the outskirts of Neath. It caters for
 people with autism who may require personal care and support with daily activities. People can
 access community amenities using public transport or the home’s own vehicle.

 People receive good quality care and support which enhances their well-being and helps them lead
 healthy and fulfilled lives. People have opportunities to engage meaningfully with others and to
 expand their social and leisure experiences. Care staff know people very well and actively promote
 independence. People have timely access to medical and specialist services.

 The home provides a comfortable and personalised living environment that meets people's needs
 and preferences. It is maintained to a good overall standard and has suitable facilities to promote
 independent living. People also benefit from regular environmental upgrades.
The service has an experienced manager who leads the home and staff team very effectively.
People are cared for by motivated staff who are appropriately recruited, trained and supported. The
organisation has recently appointed a new Responsible Individual (RI) and assistant director, who
are making changes to improve operations. However, the RI must ensure the manager receives
regular support and supervision, so expectations are clear and planned changes can be
implemented successfully.

source_index.name: Riverdale
source_index.summary:
Riverdale is a care home located in Cardiff. The service supports people living with autism, mental
 health needs and associated support needs.



 People living at Riverdale experience excellent well-being outcomes. Where they are supported to
 live safely, maintain healthy lifestyles and have meaningful control over their daily lives. We found
 staff promote independence and positive risk-taking. Activities are person-centred and support
 people to develop new skills and access their local community.



 The standard of care and support is excellent. Personal plans are detailed, accurate and regularly
 reviewed with people and their multi-disciplinary teams. People are supported to access healthcare
services and staff are proactive in identifying and responding to changes in health needs.



The environment at Riverdale is good. People have highly personalised bedrooms which reflect
their individual needs and preferences. Outdoor areas are maintained to a high standard and are
accessible to all. Regular servicing, maintenance and repairs ensures people live in a safe and
comfortable home.



Leadership and management at Riverdale is excellent. People and their representatives have
confidence in the service because leaders actively seek feedback and respond proactively to
concerns and suggestions. Effective oversight and governance arrangements support continuous
improvement and help ensure positive outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Rozelle Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Rozelle care home service providing nursing care located on the western outskirts of Abergavenny.
 We rated Well-being as Good because people are treated with dignity and respect by staff who
 know them well and understand their individual needs and preferences. People are supported to
 maintain relationships, participate in meaningful activities and make choices about their daily lives.

 We rated Care and Support as Good because people receive person-centred care that reflects
 their assessed needs and desired outcomes. Care plans are reviewed regularly, people have
 access to healthcare professionals when required and staff support people to maintain their health,
 well-being and independence. Medication is managed safely and people receive care that
 promotes positive outcomes.

 We rated Environment as Good because people live in a comfortable, homely and well-maintained
 environment. Bedrooms are personalised, communal areas are welcoming and people have
 access to outdoor space.

 We rated Leadership and Management as Good because effective leadership, quality assurance
 systems and a committed staff team support the delivery of good quality care and positive
 outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Sketty House Care Home
source_index.summary:
People living at Sketty House are able to achieve their well-being outcomes because they are
 supported to make choices, maintain important relationships and take part in a varied range of
 meaningful activities.

 Care and support is good because care plans provide detailed guidance about people’s needs,
 preferences and desired outcomes, and people have access to health professionals and safe
 support with their medicines. Some daily records did not consistently demonstrate that fluid
