 monitoring, continence care and oral hygiene had been provided.

 The environment at Sketty House is good because people live in a clean, comfortable and
 generally well-maintained environment. Safety checks, equipment servicing and infection
 prevention arrangements support their well-being, although parts of the older building remain in
 need of refurbishment.

 Leadership and management is good because management are visible and supportive. Care staff
spoke positively about training, supervision and the culture of the service. Quality assurance
processes are robust and provide effective monitoring of the service.

source_index.name: St Albans Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Situated in small community in the centre of Cardiff, St Albans provides specialist, person-centred
 nursing support for people over the age of eighteen, living with Dementia, Complex Mental Health
 Needs, Huntington’s Disease, Acquired Brain Injury, Neurological Conditions, and Learning
 Disabilities.

 Wellbeing is rated good because most people experience positive wellbeing outcomes and benefit
 from a caring, person-centred approach which promotes meaningful lives, independence,
 relationships and participation. Whilst improvements are needed to strengthen involvement in care
 planning and ensure greater consistency in some aspects of care delivery, people are generally
 supported to achieve outcomes that matter to them and enjoy a good quality of life.

 Care and support require improvement because people are not always meaningfully involved in
 care planning and review processes. Personal plans and associated records are not always
accurate, up to date and do not clearly demonstrate how care is delivered in accordance with
individuals' wishes, aspirations, risks and specialist needs.

Environment is rated good as people benefit from a welcoming and well-resourced environment
that supports wellbeing, activity and independence. The provider has demonstrated ongoing
investment and improvement in the physical environment.

Leadership and management require significant improvement because people do not consistently
benefit from effective operational leadership, governance, and workforce arrangements to promote
safe, high-quality care and support. People are not routinely involved in the development of their
initial personal plans or in subsequent reviews, limiting opportunities to ensure care reflects their
needs, preferences, and changing circumstances. As a result, there is an increased risk that care
and support may not be appropriate, effective, or responsive to individual needs.

source_index.name: Swansea Living Solutions Ltd
source_index.provider: Calon Fawr Nursing Home Limited trading as Swansea Living Solutions
source_index.summary:
Swansea Living Solutions is located in Ty Coch, Swansea close to many local amenities such as a
 local college, coffee shops and restaurants. The service provides person-centred support to
 people.

 People experience positive well-being outcomes as they receive person-centred care and are
 supported to achieve their well-being outcomes. People spoken with told us they were happy living
 at the service.

 Care and support is good and personal plans and risk assessments provide clear guidance for staff
 and reflected people's individual circumstances, strengths and preferences. Records show people
 receive ongoing support to maintain their health and well-being.

 The environment is clean, comfortable and homely. Bedrooms are personalised and spacious,
 helping people feel settled and at home. Significant improvements had been made since the
 previous inspection, including refurbishment work and environmental upgrades.
Leadership and management of the service is good. The registered manager and responsible
individual (RI) demonstrate effective oversight and a clear commitment to continuous improvement.
There are quality assurance systems in place to identify areas for development and respond
positively to feedback. Overall, staff spoke highly of the support they receive and say there is a
positive team culture.

source_index.name: Swn Y Wylan
source_index.summary:
Swn Y Wylan is a residential care home in Rhos on Sea providing accommodation and support for
 up to six adults whose primary diagnosis is a learning disability and/or mental illness.

 People receive quality support from staff who know them well and promote their well-being, choice
 and independence. People are supported to maintain important relationships, participate in
 community activities and achieve outcomes that matter to them.

 Care and support arrangements are good, responsive to people's individual needs and are
 underpinned by detailed care planning and multidisciplinary involvement. The environment is
 welcoming, comfortable and generally well maintained.

 Leadership and management arrangements provide a good level of oversight through regular
 audits, governance meetings, quality reviews and responsible individual (RI) visits.

source_index.name: The Beeches
source_index.summary:
People experience good well-being outcomes; they are treated with dignity and respect and have
 activities available to them. People are supported to stay as healthy as possible, with systems in
 place to protect people in an environment that meets their needs. People are treated as individuals
 and can live their lives how they wish.

 Care and support are good. Detailed care documentation is in place to support people’s needs. The
 service has good systems to safeguard people, and good systems to reduce the risk of the spread
 of infection. Care staff treat people with kindness and compassion. Personal plans are an accurate
 reflection of the individual and people receive appropriate care and support.

 The environment is good and meets people’s needs and outcomes, enhances their well-being, and
 is safe. The Beeches is appropriately decorated throughout and has enough communal space.
 People’s rooms, as well as communal areas, are kept clean and free from hazards. People can
personalise their rooms if they wish. Investment in the environment is evident.

The leadership and management of The Beeches is good. Managers and the Responsible
Individual (RI), have good oversight of the service. They ensure the required staff recruitment,
training, and support is undertaken and provide good-quality support and facilities. Care staff told
us they are happy working at the service.

source_index.name: The Headlands Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
The Headlands is situated on the outskirts of Llangollen town centre, in a residential area. The
 service is set over two floors with access by a lift. The service provides nursing care and support
 for up to twenty-eight adults.

 People’s well-being outcomes are good. Care staff support people to understand their rights and
 maximise their independence. Care staff know the people they support well; they know what is
 important to them and what approaches to use when delivering care and support.

 Care and support are good. Personal plans and risk assessments are detailed and reviewed
 regularly. People receive the support they require in a way which reflects their individuality. People
 are treated by care staff with respect and in a dignified manner.

 Leadership and management of the service is good. The service is well-led and has a positive
 culture of promoting the well-being of people and staff. Suitable governance and quality assurance
 systems help the service operate smoothly. Care staff receive training and support relevant to the
 needs of the people they care for.

 The environment is good and meets people’s needs. The home is clean, comfortable, and
appropriately decorated. The provider undertakes regular maintenance and repairs, and ensures
the environment is safe. Investment in the service is evident and ongoing.

source_index.name: The Oaks
source_index.summary:
The Oaks provides care and support for up to 73 adults aged 50 and over, including residential,
 nursing, dementia and palliative care. The purpose-built home, located in the heart of Newtown,
 offers a modern, welcoming and well-maintained environment designed to meet people's varying
 needs.

 People experience excellent well-being and benefit from a strong sense of belonging. They are
 supported to maintain meaningful relationships, pursue individual interests and remain connected
 to their local community. Staff promote choice, dignity and independence, helping people achieve
 positive outcomes and live fulfilling lives.

 The care and support provided is good. People receive person-centred care from skilled and
 experienced staff who understand their needs and preferences. Care planning and review
 processes are effective and involve people, their representatives and relevant professionals. The
 service demonstrates a strong commitment to providing compassionate palliative and end of life
 care.
The environment is excellent. Accommodation is spacious, personalised and designed to promote
comfort, independence and social engagement. Dementia-friendly features support orientation,
reduce anxiety and enhance people's quality of life.

The leadership and management arrangements at the service are effective. Strong governance,
quality assurance processes and active oversight by the Responsible Individual (RI) support
continuous improvement. Staff feel well supported through training and supervision, helping to
ensure people receive safe, responsive and high-quality care.

source_index.name: Trevelyan
source_index.summary:
Trevelyan is a mental health service that provides support to adults who have a functional mental
 illness requiring personal care and support. It is in the rural village of Bronwydd, three miles from
 the market town of Carmarthen.

 The well-being outcomes of people is “Excellent” as people receive exemplary care and support to
 achieve self-directed outcomes relating to their physical, mental and emotional health.

 The care and support people receive is “Excellent” as highly skilled care staff understand and
 support people as individuals consistently considering their wishes, aspirations, risks and specialist
 needs.

 The environment of which people live is “Excellent” as people benefit from living in a home that
 meets their individual needs and places them at the heart of the service.

 The leadership and management of the service is “Excellent” as leaders promote a strong positive
 culture that is supportive, inclusive and respectful.

source_index.name: Ty Carreg
source_index.summary:
People experience excellent well-being outcomes through highly personalised support which
 promotes independence, emotional well-being, meaningful relationships and participation in
 community life. People develop life skills, access educational opportunities and engage in activities
 aligned with their interests and aspirations. Family members provided highly positive feedback
 regarding the quality of support and progress achieved. Care staff know people well and support
 them to lead fulfilling lives.

 Care and support people receive is excellent. Assessments, personal plans, behaviour support
 plans, risk assessments and health plans are comprehensive, regularly reviewed and focused on
 achieving positive outcomes. Care staff have clear guidance to provide consistent, person-centred
 support. Effective partnership working with health professionals, alongside regular health reviews
 and quarterly multi-disciplinary team meetings, ensures people's needs are monitored and
 responded to promptly. People are supported to increase independence, develop skills and achieve
personal goals.

People experience excellent environmental outcomes because they live in a safe, comfortable and
highly personalised setting comprising self-contained flats and converted barns. Dedicated
communal areas, a sensory room and activity room promote independence, well-being and
engagement. The environment is well maintained, supports individual needs and provides excellent
opportunities for personal development and community inclusion.

Leadership and management are excellent because the service benefits from strong, visible
leadership and effective governance arrangements. Quality assurance systems drive continuous
improvement and support high standards of care. Care staff reported feeling valued, supported and
empowered, while professionals praised communication and partnership working. Managers have
established a positive culture focused on achieving the best possible outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Ty Coch Care Home
source_index.summary:
Ty Coch Care Home provides residential and nursing care in the Llanishen area of Cardiff. The
 provider supports older people, including those living with dementia. Services include respite care,
 long-term nursing care, end-of-life support, and palliative care.

 Well-being requires improvement because while staff know people well and provide dignified and
 respectful support, people, or their representatives, are not actively involved in identifying,
 developing or reviewing their own well-being outcomes.

 Care and support requires improvement. While staff have good relationships with people, records
 and case recordings are not completed accurately. We cannot be assured people consistently
 receive care and support which fully meets their needs.

 The environment is good because people live in a warm, vibrant and homely atmosphere which
promotes a sense of belonging.

Leadership and management is good because there is a committed and proactive management
team who are focused on improving outcomes and experiences for people living at the service.
Leaders demonstrate a good understanding of the service's strengths and areas for development
and have established systems to monitor quality, safety and performance.

source_index.name: Ty Ddraig
source_index.summary:
The quality of well-being, care and support, environment, and leadership and management at Ty
 Ddraig is Good. This is a newly established service and, whilst systems and practice continue to
 develop, people receive safe care and support and achieve positive outcomes. Relatives and
 professionals are positive about the service and describe staff as caring, professional and
 responsive to people's needs.

 People receive support informed by care plans, risk assessments and positive behaviour support
 plans, although further work is needed to strengthen links between these documents and ensure
 information is clear and outcome focused.

 The provider responds appropriately to significant incidents by reviewing practice, supporting staff
 through debrief sessions and implementing measures to reduce the risk of recurrence. Medication
 is managed safely, with appropriate auditing and oversight arrangements in place. People live in a
 clean, purpose-built environment that is personalised and generally well maintained, although some
 environmental improvements remain in progress.
Leadership and management arrangements continue to develop appropriately for a new service,
with evidence of supervision, staff meetings, quality assurance processes and reflective practice.
Areas requiring further development include staffing consistency, care planning and ensuring
training fully equips staff to meet the needs of people using the service. Overall, people receive
good quality care and support, and the provider continues to develop and embed systems that
promote consistency, learning and service improvement.

source_index.name: Ty Richards
source_index.summary:
Well-being is rated excellent because people receive highly personalised support that promotes
 choice, independence and meaningful engagement. Staff know people exceptionally well, support
 positive health and well-being outcomes, and help people maintain important relationships and
 participate in activities which are meaningful to them.

 Care and Support is rated excellent because people benefit from consistently effective and
 responsive care that is tailored to their changing needs. Comprehensive assessments, detailed
 care planning and regular reviews ensure support remains current and achieves positive outcomes

 Leadership and Management is rated excellent because leaders promote a strong person-centred
 culture and provide effective oversight of the service. Quality assurance systems drive continuous
 improvement, staff feel supported and valued, and partnership working contributes to positive
 outcomes for people.

 Environment is rated Good because people live in a safe, welcoming and personalised home which
 promotes comfort, dignity and independence. The environment meets people's needs, supports
 meaningful daily experiences and is continually reviewed and developed to enhance people's well-
being and quality of life.

source_index.name: Westhaven Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Westhaven Nursing Home is situated in a residential area in Rhos-on- Sea. People can access
 local amenities and the sea front.


 The well-being for people in Westhaven is rated as good. This is because the home has worked
 hard to increase activities for people and has had expert advice to ensure appropriate activities for
 all residents. Menu choices have improved; people have varied meals.


 The care and support are rated as good. People benefit from a stable staff group who know their
 needs well. Care is planned according to people’s needs and preferences.


 The environment is rated good. The home has a continuing maintenance plan in place to refresh
the décor and upgrade bedroom furniture. People can personalise their rooms and add homely
touches to them.


Leadership and management are rated good. There is good oversight of the standards of care. The
Responsible Individual (RI) provides visit and quality reports in line with legislation.

source_index.name: Windsor Street
source_index.summary:
Windsor Street is located near the town of Aberdare, offering convenient access to local amenities.
 The service provides accommodation for up to four people, each in their own self-contained flat.

 People experience good well-being outcomes. People can make choices about their day to day
 lives and are supported to engage in activities they enjoy. People are supported with their health
 needs and have good access to relevant health and social care professionals.

 Care and support is good. Care documentation is person-centred, outcome focused and reflective
 of people’s care and support needs. Care documentation is reviewed regularly and updated as
 required to reflect changes in needs. Risks to people’s health and safety are appropriately
 assessed and managed.

 The environment is good. People live in an environment that is suited to their needs and promotes
 their comfort, safety, and well-being. The home is clean, well maintained, and provides a
 welcoming and homely atmosphere.

 Leadership and management require improvement. Care staff report feeling well-supported in their
roles and express satisfaction working at the service. Care staff have access to training to support
them in meeting the needs of people; however, further improvement is required to ensure training
provision is consistently effective and meets all identified needs.

source_index.name: Woodland Lodge Care Home
source_index.summary:
Woodland Lodge Care Home provides residential care for adults age eighteen and over. It can
 accommodate a maximum of nineteen people, of any gender. The service is located near the
harbour town of Tenby on the picturesque Pembrokeshire coastline.

People experience good well-being outcomes. They told us they feel safe and happy with the
service. Care staff have developed positive relationships with people, relatives and visiting
professionals.

Care and support are good. We saw care staff treat people with dignity and respect and encourage
them to make choices about their care and support. Care staff know people well and understand
what is important to them.

The environment is good. People live in a clean, comfortable and welcoming home. The provider
continues to invest in the environment and people benefit from a range of communal and private
spaces which reflect their individual preferences and interests.

Leadership and management are good. An experienced management team leads the service with
oversight from a visible and accessible Responsible Individual (RI).

source_index.name: Y Frondeg
source_index.provider: Gwynedd Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Y Frondeg provides a home for people living with physical and learning disability. The home is
 situated close to Caernarfon Town.

 Wellbeing at Y Frondeg is excellent. People are supported to be as independent and active as
 possible and achieve their chosen objectives. A person told us their life has improved drastically
 since living in the home. The service offers a strong active offer of the Welsh language and people
 remain a part of the local community.

 Care and support are excellent. People have care planned with them and records are person
 centred and reflect people’s choices and preferences. People receive care from familiar staff who
 provide continuation in care. Medicine processes are well thought out and audited.

 The environment is rated good. People can personalise their bedroom surrounding themselves with
things of importance to them. The home is an older building that requires upgrading, a budget has
been agreed to meet this.

Leadership and management are excellent. Senior staff are supportive of care staff. Care staff
receive training and meaningful supervision. Care staff are supported to advance their careers and
young apprentices receive mentorship. The Responsible Individual (RI) visits the service and
provides quality reports in line with legislation.

source_index.name: Y Plas EMI Care Home
source_index.summary:
People are generally treated with kindness, dignity and respect and live in an environment that
 supports their well-being. However, inconsistencies in care documentation and monitoring records
 limit assurance that people’s health, personal care and social needs are always met effectively.

 Care and Support is rated Requires Significant Improvement. There are continued inconsistencies
 regarding personal planning, medication management and record keeping. Personal plans do not
 always provide clear, accurate or person-centred guidance. Medication errors and weaknesses in
 oversight processes were also found. Due to the seriousness of these issues, Priority Action
 Notices were re-issued.

 The service provides a generally safe, clean and homely environment. Living spaces support
 people’s comfort and safety. Communal areas offer opportunities for social interaction and
 relaxation.

 Leadership and Management is rated Requires Improvement. Although some progress has been
 made since previous inspections, quality assurance and governance systems have not been
 effective in identifying and addressing ongoing concerns. Further improvements are required to
strengthen oversight, ensure compliance and secure sustained positive outcomes for people using
the service.

The provider has acknowledged the areas of concern identified in the inspection. They have
assured us actions are underway to make the necessary improvements and provide additional
leadership and management oversight. Further embedding of these actions is required to ensure
the required improvements are made.

source_index.name: Yr Ysgol Ltd
source_index.summary:
People who have made Yr Ysgol their home receive a good standard of care. Most people are
 happy with the care and support they get and have formed positive relationships with the staff
 team. Relatives have high levels of confidence in the service.

 Wellbeing is rated as good because the motivated staff team strive to give people opportunities to
 do things that matter to them.

 Care and support is rated as good because the team is led by an experienced manager and deputy
 who are well regarded by the rest of the team. Personal plans help inform and direct care and
 support.

 The environment is rated as good because standards of cleanliness are high and the service is well
 maintained with plenty of outside space as well as several small lounges and dining rooms.
Leadership and management is rated as good because the manager is very visible throughout the
service and has support from a wider team of staff including human resources and senior leaders.
Staff feel proud to work for the service.

reports.title: October 2026 publication-month manager learning report
narrative: The fixed cohort contains 65 homes across 21 authorities; 65 latest archived reports provide 630 source PDF pages.
65 reports have official CIW summaries and 0 have explicitly labelled theme extracts. 0 cohort homes have no archived report.
65 homes have at least one published theme rating and 0 have none. The four theme distributions retain missing values and use the full cohort denominator.
Published tables contain 51 specific rows: 25 Priority action and 26 Area for improvement. 0 rows are Achieved; 51 have unknown status.
4 specific action rows have no topic assignment and remain included in the whole-cohort row totals; topic charts must not be treated as a complete action inventory.
All 3,866 extracted finding rows and 390 sections inform the evidence map. Positive and Improvement wording counts are separate overlapping search-label cohorts.

topics.name: Medicines management
topics.actions: Audit medicine administration records, storage, reconciliation, PRN protocols and staff competency; document exceptions and follow-up.
topics.evidence: MAR audit, competency records, storage checks and documented corrective actions

positive.name: Thompson Court
positive.text: Care staff work proactively with healthcare professionals to support positive health outcomes whilst encouraging people to develop confidence and independence in managing their medication.

positive.name: Treeside
positive.text: Staff demonstrate appropriate competence and understanding of the people’s medication requirements, with regular audits providing assurance that high standards are maintained.

positive.name: Clynsaer House
positive.text: The deputy manager oversees medication practice by completing annual care staff competency checks and regular medication audits to maintain consistency and good standards.

negative.name: Heathfields Residential Home
negative.text: We identified gaps in some staff medication administration signatures and found records relating to 'as required' medicines did not consistently provide sufficient detail regarding decision-making and outcomes.

negative.name: Shillings Care
negative.text: We found there was limited information within it to help guide care staff to manage and administer medication safely. ‘When required’ medication is recorded but this is not always in line with current guidance.

negative.name: Cedar House
negative.text: During our review of records we identified gaps in Medication Administration Records (MAR) charts and stock-count discrepancies that had not always been identified through existing audit processes.

actions.name: The Oaks
actions.text: People are exposed to the risk of harm because medicines management systems and processes are ineffective. The provider cannot demonstrate that medicines are consistently stored, monitored and administered safely.

actions.name: Ty Clyd
actions.text: counts not being carried out for PRN medication. People medication who was not in blister packs yet were not being counted. No reference of assuring that the count in the stock is correct.

actions.name: Castle Court Residential Home
actions.text: People are at risk of harm because medicines are not consistently managed safely and effective systems are not in place to ensure medication-related risks are identified and addressed.

actions.name: Balmoral House - Skyline Care Ltd
actions.text: These failings place people at risk of receiving unsafe or ineffective medicines management as people cannot be assured that medicines are stored, administered and monitored safely, placing them at risk of avoidable harm and poor health outcomes.

actions.name: Ty Ross Care Home
actions.text: People are at risk of experiencing poor health outcomes where medication administration practices are not consistently safe, accurate and subject to effective oversight.

topics.local_test: Sample administration records against actual staff practice with the medicines lead.
topics.success_outcome: Exceptions are detected, followed up and checked; staff demonstrate the agreed local procedure.

topics.name: Safeguarding & incident learning
topics.actions: Review safeguarding escalation, incident reporting and CIW notifications. Check that staff understand local procedures and that learning reaches the team.
topics.evidence: Escalation log, training records, incident reviews and notifications

positive.name: Treeside
positive.text: Staff use information from incidents, reviews and ongoing monitoring to continually strengthen practice, resulting in care and support that is tailored, safe and promotes the best possible outcomes for people.

positive.name: Fairways Nursing Home
positive.text: Monthly audits of service delivery, supported by governance logs, incident reviews, detailed analysis and policy monitoring, provide clear evidence of effective oversight and quality assurance.

positive.name: Picton Court
positive.text: The service maintains accurate records of incidents and accidents and completes detailed risk assessments to support safe practices while enabling individuals to take positive risks.

negative.name: The Oaks
negative.text: Whilst the RI undertakes monitoring activities and there are some safeguarding arrangements in place, governance and oversight systems have failed to identify a range of significant concerns found during this inspection.

negative.name: Apley Lodge Residential Home
negative.text: Whilst systems are in place to monitor Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS), records do not consistently contain key information such as application, authorisation and expiry dates.

actions.name: The Oaks
actions.text: People's privacy, dignity and confidentiality are not consistently safeguarded because confidential care records were found unsecured in communal areas. This creates a risk of unauthorised access to personal information and means people cannot be assured that their sensitive information is being managed and stored securely.

topics.local_test: Walk through a local escalation scenario and trace a recent incident review.
topics.success_outcome: Staff explain escalation confidently and can show how incident learning changed practice.

topics.name: Personal plans & risk assessment
topics.actions: Sample personal plans for individual preferences, changing needs, review dates and usable risk controls. Check that staff can apply the guidance in practice.
topics.evidence: Plan reviews, resident involvement and observed practice

positive.name: Fairways Nursing Home
positive.text: Effective assessment, care planning and review processes ensure people remain safe and support remain responsive and centred on achieving positive outcomes, promoting health, wellbeing, dignity and independence.

positive.name: Llannerch Grange
positive.text: This highly effective approach has led to significant outcomes, including increased independence, progress in sport and a return to employment through shared planning and proportionate risk assessment.

positive.name: Llys Y Seren

actions.success_outcome: People describe opportunities that matter to them and feedback shapes future support.

limitations: This is a fixed all-data period cohort, not a dashboard-filter cohort. Only each service's latest archived report is included; this is not the complete historical inspection series or a trend in care quality. Early empty periods must not be interpreted as an absence of historical inspections: earlier reports are outside this latest-only archive.

Monthly membership uses reportPublishedActualDate, not the inspection visit or report issue date. Visit start/end, issue and publication are distinct. Empty months mean no latest archived report was published in that month, not that CIW did no inspections.

Ratings are the exact four published directory-snapshot theme values. Their effective dates are not independently auditable and cannot be assumed to match the historical publication month. Missing ratings and missing reports are not evidence of poor care. No overall quality score is calculated.

Positive wording and Improvement wording are automated search labels, not independent CIW findings. Topic counts mean reports mentioning a topic, not failures; topics and evidence sets overlap and must not be added together.

Published action-table rows can be historical or Achieved. New and Reviewed describe status words published in the source, not validation today. Missing status means unknown, not unresolved. Category counts are not counts of current failures or confirmed enforcement notices.

Excerpts and official summaries retain extracted wording and PDF page provenance. Layout changes and damaged characters can occur; the archived PDF is authoritative. Representative examples are not an exhaustive account or a prevalence estimate.
Public latest-report URLs can change after this snapshot. Use the linked local archived PDF to verify the captured evidence; the external source link establishes its CIW origin.

Management controls and the illustrative learning workflow are assistant-suggested local learning prompts, not CIW requirements, legal advice, clinical advice or an accreditation assessment. Validate applicability with appropriate local leads.

CareLens Cymru is independent and not an official CIW product. Source: Care Inspectorate Wales / Welsh Government, Crown copyright in each report's stated year; reuse under the Open Government Licence, excluding logos. 979 archived reports contain explicit licence notices. The Haven has no extracted notice; the general CIW copyright page provides Crown-material reuse permission. Source links and attribution are retained.

source_index.name: Abergarw Manor
source_index.summary:
People achieve positive outcomes because they receive compassionate, person-centred care from
 a care staff team that knows them well and is committed to promoting their well-being. During our
 inspection, people and relatives spoke positively about the service and consistently described staff
 as kind, respectful and responsive. We observed positive interactions throughout the home and
 found people were relaxed, comfortable and treated with dignity.

 People receive care and support that reflects their individual needs, preferences and personal
 outcomes. Care staff work effectively with healthcare professionals to support people's health and
 well-being and respond promptly when needs change. Care planning arrangements provide staff
 with clear guidance to deliver consistent and personalised support.

 People live in a clean, safe and comfortable environment that enhances their quality of life.
 Bedrooms are personalised and communal areas provide opportunities for social interaction,
 meaningful engagement and relaxation. The provider maintains the premises to a good standard
 and ensures appropriate equipment and safety measures are in place to support people's well-
being.

Effective leadership and management underpin the quality of the service. The management team
promotes a positive culture, supports staff to develop their skills and maintains oversight through
established quality assurance systems. Staff feel supported in their roles and demonstrate a clear
commitment to achieving positive outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Apley Lodge Residential Home
source_index.summary:
Well-being is rated good as people experience positive well-being outcomes. They benefit from
 caring relationships with care staff who know them well, promote independence and provide
 opportunities for meaningful engagement. People appear comfortable, settled and receive support
 to maintain relationships with those important to them.

 Care and support is rated as requires improvement because care planning, record keeping,
 medication management and risk oversight do not consistently demonstrate people receive safe,
 effective and person-centred care in line with their assessed needs.

 Environment is rated as requires improvement because environmental oversight and fire safety
 arrangements are not consistently effective in identifying, monitoring and responding to risks,
 reducing assurance that people are protected from harm.

 Leadership and management is rated as requiring improvement because governance, quality
 assurance, regulatory oversight and workforce monitoring arrangements are not consistently
 effective in identifying concerns, driving improvement and ensuring compliance.

source_index.name: Aspen House Care Home
source_index.summary:
People’s well-being outcomes are good. People are provided with opportunities to participate in a
 range of activities if they choose. They receive appropriate support to meet their healthcare needs,
 with access to relevant healthcare professionals when required. People are also supported to
 maintain and develop important relationships with family members and friends, promoting their
 overall well-being and quality of life.

 Care and support is good. People living at the service report high levels of satisfaction and describe
 positive, respectful relationships with staff. Person-centred personal plans are in place, providing
 clear and comprehensive guidance that reflects peoples’ assessed needs, preferences, and
 desired outcomes. Medication is stored securely, managed appropriately, and administered in a
 timely manner by suitably trained staff.

 The environment is good. The service provides a safe and secure setting, while enabling people to
 personalise their bedrooms to reflect their preferences and maintain a sense of comfort and
 identity. Communal areas are readily accessible and support social interaction and engagement.

 Leadership and management require significant improvement. At the last inspection we issued a
Priority Action Notice in relation to governance arrangements. This remains in place as we were
unable to test the non-compliance at this inspection.

source_index.name: Baglan Lodge Care Home
source_index.summary:
Wellbeing is rated good because people felt safe, respected and supported to make choices about
 their lives. Residents, relatives and professionals provided consistently positive feedback about
 care, relationships and wellbeing. People maintained family and community connections and
 experienced kind, person-centred support.

 Care and support are rated good because people received safe, person-centred care that met their
 assessed needs. Care records evidenced effective risk management, healthcare involvement,
 medication management and monitoring of nutrition, hydration and skin integrity. Positive
 interactions were observed throughout the inspection. Improvements were required to strengthen
 outcome-focused care planning and meaningful activity provision.

 Environment requires improvement because inconsistent health and safety monitoring, gaps in fire
 safety checks and an unresolved patio trip hazard reduced assurance that environmental risks
 were being effectively managed. However, people lived in a clean, comfortable and well-maintained
 environment. Bedrooms, communal areas and facilities supported wellbeing outcomes.

 Leadership and management require improvement because governance systems were not
consistently effective. Recruitment file deficiencies, gaps in staff supervision and appraisal, and
weaknesses in audit and health and safety oversight require improvement to ensure sustained
regulatory compliance. However, people benefited from approachable leadership, positive
feedback from relatives and staff, and evidence of service improvements since the previous
inspection.

source_index.name: Balmoral House - Skyline Care Ltd
source_index.summary:
People’s well-being requires improvement as they are living in a home which does not consistently
 promote their well-being. Choices are not always given as there is not always enough care staff on
 duty. Shortcomings in the quality and maintenance of the living environment, are having a negative
 impact on people’s comfort, dignity and overall quality of life. There is little to occupy peoples time
 and no outings into the community due to staff shortages. Staff morale is low as they do not feel
 valued.

 Care and support require significant improvement as people are not consistently supported to
 achieve positive outcomes due to shortcomings in the dining experience, nutrition, activities
 provision, staffing arrangements, care planning, risk management and Welsh language provision.
 Insufficient staffing arrangements limit opportunities for meaningful engagement, supervision and
 the delivery of care that reflects people's individual needs, preferences and rights.
The environment requires improvement. The premises are not being maintained to a suitable
standard and do not currently support the delivery of safe, dignified care. The service provider has
failed to ensure environmental risks are consistently identified, assessed and managed. This
includes risks relating to access to hazardous areas, external exits, boiler rooms and trip hazards.
The provider must ensure people live in a safe, clean and well-maintained environment where risks
are effectively controlled, and infection prevention and control standards are consistently
maintained.

Leadership and management require significant improvement. The Responsible Individual (RI) has
not ensured effective governance, oversight or organisational arrangements to support the safe
and effective operation of the service or the delivery of consistently high-quality care. Staff
recruitment is not robust and there is not enough staff employed in the home.

source_index.name: Beechlea
source_index.summary:
Beechlea is a small care home situated in a village close to Bargoed and provides accommodation,
 care and support for up to four adults.

 People’s well-being and the care and support they receive are both rated as good. People are at
 the centre of their care and are treated with dignity, kindness and respect. Their choices,
 independence and individual outcomes are promoted, with personal plans reflecting their needs
 and wishes and are regularly reviewed. People receive their medicines as prescribed, with some
 aspects of medication management identified for further improvement.

 The environment and leadership and management of the service are both rated as good. People
 live in accommodation that supports their independence, safety and sense of security. Improved
 environmental oversight is required to ensure people continue to live in a safe and well-maintained
 home. The service is generally well managed, and quality assurance arrangements continue to
 develop to support effective monitoring and improvement. The RI is strengthening their oversight to
 provide greater assurance about the ongoing quality and safety of the service.

source_index.name: Beechwood Court
source_index.summary:
Beechwood Court is a care home service providing residential care, support and specialist
 education for adults with learning disabilities, autism, mental health needs, acquired brain injuries
 and epilepsy. The service is comprised of six homes and delivers personalised education,
 independent living skills and work-related learning opportunities alongside residential care,
 supporting people to develop independence, participate in their communities and achieve their
 personal outcomes through a person-centred approach.

 People achieve excellent well-being outcomes because they are supported to make choices,
 maintain relationships, access healthcare, participate in education and engage in meaningful
 community activities. Strong advocacy arrangements, excellent health support, positive family
 involvement and a wide range of social opportunities enable people to develop independence,
 achieve personal goals and enjoy fulfilling lives.
People receive excellent care and support that is personalised, responsive and based on detailed
assessments of their needs and aspirations. Strong multidisciplinary working, effective
communication support, robust behaviour support planning and safe medication management
ensure people receive consistent support that promotes independence, safety and positive
outcomes across all aspects of their lives.

The environment is good and largely supports people’s independence, well-being and daily
routines. Personalised bedrooms, welcoming communal spaces and extensive outdoor facilities
contribute to positive outcomes and enhance people’s quality of life. However, improvements are
required to ensure maintenance issues in some areas are addressed in a timely manner and are
consistently maintained to a good standard. This will help ensure people continue to experience
safe, comfortable and well-maintained environments that fully support their well-being outcomes.
The provider has recognised these areas for improvement and has developed action plans to
address them.

People benefit from excellent leadership and management arrangements that promote a positive
culture, effective governance and continuous improvement. Leaders are visible, knowledgeable
and committed to high-quality care. Care staff feel valued and supported, families express high
levels of confidence in the service, and robust quality assurance systems help drive positive
outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Bod Hyfyrd Care Home
source_index.summary:
Bod Hyfryd provides nursing care and dementia nursing care to a maximum of 40 people. It is
 located in Flint in Flintshire. People live in a generally clean environment; bedrooms are
 personalised and there is evidence of some activities taking place as well as links with the local
 community. People say staff are kind and compassionate. The provider has invested in the
 environment, and we found high training compliance and established systems for governance in
 place.

 However, we found well-being requires significant improvement as we found people cannot always
 exercise choice and control over their lives and do not always experience timely support when they
 need assistance. Care and support require significant improvement as people do not consistently
 receive care and support that meets their assessed needs.

 Environment requires significant improvement because although the premises is generally clean
 and well-maintained we found health and safety concerns were not always identified and
addressed proactively. Leadership and management require significant improvement as
governance systems had not identified, monitored or responded to the issues identified at
inspection.

source_index.name: Bridge House
source_index.summary:
Bridge House Residential Home provides care and support to people with and/or without dementia
 needs. It is a caring, supportive and well-managed service where people experience positive
 outcomes and good quality care. People told us they feel safe, enjoy living at the service and value
 the support they receive. Staff are experienced, know people well and have a good understanding
 of each person’s needs and routines. The service works collaboratively with healthcare
 professionals to promote people's health and well-being.

 Managers have established effective governance arrangements and demonstrate a commitment to
 continuous improvement. The provider maintains effective systems to monitor and maintain the
 safety of the environment. We saw evidence of ongoing investment in the premises which ensures
 people live in a comfortable, safe and welcoming home. Service development would benefit from
 providing people with regular opportunities to share their views and contribute to decisions about
 how the service is run.
We rate the service as “good” across the four domains of wellbeing, care and support, environment
and leadership and management.

source_index.name: Bryn Edwin Hall Residential Home
source_index.summary:
Bryn Edwin Hall Residential Home is a care home providing accommodation and personal care for
 people living with dementia. Well-being is good at the home because people are supported by staff
 who know them well and provide respectful, person-centred care. Positive interactions were
 observed throughout the home, with staff promoting dignity, inclusion and engagement. People are
 encouraged to maintain relationships, participate in activities and contribute to decisions about their
 daily lives. Monitoring of wellbeing and health helps ensure people receive appropriate support.

 People have good care and support through personalised care based on assessments and
 regularly reviewed care plans. Staff understand individual needs and provide support that promotes
 health, wellbeing and independence. Effective arrangements are in place to manage risks and
 respond to changing needs.

 The Environment is good because people live in a clean, comfortable and welcoming home.
 Bedrooms and communal areas support social interaction, relaxation and meaningful activity.
 Effective processes are in place to maintain cleanliness, safety and the suitability of the
 environment, including outdoor spaces that enhance wellbeing.
Leadership and Management is good because the service benefits from effective leadership and a
skilled workforce supported through recruitment, training and supervision. Governance systems
provide oversight of quality and safety, while audits and reviews drive improvement. Management
oversight has strengthened since the previous inspection, contributing to improved quality
assurance and service development.

source_index.name: Bryngwy
source_index.summary:
Bryngwy Residential Home provides residential care for older adults in Rhayader in Powys. It is
 situated in a rural setting in Powys.

 Well-being is good. People are supported to maintain their physical, mental health, and emotional
 well-being. People speak positively about the service and the care they receive as they have
 effective working relationships with care staff.

 Care and support are good. Care staff develop and maintain personalised care plans and risk
 assessments which provide clear information about people’s needs, preferences and outcomes.

 Leadership and management are good. The service benefits from effective leadership and
 management arrangements which support positive outcomes for people. Leaders have a good
 understanding of the service and have established systems to review quality, monitor performance
 and identify areas for improvement.
The environment is good. People live in an environment which is comfortable, safe and suitable for
their needs. The home provides a welcoming, warm, homely atmosphere which supports people.

source_index.name: Bryntirion
source_index.summary:
Bryntirion is a care home for adults located in a residential area of Bridgend. People experience
 excellent well-being outcomes. They have meaningful choice and control over their daily lives, with
 highly effective approaches helping them communicate their wishes and preferences. People
 maintain meaningful relationships, enjoy fulfilling social opportunities and receive strong support to
 achieve positive health and well-being outcomes. Effective safeguarding arrangements promote
 people’s safety.

 People receive excellent care and support which is highly personalised to their individual needs,
 preferences and outcomes. Comprehensive care planning and knowledgeable care staff ensure
 people receive consistent support. People are encouraged to develop their independence and
 make progress towards outcomes that are important to them. Care is delivered using the least
 restrictive approaches and feedback about the quality of support is very positive.

 People benefit from an excellent environment which is spotlessly clean, comfortable and homely.
 Personalised bedrooms and welcoming communal areas reflect people’s individual needs and
 preferences. People have opportunities to spend time with others, pursue their interests and enjoy
 privacy when they choose. Robust health and safety, maintenance and management systems
ensure the environment remains safe and exceptionally well maintained.

Leadership and management are excellent and have a positive impact on people's experiences
and outcomes. People benefit from a stable, well-supported and skilled care staff team. Senior
management provide strong oversight, supported by highly effective governance, auditing and
quality assurance arrangements. Care staff describe a positive team culture and excellent
opportunities for learning and development.

source_index.name: Caerlan
source_index.summary:
Well-being is good because people receive care from a committed staff team who know them well
 and support them to live active and meaningful lives. People are treated with dignity and respect
 and are supported to make choices about their daily lives. Care staff respect people’s preferences,
 communicating in a patient, professional and kind manner.


 Care and support is good. People have access to healthcare services, meaningful activities and
 opportunities to participate in their local community. Relatives and staff spoke positively about the
 quality of support provided. Comprehensive assessments and care plans, which are reviewed
 regularly, provide care staff with clear guidance to support people safely and effectively.


 The environment is good. It is clean, spacious and designed to meet the sensory needs of people
 living at the service. Bedrooms are personalised and people have access to well-maintained indoor
 and outdoor spaces which supports their wellbeing, privacy and independence. Robust systems
 are in place to monitor health and safety.
Leadership and management is good. The service benefits from established management
arrangements and governance systems. Care staff have the correct training, and recruitment
practices are effective. A range of audits and quality assurance processes are in place.

source_index.name: Castle Court Residential Home
source_index.summary:
Castle Court is a residential care home for older people located in the centre of Chepstow. We
 have awarded a rating of requires improvement for the well-being theme. Many people experience
 positive outcomes because they are supported by a stable and caring staff team who know them
 well. People, relatives and professionals spoke positively about the support provided, the homely
 environment and opportunities for social engagement. However, people are not always supported
 to identify and achieve their personal outcomes because information about their life experiences,
 aspirations and interests is not consistently reflected in care planning.

 We have awarded a rating of requires significant improvement for the care and support,
 environment, and leadership and management themes. People are at risk of inconsistent care
 because personal plans do not always provide reliable or up-to-date information. Medicines
 management arrangements are not sufficiently robust, environmental risks are not always identified
 and reduced, and governance systems have failed to identify and address significant concerns
 affecting people's care, well-being and safety.
 Outcomes for people require significant improvement. As a result, we have issued five Priority
Action Notices, including one relating to the oversight provided by the Responsible Individual.
Three areas previously identified for improvement have been escalated to Priority Action Notices,
and one Priority Action Notice has been re-issued because sufficient improvements have not been
made. The provider has given assurances that immediate action will be taken to address the
concerns identified during the inspection and improve outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Cedar House
source_index.summary:
People experience good well-being and receive person-centred support that promotes choice,
 independence and positive outcomes. Care planning is detailed and people, relatives and
 professionals speak positively about the support provided. People maintain relationships, access
 activities and live in a welcoming environment. Staffing pressures have affected consistency at
 times, although recent recruitment is improving this.

 People receive good care and support that is tailored to their individual needs through detailed care
 planning, effective risk management and strong partnership working with professionals.
 Safeguarding arrangements and Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) processes support
 people's rights and safety. Medication management requires improvement due to recording errors;
 however, enhanced oversight has been implemented to minimise risk.

 The environment is good. People live in a homely, personalised and well-maintained environment
 that supports comfort, dignity and well-being. Ongoing refurbishment and environmental
 improvements enhance quality of life. Robust maintenance systems, regular servicing, fire safety
 arrangements and environmental audits help ensure facilities; equipment and the environment
 remain safe and suitable.
Leadership and Management is good. The service benefits from effective leadership, governance
and quality assurance systems. Audits, quality reviews and Responsible Individual oversight
support continuous improvement. Staff are appropriately trained and skilled to meet people's
needs. Workforce stability remains a challenge; however, active recruitment and development
plans are helping strengthen consistency and sustainability.

source_index.name: Clydach Court
source_index.provider: Rhondda Cynon Taff County Borough Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Clydach Court is a residential care home in Tonypandy, operated by Rhondda Cynon Taff County
 Borough Council. The service is set over two communities, providing support to older adults with
 care needs who live with dementia in one, and supporting adults with a learning disability in the
 other.


 Well-being is good because people are supported to experience positive outcomes which promote
 their overall well-being. Care and support requires improvement because, while people receive
 support from care staff who understand and respond to their individual needs, they do not always
 protect and promote people’s safety. The environment is good because the provider has taken
 action to improve safety, security and oversight within the home. Leadership and management is
 good because effective leadership and strengthened governance arrangements are driving
 improvements across the service.

source_index.name: Clynsaer House
source_index.summary:
Clynsaer House is a large detached house sitting in over 3 acres of beautiful grounds and gardens
 situated in a rural location in Cynghordy, a small village close to the town of Llandovery in
 Carmarthenshire.

 The well-being outcomes for people are “Excellent” as people maintain and improve upon their
 physical, mental, and emotional health because of the exemplary support they receive from staff.

 The care and support people receive is “Good” as people receive high-quality care and support
 from staff who know them well and place them at the heart of the service.

 The environment of which people live is “Good” as people benefit greatly from living in a well
 maintained and safe home which is suitable to their individual needs.

 The leadership and management of the service is “Excellent” as people have very high levels of
 confidence in the provider because leaders promote an exemplary positive culture that is
 supportive, inclusive and respectful.

source_index.name: College Fields
source_index.summary:
College Fields provides high-quality, person-centred care and support to men aged 18 and over
 with mental health needs, including those with forensic histories.

 The well-being outcomes for people are excellent, with highly personalised support enabling
 individuals to build on their strengths, maintain and develop their independence and achieve
 positive outcomes.

 The care and support people receive is excellent. People receive personalised support that is
 tailored to their needs through effective care planning, risk management and professional
 involvement. This helps people develop skills, pursue interests and make informed choices safely.

 The environment is good. People live in a homely, personalised and well-maintained environment
 that supports comfort, dignity and well-being. The provider undertakes regular maintenance and
 repairs, and ensures the home is safe.

 The leadership and management of the service is excellent. The provider has good oversight of the
 service. The management promotes an exceptionally strong, positive culture where people,
 relatives, care staff and professionals feel listened to and valued.

source_index.name: Fairways Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
Fairways Nursing Home is located in a residential area which is off the main road into Trearddur
 Bay, Anglesey.

 Well-being is rated Excellent because people consistently achieve positive outcomes and are
 supported to live fulfilling lives that reflect their individual wishes, preferences and aspirations.
 People are actively involved in decisions about their care, maintain meaningful relationships,
 participate in a wide range of activities and community opportunities, and are supported to remain
 connected to what matters most to them.

 Care and Support is rated Excellent because people receive highly personalised, outcome-focused
 care from skilled staff who understand their needs. Effective assessment, care planning and review
 processes ensure people remain safe and support remain responsive and centred on achieving
 positive outcomes, promoting health, wellbeing, dignity and independence.
Environment is rated Good because people live in a welcoming, comfortable and well-maintained
home that promotes safety, wellbeing and independence. The environment is personalised to
reflect individual preferences, and appropriate equipment and adaptations are in place to support
people's needs and enhance their quality of life.

Leadership and Management is rated Excellent because leaders have established a strong, values-
based culture that promotes rights, inclusion and positive outcomes for people. Effective
governance, robust quality assurance processes, investment in staff development and responsive
management oversight drive continuous improvement and support the delivery of high-quality,
person-centred care.

source_index.name: Glan y Felin
source_index.summary:
Glan Y Felin care home in Pontardawe, supports up to seven adults, living with mental health
 needs and learning disabilities.

 People experience good wellbeing outcomes through consistent, person- centred support from a
 skilled staff team, which promotes independence, choice and control while upholding peoples’
 rights. They have choice and control over their daily lives and receive support to maintain
 relationships, pursue interests.

 The care and support provided is good. People receive personalised care from staff who know
 them well. Personal plans and risk assessments guide staff practice, and people receive support to
 access healthcare and manage their medicines safely.

 The home environment is warm, clean and homely and supports people’s comfort and
 independence. Safety checks are completed and bedrooms are personalised and meet people’s
 needs. The provider has identified further improvements to the garden, kitchen and flooring, which
 do not currently have a significant impact on people.
Leadership and management oversight arrangements are effective. The Responsible Individual
(RI) visits regularly and seeks feedback from people using the service to support ongoing
improvement. Leadership and governance promote a positive culture through audits, feedback and
regular review. Staff feel supported in their role through appropriate training, supervision and
guidance, enabling them to provide safe, consistent and responsive care.

source_index.name: Glasfryn (L'Arche)
source_index.summary:
Glasfryn L’Arche is residential care home which provides assisted living for up to six younger
 adults. It is situated in a rural setting just outside Brecon in the county of Powys.

 Wellbeing is good. People speak positively about the service and the care they receive as they
 have highly effective working relationships with care staff. People are supported to remain as
 healthy as possible as the service links closely with health and medical professionals.

 Care and support are good. Care staff understand people well and use this knowledge to deliver
 care in a dignified, respectful and responsive manner.

 Leadership and management are good. People are supported by care staff with the necessary
 expertise, skills and qualifications to meet people’s care and support needs. The provider follows
 safe recruitment and induction processes.

 The environment is good. People told us they are happy with their surroundings and felt
comfortable living at the service. The atmosphere within the home is calm, relaxed and welcoming.

source_index.name: Graig Y Bedw
source_index.summary:
People achieve excellent outcomes because they receive highly personalised care and support
 from a skilled and committed staff team that understands their individual needs, preferences and
 aspirations. People are happy, settled and actively involved in decisions that affect their daily lives.
 Care staff develop strong relationships with people. They use individual communication
 approaches to ensure people can express their views, make informed choices and maintain control
 over their lives. People benefit from meaningful opportunities that reflect their interests and
 aspirations and are supported to achieve positive physical, emotional and mental well-being
 outcomes.

 People receive a very high standard of care and support informed by comprehensive assessments,
 detailed care planning and effective partnership working with families and professionals. Care staff
 understand people’s needs well and tailor support to promote independence, choice and personal
 development. Care staff support people to access healthcare services, attend appointments and
maintain healthy lifestyles. Medication arrangements are highly effective, with robust systems
ensuring medicines are managed safely and accurately. Safeguarding arrangements are strong
and help ensure people remain safe while maintaining independence.

People live in an exceptionally clean, welcoming and highly personalised environment that
promotes well-being and independence. Bedrooms and living spaces reflect individual preferences
and provide a strong sense of ownership and belonging. Extensive outdoor areas offer
opportunities for recreation, relaxation and emotional well-being. The provider maintains highly
effective health and safety, maintenance and fire safety systems, ensuring people live in a safe and
comfortable home environment.

People benefit from excellent leadership and management arrangements. Managers provide strong
oversight through effective governance, auditing and quality assurance systems. Staff feel valued,
supported and confident in their roles and describe leaders as approachable and responsive.
Recruitment, supervision and training arrangements ensure people receive support from a
knowledgeable workforce. Leaders demonstrate a strong commitment to continuous improvement
and maintaining positive outcomes for people throughout the service.

source_index.name: Hafan Deg Residential Care Home
source_index.provider: Ceredigion County Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Hafan Deg is a residential care home on the outskirts of Lampeter. Well-being is rated as good
 because people receive a service that is highly person centred, that enables them to achieve their
 health and well-being outcomes. People have developed extremely positive relationships with the
 familiar and caring staff.

 Care and support is rated as good because people receive care and support from a team of
 passionate and friendly care workers. Care workers are guided by accurate and individualised
 personal plans that enable them to successfully meet people’s needs.

 The environment is rated as good because people are very comfortable and relaxed throughout the
 home. Improvements have been made to the home and the provider intends to continue these to
 enhance people’s well-being.

 Leadership and management is rated as good because the provider has good oversight of the
 service. Strong leadership ensures people receive high-quality care from a team of dedicated and
 skilled care workers who receive effective support from their managers.

source_index.name: Heathfields Residential Home
source_index.summary:
Overall people experience good wellbeing outcomes and enjoy living in Heathfields Residential
 Home where they feel safe, respected and valued. People told us they feel safe, are treated with
 dignity and respect, and are confident in the current manager’s ability to lead the service effectively.
 Relatives provided positive feedback about the quality of care, the approachable nature of staff and
 the communication maintained by the service. We observed warm and positive interactions
 throughout the inspection and found the atmosphere to be welcoming and person centred. While
 people benefit from positive relationships and support, opportunities remain to further enhance
 well-being through increased access to meaningful activities, occupation and community
 engagement to ensure all people can consistently enjoy fulfilling and enriching experiences.

 People receive good care and support from a committed staff team who know them well and
 understand their individual needs and preferences. A stable core staff team promotes continuity of
 care and enables positive relationships to develop. Care staff work collaboratively with health and
 social care professionals to support people’s health needs and ensure access to appropriate
 healthcare services when required. Regular multidisciplinary meetings help to monitor people's
 well-being and respond to changing needs.
People live in a comfortable and homely environment that supports their safety, comfort and well-
being. We found the home to be welcoming, with communal areas that provide opportunities for
social interaction and engagement. People have personalised their bedrooms to reflect their
preferences and individuality, helping to create familiar and meaningful living spaces.

The manager has developed a good understanding of the service since taking up post and has
identified areas for further development to strengthen outcomes for people. The provider must
ensure the service is delivered consistently in line with its Statement of Purpose so people can be
confident they receive the care, support and opportunities described within this document.

source_index.name: Highgrove Residential Home
source_index.summary:
Highgrove House is a residential care home on the outskirts of Haverfordwest. Well-being is rated
 as good because people receive a service that is highly person centred, that enables them to
 achieve their health and well-being outcomes. People have developed extremely positive
 relationships with the familiar and caring staff.

 Care and support is rated as good because people receive care and support from a team of
 dedicated and understanding care workers. Care workers are guided by accurate and
 individualised personal plans that enable them to meet people’s needs.

 The environment is rated as good because people are comfortable and relaxed throughout the
 home. Improvements have been made to the building, and the provider intends to continue these to
 enhance people’s well-being.

 Leadership and management is rated as good because the provider promotes a positive and
 supportive culture that helps people achieve positive outcomes. Staff described managers as
 approachable and supportive. Whilst improvements are needed to strengthen recording systems
 and policy oversight, these had no impact on people's well-being.

source_index.name: Homelands
source_index.summary:
Homelands is a small residential care service located in Newport, providing specialist residential
 support for adults with mental health needs, learning disabilities, needs associated with Autism
 Spectrum Conditions, and complex or challenging behaviours. The service adopts a person-
 centred, rights-based and trauma-informed approach, supporting people to achieve positive
 outcomes and live fulfilling lives.

 During this inspection, we found consistent evidence of exceptional practice and rated all four
 themes, Well-being, Care and Support, Environment, and Leadership and Management, as
 Excellent.

 People experience excellent wellbeing outcomes and are supported to exercise choice, develop
 independence and participate fully in their communities. Care and support are highly personalised,
 with comprehensive assessment, planning and review processes ensuring individual needs,
 strengths and aspirations remain central to service delivery. The environment is safe, welcoming
 and homely, with extensive countryside surroundings that enhance wellbeing and provide
 meaningful opportunities for recreation and engagement. Strong leadership and management
create a positive culture where people are respected, care staff are valued, and continuous
improvement is embedded throughout the service.

Effective governance, a committed and skilled workforce, and a strong focus on achieving personal
outcomes contribute to consistently high standards of care. Overall, Homelands demonstrates
exceptional practice and delivers excellent outcomes for the people it supports.

source_index.name: Hullah Farm
source_index.summary:
Hullah Farm provides care and support for up to 10 adults with learning disabilities, autism and
 complex support needs. People live in a range of accommodation including cottages, apartments
 and farmhouse accommodation. Well-being is excellent because we found people experience
 exceptionally positive outcomes and benefit from highly personalised care and support. Strong
 communication approaches help people make choices and exercise control over their daily lives.
 People are supported to participate in meaningful activities, maintain important relationships and
 engage in their local communities. The environment is good because the premises is well
 maintained and supports people to achieve their well-being outcomes.

 Care planning and positive behaviour support (PBS) are excellent. Documentation is detailed,
 person-centred and focused on improving quality of life and helping people achieve their personal
 outcomes. The service works in partnership with families and professionals and receives
 consistently positive feedback about the care and support provided. Leadership and management
 arrangements are also excellent. Governance systems support a culture of learning, reflection and
 continuous improvement, with a strong focus on achieving positive outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Kinmel Lodge
source_index.summary:
Kinmel Lodge is a residential home for people with dementia. It is located in Kinmel Bay close to
 local amenities.

 Wellbeing is excellent because people are involved and included in making choices and decisions
 which affect them. They are supported to look after their own health and wellbeing, achieve their
 outcomes and have an extensive range of activities and opportunities available to them. They are
 valued as individuals and benefit from positive relationships with friends, families and their pets.

 Care and support is good because care plans are person centred for staff to follow. Health needs
 are met with professionals involved when required.

 People live in a good environment with ongoing improvements. The home has areas of interest for
 people to enjoy and there is a private garden area.

 Leadership and management of the service is good. Staff work well as a team and feel very well
 supported and are valued. They receive training and have opportunities to develop in their roles.
 Systems and processes are more robust providing effective oversight of the service. The
responsible individual (RI) carries out three monthly visits and six-monthly quality of care reviews,
identifying areas to move the service forward. A positive and compassionate culture is promoted.

source_index.name: Llandaff House Care Home
source_index.summary:
Llandaff House is a residential care home registered for up to 21 adults situated in the village of
 Llangennech, on the outskirts of Llanelli, Carmarthenshire.

 People experience good well-being outcomes as experienced care staff who know them well
 support them to maintain their physical, mental health and emotional well-being.

 The care and support is good as care staff always place people’s health and well-being at the heart
 of the service.

 The environment is good as people live in well maintained safe environment where they feel at
 home.

 The leadership and management is good as the management team has oversight and governance
 arrangements that promote a positive and compassionate culture at the service.

source_index.name: Llannerch Grange
source_index.summary:
Llannerch Grange is in a quiet residential area, within walking distance of the beach and local
 shops and amenities.

 People experience excellent well-being because they receive highly personalised support that
 promotes choice, independence and positive relationships. They shape their routines, pursue
 interests at home and in the community, and take positive risks such as volunteering, work, sport,
 cooking, gardening and planning a holiday. People feel safe, know how to raise concerns and live
 in a homely environment which reflects their identities and gives them ownership.

 Care and support is good because staff understand people well, work with professionals and
 respond to changing needs. Personal plans and risk assessments are detailed, reviewed regularly
 and linked to people’s goals. Medicines, infection prevention and environmental safety are
 managed effectively.

 People live in a good environment because the home is comfortable, welcoming, well maintained
 and personalised. People contribute to its appearance and use the indoor and outdoor spaces in
ways which reflect their interests.

Leadership and management is good because leaders maintain oversight through audits,
Responsible Individual (RI) visits, management meetings and reporting. Staff are safely recruited,
trained and supported, and the service has a stable workforce and positive culture.

source_index.name: Llantrisant Care Home
source_index.summary:
Llantrisant Care Home provides care and support to adults requiring residential or nursing care, set
 in the countryside near Llantrisant.


 We have not considered the inspection themes in full and have focused on specific areas of the
 service. Well-being is good because people receive care and support which promotes their rights,
 independence and overall wellbeing. Care and support is good because people receive safe,
 person-centred care from care staff who are kind, respectful and responsive to their needs. The
