 environment is good because the provider takes appropriate action to manage identified
 environmental risks while maintaining a suitable home for people. Leadership and management is
 good because effective governance, oversight and quality assurance arrangements support
 positive outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Llys Gwyn Residential Home
source_index.summary:
Llys Gwyn is a well-established care home set in extensive private grounds. It is a 10-minute drive
 to the M4 motorway and is within easy reach of Swansea, Bridgend, Porthcawl and Cardiff. The
 service provides accommodation and personal care for older adults, including people living with
 dementia.

 People experience excellent well-being outcomes and are supported to maintain their
 independence and make choices about their daily lives. They maintain meaningful relationships
 with family and friends and participate in a wide range of activities that promote their well-being and
 social inclusion.

 People receive excellent personalised care and support from a dedicated and highly skilled staff
 team. Personal plans are comprehensive, regularly reviewed and reflect people's wishes,
 preferences and outcomes. Staff work effectively with health and social care professionals to
ensure people receive the support they need. Medication and infection prevention arrangements
are robust.

People live in a clean, comfortable and welcoming environment that supports their needs.
Bedrooms are comfortable, personalised and homely, helping people feel settled and secure. The
provider continues to invest in improvements to the premises.

Leadership and management are excellent. The service benefits from strong leadership, effective
governance arrangements and a stable workforce. Quality assurance systems support continuous
improvement and feedback from people, relatives, staff and professionals is overwhelmingly
positive.

source_index.name: Llys Y Seren
source_index.summary:
Llys y Seren is a purpose-built residential care home in Port Talbot that sits in the heart of the local
 community. People experience outstanding well-being outcomes through highly personalised
 support that promotes choice, independence and inclusion. They actively influence their care and
 daily lives and benefit from meaningful activities, strong community connections and positive
 relationships. Feedback demonstrates people enjoy fulfilling lives, remain safe and achieve
 outcomes that matter to them.
 Care and support is excellent. People receive exceptionally responsive, person-centred care from a
 skilled and compassionate staff team. Care plans are regularly reviewed and tailored to individual
 needs, while safeguarding, medication management and infection control arrangements are robust.
 People, families and professionals consistently praise the quality of support, with staff described as
 going “above and beyond”.
 The environment is excellent, People live in a dementia-friendly environment that enhances
 independence, safety and quality of life. The home is spacious, accessible and exceptionally well
 maintained, with specialist facilities and attractive outdoor spaces promoting well-being. Strong
 maintenance and health and safety systems ensure people benefit from a safe, comfortable and
 welcoming home.
 Leadership and Management is Excellent, People benefit from inspirational leadership, strong
governance and a culture of continuous improvement. Effective oversight systems ensure high
standards of care, while a skilled and stable workforce consistently delivers positive outcomes.
Relatives and professionals express high confidence in the service, describing the management
team as approachable, responsive and committed to excellence.

source_index.name: Llys y Tywysog Care Home
source_index.summary:
Llys y Tywysog is a residential care home located in Grovesend, Swansea. The home provides
 accommodation and support for up to 54 people with residential and dementia care needs across
 two floors. The service also provides respite care.

 Well-being is excellent because people have a strong voice in how the service is run and receive
 highly personalised support that reflects what matters to them. They are supported to maintain
 relationships, pursue meaningful interests, influence decision-making and take positive risks,
 resulting in people feeling safe, connected, valued and engaged in daily life.

 Care and support is excellent because people receive highly personalised care from staff who
 know them exceptionally well and understand their individual needs and preferences.
 Comprehensive care planning, effective risk management, strong partnership working and robust
 safeguarding arrangements support positive outcomes for people. High standards of medication
management and infection prevention further ensure people receive safe and consistent care.

The environment is excellent because people live in a high-quality and well-maintained home that
promotes comfort, dignity and well-being. The environment offers a range of facilities and spaces
that enhance people's daily lives, while ongoing investment, effective maintenance and robust
health and safety arrangements ensure people experience positive outcomes in a safe setting.

Leadership and management is excellent because strong, visible leaders promote a positive culture
and use effective governance systems to drive continuous improvement. Feedback is actively
sought and acted upon, while robust oversight provides assurance of high-quality care. Staff are
well supported, highly trained, recognised for their contributions and motivated to deliver excellent
outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Maesllewellyn
source_index.provider: Carmarthenshire County Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
Maes Llewelyn Residential Care Home, in Newcastle Emlyn, provides care and accommodation for
 up to 40 people across five units.

 Well-being is “Good” as people have control over daily life and receive respectful support to
 maintain their health, relationships and interests.

 Care and Support is “Good” as care staff know people well and provide consistent, person-centred
 care. Effective safeguarding and risk-management systems help people feel safe and protect their
 rights.

 The Environment is “Good” as people live in comfortable, personalised accommodation that
 promotes privacy, independence and social contact.

 Leadership and Management is “Good” as Leaders promote an open culture, support care staff
 effectively and use strong governance and feedback systems to improve the service.

source_index.name: Meddyg Care Dementia Home - Rhyl
source_index.summary:
Meddyg Care Dementia Home - Rhyl is in a quiet residential area, close to the seafront and local
 cafes, shops and amenities.

 People have good well-being because staff know people well and support them to make everyday
 choices. People take part in activities that reflect their interests and benefit from meaningful
 engagement, positive relationships and a dementia-friendly environment. The service promotes the
 Welsh language and culture.

 People receive good care and support because detailed personal plans provide clear, risk-
 assessed guidance for timely, respectful and dignified support that meets their needs. Medication
 and infection prevention arrangements are safe. Relatives and professionals are positive about the
 manager and the quality of care provided in the home.

 People achieve good outcomes because the environment is clean, secure, and well maintained,
 with quiet areas, sensory features, and accessible outdoor space. There is ample equipment,
 supplies and facilities to meet people’s needs.
Leadership and management support people’s outcomes through governance systems that identify
issues and actions required. The provider has strengthened training since the last inspection. The
manager ensures good staffing levels and deployment support people’s needs.

source_index.name: Millbrook Care Home Ltd
source_index.summary:
Millbrook Care Home is a residential service located in Blackwood. The service provides care and
 support in a homely and welcoming environment where people are encouraged to maintain their
 independence, make choices about their daily lives and enjoy meaningful experiences.

 We rated Well-being as Excellent because people experience positive outcomes. People are
 treated with dignity and respect and have extensive opportunities to take part in meaningful
 activities, maintain important relationships and achieve positive physical, emotional and social well-
 being outcomes. Care staff know people well and support them to live fulfilling lives in line with their
 preferences and aspirations. People enjoy a rich programme of activities and maintain strong
 connections with their families and community.

 We rated Care and Support as Excellent because people receive highly personalised care from
 attentive and knowledgeable care staff who know them well.

 We rated Environment as Excellent because people live in a clean, comfortable and well-
maintained home that promotes their well-being and independence.

We rated Leadership and Management as Good because the service provider has effective
governance arrangements and supports a positive culture focused on achieving good outcomes for
people.

source_index.name: Parkview House
source_index.summary:
Well-being is rated good because people are supported to live healthy, safe and meaningful lives
 with choice and control over daily decisions. People told the inspector they were happy living at the
 service. Individuals access community activities, maintain relationships and are supported through
 positive risk-taking. No safeguarding concerns, notifications or open compliance issues were
 identified. Areas for development include strengthening the Welsh language active offer and
 evidencing activities through photographs and displays.

 Care and Support is rated good because people receive person-centred care supported by current
 care planning, risk management and multidisciplinary involvement. Safeguarding, infection
 prevention and activity provision were compliant. Medication systems were generally effective with
 regular audits in place; however, medication recording issues indicate the provider should continue
 to demonstrate audit actions are reducing risk.

 Environment is rated good because accommodation is suitable, well maintained and supports
 people’s well-being outcomes. Most fire safety actions had been completed, with remaining works
 subject to clear plans and timescales.
Leadership and Management is rated good because governance, quality assurance and Care Staff
development arrangements were effective. However, significant reliance on agency Care Staff
requires ongoing monitoring to maintain continuity of care. Overall, the service was meeting
expectations and achieving positive outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Pen Y Graig
source_index.summary:
Pen-Y-Graig offers a family home for people with physical and mental disabilities. They are cared
 for by a family and people feel they are part of the family. People have access to transport and
 local amenities.

 Well-being for people is good. They attend day services if they choose, the people attending enjoy
 these services. People are supported to be as independent as possible. People live a full life,
 helping with the animals on the small holding and attending local events.

 Care and support are good. People access health care in a timely way as the family know them
 well and can anticipate their needs. People receive their medications as prescribed. There has
 been a bereavement in the family, people received support in a sensitive way and were able to
 attend the funeral.

 The environment is good. The home is a busy family home and small holding. People assist with
 chores. The home is subject to ongoing maintenance; grants have been received to upgrade
people’s bedrooms and facilities.

Leadership and management are good. The family, and new manager, are still adjusting post
bereavement. They are updated with training and supervision and continue to be happy supporting
people.

source_index.name: Pen-coed Residential Care Home
source_index.summary:
Pen-coed is a residential care home for adults situated in a village in Pembrokeshire, close to the
 well-known coastal towns of Tenby and Saundersfoot. Up to twenty-five people can be
 accommodated in a two-storey building.

 Overall people achieve good wellbeing outcomes and benefit from care that is compassionate,
 respectful and focused on their individual needs. People are supported to maintain their health,
 remain connected to those important to them and engage in experiences that enhance their quality
 of life.

 Care and support are good. People receive good quality care and support from a stable, caring and
 knowledgeable staff team. Strong healthcare partnerships and positive relationships between staff
 and people contribute to positive outcomes for people living at the service. While improvements are
 required in some areas of care planning and documentation, these issues are recognised by
 management and are being addressed and have not impacted on the good quality care people
 receive.

 The environment is good. People live in a safe, comfortable and supportive environment that
promotes their wellbeing. The provider has made significant improvements to the front and
entrance of the building. Ongoing investment and development plans demonstrate a commitment to
continuous improvement, and we have been assured that improvements to the décor and fabric of
the home will be addressed as part of the ongoing improvement plans.

Leadership and management are good. The service is well led, with a strong commitment to
person-centred care and positive outcomes for people. Leadership is viewed positively by relatives
and staff, and effective systems are in place to support the quality and safety of the service.

source_index.name: Picton Court
source_index.summary:
People achieve excellent well-being outcomes because their care is person centred and individual
 needs, likes and dislikes are considered fully. Care staff understand what matters to individuals and
 consistently anticipate their needs and preferences. People benefit from a wide range of
 meaningful activities that significantly enhance their overall well-being.

 Care and support are excellent. Care staff know people extremely well and deliver care with
 kindness, dignity, and genuine warmth. Their strong relationships with individuals ensure that
 support is tailored, responsive, and consistently of a very high standard.

 The environment is good, offering a warm, comfortable, and welcoming home that meets people’s
 needs reliably. The provider carries out regular maintenance and repairs, ensuring the setting
 remains safe and supportive for those who live there. The environment meets people's needs
 effectively and contributes positively to their overall quality of life.


 Leadership and management are excellent. The service is very well-led, with a strong and positive
 culture that promotes the well-being of both the people supported and the staff team. Staff have
 robust training, recruitment practices are effective, and governance and oversight systems are in
place to support the running of the service.

source_index.name: Plas Cwmcynfelin Ltd
source_index.summary:
Plas Cwmcynfelin Limited is a well-established care home where people achieve excellent
 outcomes because they receive highly personalised care and support from a skilled, committed and
 well-supported staff team. People are treated with dignity and respect and are encouraged to make
 choices about their daily lives. They maintain important relationships, take part in meaningful
 activities and are supported to achieve their personal goals and aspirations.

 People benefit from an excellent environment that is warm, welcoming and homely that promotes
 independence, choice and well-being. Bedrooms and communal areas reflect individual
 preferences, and the gardens provide opportunities for relaxation, recreation and meaningful
 occupation. Welsh language and culture are embedded throughout the home and support people to
 communicate in their preferred language.

 Leaders are visible, approachable and provide excellent leadership. They work alongside care
 staff, promote a positive culture and invest significantly in workforce development. Staff receive
extensive training and support to develop their skills and careers, which has a positive impact on
outcomes for people. Robust governance and quality assurance systems ensure the service is
continually reviewed and improved.

Care and support is excellent. Professionals, relatives and people living at the home consistently
speak positively about the quality of care, communication and leadership. The home demonstrates
a clear commitment to continuous improvement and delivering high-quality, person-centred care

source_index.name: Primrose Cottage
source_index.summary:
Primrose Cottage is a small care home situated in the Vale of Glamorgan. People living at the
 service have easy access to good transport links and local amenities, which they frequently use.
 People experience excellent well-being outcomes because they live healthily and safely with
 control over their lives. They experience highly positive outcomes because they feel valued,
 respected and included. They receive support with meaningful activities, communication needs and
 health needs to achieve their personal aspirations and goals. Care and support outcomes are
 good, people experience successful health, well-being and safety outcomes because they receive
 person-centred support from care staff who know them well.

 The service environment is good, and supports people’s daily routines in clean, well-maintained
 and homely premises. The accommodation supports people's well-being outcomes by providing an
 environment where they experience independence, accessibility, choice and control.

 Leadership and management are good. We found there to be mostly effective quality assurance,
 with strong engagement, and clear accountability resulting in a provider committed to service
 improvement. Governance arrangements are generally effective and have contributed to improved
 outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Prince Llewellyn Farm
source_index.summary:
People’s well-being outcomes are consistently positive, reflecting the high levels of skill,
 compassion, and dedication demonstrated by care staff. Care staff provide person-centred support
 enabling people to achieve their personal outcomes, make informed choices, and maximise their
 independence. As a result, people are empowered to lead meaningful and fulfilling lives, with
 opportunities to exercise choice and maintain control over matters that are important to them.

 People receive an excellent standard of care and support. Care staff demonstrate a comprehensive
 understanding of people’s needs, preferences, and aspirations, enabling them to consistently
 deliver high-quality, person-centred care. Personal plans are exceptionally detailed, accurate, and
 regularly reviewed, ensuring they remain relevant, responsive, and effective in meeting people’s
 changing needs and desired outcomes.

 The environment is good. The detached home is set in a peaceful rural location, with well-
 maintained indoor and outdoor areas. Systems are in place to promote safety. Communal areas
 are welcoming, and people can personalise their bedrooms to reflect their preferences.

 Leadership and management arrangements are strong. Staff feel well supported and receive
ongoing training. Effective governance systems, including regular Responsible Individual (RI) visits
and quality of care reviews, provide oversight and drive improvement. Robust recruitment
processes help ensure staff are suitable to work with vulnerable people.

source_index.name: Princes Court
source_index.summary:
Princes Court is a residential service in the Roath area of Cardiff. It supports up to five adults with
 mental health needs to build confidence, develop independence and achieve their goals through
 personalised, recovery-focused support.

 Well-being is excellent. People are at the heart of the service and receive personalised support
 which promotes choice, independence and well-being. Positive relationships with staff help people
 feel valued, included and empowered to live fulfilling lives.

 Care and support is excellent. People receive highly individualised support from a skilled and
 dedicated staff team who know them well. Support is flexible, responsive and focused on what
 matters most to each person, helping them achieve positive outcomes and greater independence.

 Environment is excellent. People live in a highly responsive and inclusive environment that is
continually adapted to meet their needs. Innovative solutions, meaningful involvement in decision-
making and a strong focus on independence promote belonging and well-being.

Leadership and management is excellent. Strong, compassionate leadership creates a positive
culture where people feel valued and listened to. Managers are approachable and committed to
ensuring people receive high-quality support and the best possible outcomes.

source_index.name: Rachel Kathryn Residential Home
source_index.summary:
Rachel Kathryn is a small residential care service for up to four people. It is set in large grounds in
 a quiet, semi-rural area. The service aims to provide a family-like home where people have
 independence, privacy, dignity and choice.


 Well-being is rated excellent. People have meaningful choice and control over their daily lives. Staff
 support them to build on their strengths, achieve personal goals, maintain important relationships
 and take part in activities that matter to them. Care and support is rated good. Care staff know
 people well, and detailed personal plans guide consistent, responsive support. The environment is
 rated good because the service is clean, comfortable and homely. People influence how their home
 is decorated and use indoor and outdoor spaces that support their interests and independence.
 Leadership and management is also rated good. Leaders are approachable and use monitoring,
 audits and feedback to maintain quality and identify improvements for ongoing development.

source_index.name: Redcroft Care Home
source_index.summary:
Redcroft Care Home is a small detached residential care home in Colwyn Bay, providing
 accommodation and care for up to 14 people. The home is located in a quiet residential area with
 access to local amenities.

 Overall, people experience positive well-being. Staff provide person-centred support that promotes
 dignity, respect and choice, enabling people to maintain control over their daily lives and enjoy a
 good quality of life.

 Care and support are effective. Personal plans and risk assessments provide clear guidance on
 people's needs, preferences and goals. Improvements have been made to care planning, risk
 management and medication storage since the last inspection.
People live in a clean, well-maintained and suitably equipped environment. Significant investment
and progress has been made in addressing environmental concerns we identified at last inspection.

Leadership and management are effective. The provider has addressed the concerns identified at
the previous inspection and has robust quality assurance systems in place to monitor the service,
drive improvement and support positive outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Riversdale
source_index.summary:
The service provides excellent support for people’s well-being and benefits from highly effective
 leadership and management. People have a strong voice and play an active role in shaping the
 service through regular engagement with leaders. The service uses an innovative approach to co-
 production through its ‘Welsh Quality Together Forum’. This gives people a genuine voice in the
 running of the service and enables them to influence decisions, developments and improvements
 that affect their daily lives. We found a positive and inclusive culture where people are respected,
 valued and supported to achieve personal outcomes. Leaders demonstrate strong oversight and a
 clear commitment to continuous improvement.

 People receive good care and support from staff who know them well and understand their needs,
 wishes, and aspirations. Staff work closely with health and social care professionals to promote
 positive outcomes, recovery and independence. Staff support people to take part in activities that
 reflect their interests and goals, helping them develop confidence, maintain relationships and
access their local community.

The environment is good. People live in a safe and comfortable home with access to communal
and private spaces. The provider has continued to invest in improvements since the last inspection,
and health and safety arrangements are well managed.

source_index.name: Shillings Care
source_index.summary:
The majority of people and relatives we spoke to gave positive feedback regarding Shillings care
 home. We saw evidence of involvement of external agencies to help with decision making and best
 interests, and there is evidence to show some outcomes are being achieved. But people’s well-
 being requires improvement. This is because information available to people is sometimes incorrect
 and cannot be relied upon. There are limited activities evidenced as being offered or encouraged to
 enable people to engage with others, to support a sense of well-being.

 People have personal plans in place which we saw are updated, when required. We saw people
 receive support from health professionals when needed and daily records show care and support is
 delivered in line with plans. However, we found improvements with medication management
 continue and this requires improvement.
The environment is clean. Relatives and professionals describe the service as homely and
welcoming. Infection control is considered and there are some health and safety measures in
place. However, we found oversight and audits of the environment failed to identify potential risks
and improvements needed and this requires improvement.

There is a manager and Responsible Individual (RI) in place. Whilst we note the provider is
responsive and has tried to seek external support to aid in quality, the provider has continued to fail
to drive, embed and sustain improvements from previous inspections. Governance and oversight of
quality is insufficient as the systems in place have failed to identify improvements and therefore
systems cannot be relied upon as being accurate and effective. This requires significant
improvement.

source_index.name: The Manor House St.Hilary
source_index.summary:
The Manor House is based in St Hilary and can accommodate 30 people with a range of nursing
 and personal care needs. This inspection was unannounced. There is a Responsible Individual (RI)
 for the service and a manager who is registered with Social Care Wales (SCW).

 People receive exceptional care and support from a skilled, experienced, and committed staff team.
 Effective staffing arrangements ensure people’s needs are consistently met, resulting in excellent
 outcomes for their wellbeing.

 Leadership and management are admirable and promote a culture of inclusivity, respect and
 transparency. Staff are highly valued and benefit from effective training, ongoing professional
 development and clear guidance to support them in their roles. Managers provide first-rate visible
 leadership and are actively involved in the day-to-day running of the service. Robust governance
 arrangements effectively monitor quality, drive continuous improvement and ensure care is
 delivered in line with people’s wishes and preferences. Feedback from people’s families,
 representatives and staff demonstrate excellent levels of satisfaction, with the service described as
“fantastic” and “we couldn’t ask for more, it truly is everything and more”. People live in a well-
maintained and welcoming environment decorated to an extremely high standard and provides
great facilities, including attractive outdoor areas for people to sit and enjoy.

source_index.name: The Oaks
source_index.summary:
People’s well-being requires improvement because they do not always have choice and control
 over their daily lives or receive support that consistently promoted their rights, independence and
 personal outcomes. Records and observations demonstrate people’s physical, mental and
 emotional well-being needs are not always met in a consistent or person-centred manner.
 Furthermore, people are placed at risk of harm because management oversight of care and
 support is not sufficiently robust.

 Care and support require significant improvement because personal plans, risk assessments and
 supporting records do not always reflect people's current needs, preferences or risks. Records
 relating to personal care, nutrition, hydration, repositioning, falls and incidents are incomplete or
 inaccurate. Medicines management arrangements are not sufficiently robust to ensure medicines
 are received, stored, monitored and administered safely. Infection prevention and control measures
 are not consistently effective.
The environment required significant improvement as poor management of the premises places
people's dignity, safety and well-being at risk. The provider has not ensured the accommodation is
maintained to an appropriate standard, and a number of environmental concerns identified during
this inspection demonstrated a lack of effective oversight and maintenance.

Leadership and management require significant improvement as governance, oversight and quality
assurance arrangements are ineffective. The Responsible Individual (RI) has not ensured robust
organisational systems are in place to support the safe and effective operation of the service.
Management oversight is weak, with auditing, monitoring and quality assurance processes failing to
identify a range of concerns relating to personal planning, falls oversight, medicines management,
record keeping, risk management, training, staff deployment and the environment.

source_index.name: The Old Vicarage Private Nursing Home
source_index.summary:
The Old Vicarage Private Nursing Home caters for people requiring nursing or personal care and
 may also offer a day service. It is set within its own grounds in Sketty, close to Swansea City
 Centre and the Gower. The service hires transport to enable people to access community facilities.

 People experience a good quality of life. Their well-being is enhanced through meaningful activities
 and strong social connections. Care staff treat people with warmth, dignity and respect.

 People receive a good standard of care and support which helps keep them active and healthy.
 However, personal plans and risk assessments need improvement to better reflect individual
 needs, preferences and goals.

 People live in a safe environment that is continuously being improved and developed. It is furnished
and decorated to a good standard and includes homely features people identify with.

The home is managed effectively by the Responsible Individual (RI), with the support of a deputy
manager, clinical lead, nursing team and care managers. Staff feel motivated and supported in their
roles. The RI closely monitors the quality of the service and makes changes to improve people’s
experiences.

source_index.name: Thompson Court
source_index.summary:
Thompson Court is a small residential home, situated in the Canton area of Cardiff. The service
 supports adults with mental health needs, learning disabilities and autism to build skills, confidence
 and independence. Support is tailored to each person and aims to help them achieve their goals
 and move towards more independent living where possible.

 Well-being is excellent because people experience exceptionally positive well-being outcomes.
 They are supported to have meaningful control over their lives, achieve ambitious personal goals,
 maintain important relationships and participate in opportunities that enrich their lives.

 Care and support is excellent because people receive highly personalised, strengths-based
 support. Care staff promote independence, well-being and choice, whilst providing outstanding
 advocacy, proactive healthcare support and effective risk management.

 Environment is good because people benefit from a safe, comfortable and homely environment that
supports their well-being and independence. The home is personalised, well maintained and
welcoming. Effective health and safety measures help ensure people feel safe and secure in their
home.

Leadership and management is excellent because the service is exceptionally well led, with
supportive leaders, a skilled and stable workforce, and strong quality assurance systems that drive
continuous improvement and positive outcomes for people.

source_index.name: Three Cliffs Care Home
source_index.summary:
Three Cliffs Care Home is in a rural location along the Gower coastline. It overlooks Three Cliffs
 Bay, and people find the view to be both stunning and peaceful. People require transport to access
 community facilities. The service offers transport to support visits and help people stay connected.

 People are content in their home. Care staff provide the physical and emotional support people
 need to promote their health and well-being. People are positively occupied and stimulated through
 their social interactions and meaningful activities.

 The service works effectively with medical and specialist services to help people stay healthy.
 Managers closely monitor practice and drive improvements where necessary. People receive the
 right level of support with their medication, and good hygiene practices help reduce infection risks.
People live in a safe environment. Private and communal rooms are spacious, personalised and
well maintained. There is ample space for people to relax and spend time with others. Regular
enhancements to the décor help keep the environment stimulating.

The service has good leadership and management. The team is open and responsive to feedback,
which helps things run smoothly. Staff are motivated and content in their roles. The Responsible
Individual (RI) monitors standards carefully and looks to make continuous improvements.

source_index.name: Treeside
source_index.summary:
People receive exceptionally personalised support that promotes choice, independence wherever
 possible, safety and wellbeing. Staff have an excellent understanding of people’s needs and
 communication, ensuring they remain central to decision-making. Strong safeguarding, positive risk
 management, meaningful activities and a highly adapted living environment support consistently
 positive outcomes and an enhanced quality of life.

 Care and support is excellent, highly individualised, outcome-focused and delivered by skilled staff
 who understand people’s unique needs. Robust safeguarding, effective care planning and strong
 multidisciplinary working ensure consistently positive outcomes. Medicines are managed safely,
 and effective infection prevention measures help maintain a safe, healthy and dignified home
 environment.

 The environment is excellent. It has been successfully adapted to meet people’s individual needs,
 preferences and wellbeing outcomes. Specialist facilities, personalised spaces and therapeutic
 resources promote independence, comfort and quality of life. Robust maintenance, health and
 safety checks, and ongoing investment ensure the environment remains safe, well maintained and
 responsive.
Leadership and management is excellent, with strong oversight, quality assurance and a
commitment to continuous improvement. Care workers are well trained, supported and very
dedicated to deliver consistently high-quality care, and they speak positively about management. A
positive culture, effective partnership working and person-centred values ensure excellent
outcomes and sustained service excellence.

source_index.name: Ty Clyd
source_index.provider: Caerphilly County Borough Council Adults and Children's Services
source_index.summary:
People living at Ty Clyd achieve good positive well-being outcomes through person-centred care,
 meaningful activities, strong healthcare support and respectful staff relationships. People receive
 good, person-centred care that promotes health, dignity and independence. Strong safeguarding
 and healthcare support contribute to positive outcomes.

 The environment is good. Promoting independence, well-being and social engagement. People
 benefit from suitable facilities, personalised living spaces and effective safety measures.
 Leadership and management arrangements support good quality care through stable leadership,
 effective monitoring and a positive staff culture.

 Greater oversight of records, training, medication competency assessments and personal plans is
 needed. Due to this, three areas for improvement were identified and issued during inspection
around personal plans, medication management and oversight.

source_index.name: Ty Cysgu
source_index.summary:
Ty Cysgu is a small respite service providing care and support for adults with a range of needs,
 including learning disabilities, physical disabilities, and mental health conditions.

 People receive high quality, person-centred care and support that is tailored to their individual
 needs, preferences and personal outcomes. Staff know people well and support them to make
 choices, develop independent living skills and participate in meaningful activities. Personal plans
 are detailed, regularly reviewed and provide clear guidance to support consistent care.

 The service benefits from effective leadership and management arrangements. Governance and
 quality assurance systems support the monitoring and development of the service. Staff are
 appropriately recruited, trained and supported, and speak positively about the culture within the
 service. The Responsible Individual (RI) maintains regular oversight and works closely with the
 management team to promote positive outcomes for people.

 People stay in a clean, comfortable and well-maintained environment that supports their well-being
 and individual needs. An ongoing programme of maintenance and repair helps ensure the
 environment, facilities and equipment remain safe.

source_index.name: Ty Eirin
source_index.summary:
Ty Eirin is a purpose-built care home in Tonyrefail providing nursing and residential care for up to
 90 people.

 People experience excellent well-being outcomes. Staff know people extremely well and provide
 compassionate, respectful support that promotes dignity, choice, independence and rights. People
 maintain relationships with family and friends and enjoy a wide range of meaningful activities.

 People receive excellent care and support from a dedicated and highly skilled staff team.
 Comprehensive assessments and detailed personal plans help ensure support is personalised and
 reflects what matters most to people. Staff respond promptly to people's needs and work closely
 with healthcare professionals to promote positive outcomes.

 The environment is excellent. The home is welcoming, safe and accessible, with a variety of
 attractive communal and outdoor areas that support social interaction, independence and well-
 being. Bedrooms are comfortable, personalised and homely, helping people feel settled and
 secure.
Leadership and management are excellent. The experienced management team promotes a
positive culture where people are at the centre of the service. Staff receive regular training,
supervision and support, and robust quality assurance systems help ensure high standards are
maintained and drive continuous improvement.

source_index.name: Ty Machen
source_index.summary:
Ty Machen is a small residential care home for adults, set in a quiet residential area near local
 shops and amenities. The service is provided in a single level property with level access to the front
 and rear gardens.

 Well-being, care and support, environment and leadership and management are rated as excellent.
 We found evidence of an outstanding commitment to delivering an exceptional standard of care
 and support to people, to enable them to improve their independence and control over their lives
 and achieve highly personalised wellbeing goals and outcomes. The environment is monitored and
 updated in line with people’s preferences, needs and enables them to achieve what matters to
 them. We found the highly effective leadership and management drives continual learning and
 development across all areas of the service, embedding a culture of reflection and empowerment.

source_index.name: Ty Melin Residential Home for the Elderly
source_index.summary:
Since the last inspection the service has implemented several improvements, these consider well-
 being, care and support, the environment and leadership and management. The service has
 listened to feedback and focused on people’s well-being and experience. They have implemented
 new activities and places for people to socialise. A new activities staff member provides regular
 opportunity for people to access the community. Goals and aspirations are now more person-
 centred, the service continue to work on this and drive improvement. One relative said, “Could not
 be more grateful for the service they provide, and the way in which it is delivered.” Well-being is
 ‘Good’.

 Care and Support is ‘Good’. Plans are detailed and informative. Risk assessments are in place
 which identify clear ways to reduce risks. Medication is appropriately administered in a safe way.
 Infection control measures are in place, and the service are developing improved systems to
maintain sufficient oversight of this. Care staff are consistent and we received consistent high
praise for them. One relative said “The most important thing for us is that the staff really care about
X.”

The service has worked hard to address improvements in the Environment. Areas where we
identified risk have been actioned and there is ongoing work in relation to decorating and managing
wear and tear. The service has implemented some systems to help plan and prioritise work
however we found ongoing work is required to ensure accurate, sufficient and effective oversight is
maintained. The Environment ‘Requires Improvement’

The service has listened to our feedback and made several changes to improve the service. We
saw a clear financial investment to drive improvement. The Responsible Individual (RI), team of
managers and administrators have worked together to take action, positively impacting people’s
experience of the service. Whilst we note some improvements in relation to effective and
sustainable oversight, Leadership and Management is ‘Good’ overall.

source_index.name: Ty Pentyrch
source_index.summary:
Ty Pentyrch is a care home located in a rural area of Cardiff. The service supports people living
 with a learning disability, those on the autistic spectrum and other associated mental health needs.

 People achieve excellent well-being outcomes at Ty Pentyrch because they are empowered to
 thrive, with numerous opportunities to maintain, develop, and explore their interests, strengths, and
 skills. This ensures people experience a strong sense of purpose, achievement, and belonging.

 People receive excellent care and support because the provider conducts highly effective
 assessments of whether they can meet the person’s needs alongside those of people already
 accessing the service, before offering a service.

 The environment at Ty Pentyrch is excellent because the service provider actively seeks out new
 technology and creative solutions to help people live with as few restrictions as possible. This
 allows people to live safely in the community and achieve their personal outcomes.
Leadership and management is excellent, because the service provider has strong working
relationships with others in the sector, sharing best practice, and leaders confidently steer the
service through challenges where necessary.

source_index.name: Ty Ross Care Home
source_index.summary:
Ty Ross is an established care home service in Treherbert providing residential care for adults,
 including people living with dementia. Following a change of provider at the end of May 2026, there
 has also been a change of Responsible Individual.

 Well-being is good because people live safely, maintain their independence and take part in
 meaningful activities that support positive outcomes. People benefit from consistent care and
 support that promotes their health, well-being and quality of life.

 Care and support are good. Staff know people well and understand their individual needs,
 preferences and routines. They work effectively with health and social care professionals to support
 positive outcomes for people, and stable staffing helps people develop trusting and supportive
 relationships.

 Environment is good. Significant improvements have been made since the previous inspection. The
 provider has addressed environmental and health and safety concerns, and people now benefit
from a safer, more comfortable environment.

Leadership and management require improvement. Positive changes have been made following
the recent change in ownership, and staff speak positively about visible and accessible leaders.
However, further work is needed to strengthen arrangements for staff training, supervision,
appraisal and communication to ensure they are consistently effective.

source_index.name: Willow Hall Residential Care Home limited
source_index.provider: WILLOW HALL RESIDENTIAL CARE HOME LIMITED
source_index.summary:
Willow Hall is located close to the centre of Caernarfon and is within reach of local amenities.

 People's wellbeing requires improvement. The condition of parts of the environment does not
 consistently provide a safe, comfortable and dignified setting, and this has the potential to impact
 on people's quality of life and overall wellbeing. Despite these concerns, people benefit from
 positive and caring relationships with staff who know them well and understand their individual
 needs and preferences. Staff are committed to supporting people in a respectful and
 compassionate manner, helping to promote their wellbeing and maintain their independence
 wherever possible.

 Care and support is good. People benefit from the input of a committed and dedicated staff team
 who know them well and understand their individual needs, preferences and routines. Medication is
 managed safely and effectively. Staff provide appropriate support that enables people to achieve
 and maintain their personal wellbeing outcomes as far as possible. Personal plans are
comprehensive, person-centred and provide clear guidance for staff on how to meet people's
assessed needs.

The environment requires significant improvement. The premises are not maintained to a suitable
standard and, in their current condition, do not consistently support the delivery of safe, dignified,
person-centred care. We identified concerns relating to repair, maintenance and the overall upkeep
of the home, which present potential risks to people's health, safety and wellbeing.

Leadership and management require significant improvement. The Responsible Individual (RI) has
not established sufficiently robust governance and organisational arrangements to ensure the
service is delivered with appropriate care, competence and skill, in accordance with the Statement
of Purpose. Systems and processes are not effective in providing adequate oversight of the
management, quality, safety and overall effectiveness of the service.

source_index.name: Woffington House
source_index.summary:
Woffington Care Home is a service in Tredegar providing care for adults without nursing needs.
 Since our last inspection, the service has appointed a new service provider, responsible individual
 (RI) and manager. Although these changes are recent, we found significant improvements across
 the service. Two areas for improvement (AFI) identified at the previous inspection have been
 addressed and are no longer required. Both related to oversight by the RI, which has strengthened
 considerably. The AFI relating to medication management remains in place. Whilst medication
 systems have improved, further action is required to ensure medicines are managed consistently
 and safely.

 Many people experience positive outcomes because their well-being is promoted and they receive
 good quality care and support. People are encouraged to make choices, maintain relationships and
 take part in meaningful activities. The environment is comfortable, personalised and supports
 people's needs. Leaders have strengthened governance and oversight arrangements, which
 support the continued development of the service. Planned environmental improvements and
 ongoing work to enhance care planning demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement.
 We have rated all four inspection themes as ‘Good’.

source_index.name: Woodside & Elms
source_index.summary:
Wellbeing is excellent at Woodshed and Elms. Staff use innovative, person-centred approaches to
 improve independence and well-being. People achieve meaningful outcomes through community
 participation, hobbies, positive risk-taking and technology. They enjoy choice, cultural inclusion and
 social connections, while skilled staff provide safe, compassionate support that promotes dignity
 and safeguards individuals.

 Care and support is good. People receive safe, person-centred care supported by effective multi-
 agency working, positive risk management and robust healthcare arrangements. Staff know people
 well and promote independence, choice and wellbeing. Improving personalised care planning and
 co-produced outcomes will further strengthen responsive support.
The environment is good. Woodside and Elms comprising of two properties supporting eight people
in a safe, accessible, and homely environment. Spacious indoor and outdoor areas promote
independence, social interaction, meaningful activities and well-being. Ongoing maintenance and
improvements ensure peoples safety and quality of life.

Leadership and governance arrangements are good and effective, with robust oversight,
responsive quality assurance processes and a strong commitment to continuous improvement.
Leaders act promptly when concerns arise, support staff development, recognise achievement, and
ensure policies, training and practices promote high-quality, safe and person-centred care.

reports.title: November 2026 publication-month manager learning report
narrative: No latest archived report published in this month at this snapshot.
This empty fixed publication cohort supplies no inspection evidence, rating distribution or evidence-derived management priorities.
This snapshot-month cohort is captured as of 2026-11-01; it is not a completed-month account or a prediction of later publications.
limitations: This is a fixed all-data period cohort, not a dashboard-filter cohort. Only each service's latest archived report is included; this is not the complete historical inspection series or a trend in care quality. Early empty periods must not be interpreted as an absence of historical inspections: earlier reports are outside this latest-only archive.

Monthly membership uses reportPublishedActualDate, not the inspection visit or report issue date. Visit start/end, issue and publication are distinct. Empty months mean no latest archived report was published in that month, not that CIW did no inspections.

Ratings are the exact four published directory-snapshot theme values. Their effective dates are not independently auditable and cannot be assumed to match the historical publication month. Missing ratings and missing reports are not evidence of poor care. No overall quality score is calculated.

Positive wording and Improvement wording are automated search labels, not independent CIW findings. Topic counts mean reports mentioning a topic, not failures; topics and evidence sets overlap and must not be added together.

Published action-table rows can be historical or Achieved. New and Reviewed describe status words published in the source, not validation today. Missing status means unknown, not unresolved. Category counts are not counts of current failures or confirmed enforcement notices.

Excerpts and official summaries retain extracted wording and PDF page provenance. Layout changes and damaged characters can occur; the archived PDF is authoritative. Representative examples are not an exhaustive account or a prevalence estimate.
Public latest-report URLs can change after this snapshot. Use the linked local archived PDF to verify the captured evidence; the external source link establishes its CIW origin.

Management controls and the illustrative learning workflow are assistant-suggested local learning prompts, not CIW requirements, legal advice, clinical advice or an accreditation assessment. Validate applicability with appropriate local leads.

CareLens Cymru is independent and not an official CIW product.
